Ideas retained from the supplied conversation and discussion

Purpose. The unrestricted odd-prime unary-PHP goal still needs a uniform way to handle complete selector blocks and their mixed coefficient moments. The private external conversation suggests topology, especially an obstruction complex modeled on the successful chessboard argument. These are proposals and literature leads, not imported theorems about the augmented source. The user explicitly requested recording all of them before pursuing the complex idea. Spin remains paused outside this single assigned cycle.

  1. The existing chessboard template. On a prescribed row set, compatible lower matching moments prescribe an augmented boundary; extending to the next row degree requires a filling. The recorded marginal-cycle interface and all-field matching argument explain why this topology is relevant. The range \(N\ge2s-1\) is a sufficient filling range used by that proof, not a claim that every feature of the exact PC threshold is classified topologically.
  2. An obstruction complex for complete extensions. Seek a chain complex, or a system of vector spaces over the matching faces, whose obstruction class measures failure to extend compatible low-degree moments after adding the actual companions and coefficient fields. It should reduce to the known chessboard mechanism when the blocks are absent. The sought gain is a structural filling theorem across many blocks, replacing or complementing weighted substitution. Merely writing a constraint matrix as a two-term complex is not such a gain.
  3. Cohomological local-to-global consistency. Organize local moment spaces and restriction maps as a presheaf or coefficient system, with compatibility on overlaps. Ó Conghaile's cohomological consistency work is a concrete lead involving presheaves, Čech obstructions and equations over finite rings. Chan–Ng's later hierarchy lower bounds offer failure controls as well as techniques. Their results do not automatically translate to bounded PC or to our source grammar. Our recorded common-root control already shows that many local extensions of the same old marginal need not yield a globally compatible family.
  4. Tseitin as a homological comparison. For an oriented incidence system over a field, solvability of prescribed charges is an image-of-boundary question; componentwise total charge is the zeroth-homology obstruction. This helps explain the accessibility of directly presented linear systems to matching-characteristic algebraic reasoning. It is a heuristic comparison, not a theorem that every CNF encoding of a homological inconsistency is easy for every linear proof system; encoding, degree and field must be specified.
  5. Hyperplane-arrangement complements. The full-field false sets are affine arrangement complements; complex arrangement topology and finite-field point counts suggest cohomological invariants. Lifting an arrangement with the same combinatorics and passing to its intersection with the Boolean cube are separate issues. No bridge from those invariants to our filtered image and original-generator certificate budgets is established. The earlier geometry audit retains the relevant limitations.
  6. Integral torsion and characteristic. Shareshian–Wachs provides a genuine lead on \(3\)-torsion in bottom homology of matching and chessboard complexes. Such torsion could matter near or outside vanishing ranges and when changing coefficient fields. It does not, by itself, explain the odd-prime extension obstruction or alter the all-field filling range already used. Threshold behavior is an optional later investigation, not the main task here.
  7. Fundamental groups and nonabelian topology. These are lower-priority candidates because our immediate unknowns and compatibility constraints are linear over a field. This is a task-specific assessment, not a general impossibility of using nonabelian invariants in proof complexity. Homology with an appropriate coefficient system is the first object to try.

Tests for the chosen idea. Keep every original companion, coefficient field and mixed-block moment; preserve the actual degree ceiling. Distinguish a normalized NS functional from a PC annihilator that also respects reuse after degree drops. Recover the unaugmented matching picture, detect the existing local-to-global control, and avoid demanding pointwise coefficient selections that the historical packing barriers already rule out. At the end, assess whether a structural filling mechanism—not just a relabeling of the equations—has emerged and warrants another bounded cycle.

Exploration: use the existing matching complex, but change the differential

The claim search found an important predecessor: the main notebook already has a projective-family lifting lemma for commuting square-zero operators in characteristic two, and a wide-row matching application. Its later relative refinements remain characteristic two and require supplied compatible data. We therefore do not introduce a new abstract complex merely by renaming the moment matrix. The present construction extends one part of that mechanism to characteristic \(p\), while leaving the complete-source interface explicit.

Let \(A_0\) be the homogeneous functional matching algebra on \(m\) rows and \(N\) labels, with original row equations \(\sum_jX_{ij}-z\), Boolean homogenizations, and row/column collisions. It need not be an unsatisfiable board for the following construction. Put \[ G=A_0/(z) =k[X]/(X_{ij}^2,\ X_{ij}X_{ij'},\ X_{ij}X_{i'j},\ \sum_jX_{ij}),\qquad K_s=G_s^*. \] The space \(K_s\) is the top moment-correction space: it is the kernel of the restriction \(A_{0,s}^*\to A_{0,s-1}^*\) dual to multiplication by \(z\). In row multidegree \(S\), its elements are injection arrays with zero marginal when any row is deleted. With the usual row orientation, these are top cycles of the fixed-row chessboard complex. Thus the underlying matching spaces are the ones already supplied by the chessboard argument; no new geometric model of the old PHP base is assumed.

For a homogeneous linear form \(\ell\), let \(D_\ell:K_s\to K_{s-1}\) be dual to multiplication by \(\ell:G_{s-1}\to G_s\). These operators commute. In characteristic \(p\), \[ \ell^p=\sum_{ij}a_{ij}^{\,p}X_{ij}^{\,p}=0,\qquad D_\ell^p=0. \] This remains true after any field extension. But \(D_\ell^2\) need not vanish for odd \(p\): two independent square-zero coordinates already give \((x+y)^2=2xy\). The unsigned contraction produced by polynomial multiplication cannot simply be identified with an oriented simplicial boundary in odd characteristic.

Instead use the \(p\)-complex and its alternating ordinary complex \[ \cdots\longrightarrow K_{d+p} \xrightarrow{D_\ell}K_{d+p-1} \xrightarrow{D_\ell^{p-1}}K_d \xrightarrow{D_\ell}K_{d-1}\longrightarrow\cdots . \] Consecutive compositions vanish because \(D_\ell^p=0\). The first obstruction group is \[ H^{(1)}_d(\ell)= \ker(D_\ell:K_d\to K_{d-1})/ \operatorname{im}(D_\ell^{p-1}:K_{d+p-1}\to K_d); \] the adjacent group replaces the kernel by \(\ker D_\ell^{p-1}\) at \(K_{d+p-1}\) and the image by \(D_\ell K_{d+p}\). These are standard kinds of amplitude homology for a \(p\)-nilpotent operator; Qi's hopfological-algebra work is a literature lead, not an imported exactness theorem for our spaces.

This choice is tied to the actual odd-prime source: the leading operator for a selector \(q=1-L^{p-1}\), whose linear part is \(\ell\), is \(-D_\ell^{p-1}\). Thus the complex is sensitive to the degree and shape of the selector. It is a candidate layer of an augmented obstruction complex on chessboard moment corrections; it is not yet a complex proved equivalent to full augmented PC feasibility.

Working lemma: two-parameter common lifting in characteristic \(p\)

Let \(C_s\) be finite-dimensional graded spaces over a field \(k\) of characteristic \(p\), with commuting degree-minus-one operators \(D_1,D_2\) satisfying \(D_1^p=D_2^p=0\). Put \(\delta=p-1\). Suppose that for every nonzero pair \((u,v)\) over an algebraic closure, the operator \(\Theta=uD_1+vD_2\) satisfies \[ \ker(\Theta:C_d\to C_{d-1}) =\operatorname{im}(\Theta^\delta:C_{d+\delta}\to C_d), \] \[ \ker(\Theta^\delta:C_{d+\delta}\to C_d) =\operatorname{im}(\Theta:C_{d+p}\to C_{d+\delta}). \tag{TP-exact} \] Then every tuple \(z_0,\ldots,z_\delta\in C_d\) satisfying \[ D_1z_0=0,\quad D_1z_j+D_2z_{j-1}=0\ (1\le j\le\delta), \quad D_2z_\delta=0 \tag{TP-closed} \] has one \(w\in C_{d+\delta}\) with \[ \binom{\delta}{j}D_1^{\delta-j}D_2^jw=z_j\quad(0\le j\le\delta). \tag{TP-lift} \] Conversely every such image satisfies (TP-closed), without the exactness hypothesis. A linear right inverse on the compatible tuple space exists under (TP-exact).

Proof. Commutation and characteristic \(p\) give \(\Theta^p=0\). Work over the algebraic closure on \(\mathbf P^1\). Use the bundle complex \[ E_2=C_{d+p}\otimes\mathcal O(-1) \xrightarrow{\Theta} E_1=C_{d+\delta}\otimes\mathcal O \xrightarrow{\Theta^\delta} E_0=C_d\otimes\mathcal O(\delta) \xrightarrow{\Theta} E_{-1}=C_{d-1}\otimes\mathcal O(p). \] Hypothesis (TP-exact) gives exactness on every fiber at \(E_0,E_1\). The two adjacent ranks at each exact position sum to a constant dimension and each is at most its generic rank, so those ranks are constant. Hence the kernel sheaves and images give exact sequences \(0\to Z_1\to E_1\to Z_0\to0\) and \(0\to Z_2\to E_2\to Z_1\to0\), where \(Z_j\) is the kernel of the outgoing map.

On \(\mathbf P^1\), \(H^1(\mathcal O(-1))=0\), and \(H^2\) of a coherent sheaf vanishes. These are the standard two-chart calculation and cohomological dimension used in the predecessor; see Stacks Project, cohomology of projective space. The second exact sequence gives \(H^1(Z_1)=0\), so the first gives surjectivity \(H^0(E_1)\to H^0(Z_0)\). The polynomial section \(z(u,v)=\sum_{j=0}^{\delta}u^{\delta-j}v^jz_j\) lies in \(H^0(Z_0)\) exactly when (TP-closed) holds. Its preimage is a constant \(w\), since \(E_1\) has twist zero. Comparing coefficients in \(\Theta^\delta w=z(u,v)\) proves (TP-lift). Solvability descends to \(k\) because the ranks of a finite linear system and its augmented matrix do not change under field extension. Choosing a basis of the image gives the right inverse. Necessity follows by multiplying by \(\Theta\). This proves the lemma.

For \(p=2\) this recovers the two-operator instance of the existing projective lemma. For \(p=3\), the target is a triple and the lift is \((D_1^2w,\,2D_1D_2w,\,D_2^2w)\). The middle component is required data, not something that can be dropped when only the two endpoint selectors are written. The output adds \(p-1\) old degrees; the sufficient fiber test also needs the next old degree \(d+p\). No polynomial-block-inventory bound is obtained from this two-parameter statement.

A direct arbitrary-family port of the binary projective proof is not automatic. The alternating twists begin \(0,-1,-p,-p-1,\ldots\). Already on \(\mathbf P^2\) in characteristic three, \(\mathcal O(-3)\) has nonzero second cohomology, so the old negative-twist vanishing argument cannot simply be reused unchanged. This flags a proof obligation, not a counterexample to every possible many-operator lifting theorem.

Exact positive and negative controls

Abstract positive model. Take \(C\) to be the graded dual of \(k[t_1,t_2]/(t_1^p,t_2^p)\), with \(D_i\) dual to multiplication by \(t_i\). Every nonzero linear combination remains a truncated coordinate after a homogeneous invertible linear change, even over the algebraic closure. The module is free over that one-variable truncated algebra, so its length-\(p\) strings make both alternating maps exact in every degree. Exact modular checks at \(p=3,5\), \(d=0,1,2\), find equality of the full compatible target space and the joint image. The respective ranks are \(3,2,1\) and \(5,4,3\).

Individual exactness is insufficient. On the dual of \(k[t_1,t_2]/(t_1^p,t_2^2)\), take \(D_1\) dual to \(t_1\) and \(D_2\) dual to \(t_1+t_2\). For odd \(p\), each listed operator individually has only length-\(p\) strings: the algebra is free of rank two over either corresponding truncated coordinate algebra. But \(D_2-D_1\) comes from \(t_2\), whose strings have length two. At \(d=0\), all \(p\) scalar target coefficients satisfy (TP-closed), whereas the source degree \(p-1\) has dimension two and its image has rank two. Thus compatible tuples need not have a common lift if the whole pencil is not tested. The checker saves an explicit coordinate target outside the image at \(p=3,5\). This is a counterexample to the weakened hypothesis, not to the lemma.

What is still missing from an augmented obstruction complex

For an accuracy-one complete block \(P=1-\sum_jr_jq_j\), a degree-\(D\) NS functional must satisfy, for every legal original cofactor, \[ \Lambda(r^\alpha m q_i) -\sum_j\Lambda(r^{\alpha+e_j}m q_iq_j)=0,\qquad |\alpha|+\deg m\le D-e_i, \] where \(e_i\) is the original degree of \(q_iP\). The exponent support \(\alpha\) ranges across all blocks. Fresh exponents reduce by \(r^p=r\), with the degree of the unreduced original cofactor still paid. Higher accuracies expand the actual product and retain all its terms. The existing binary density coordinates make this coupling explicit, and the prime-field pairing supplies a possible coordinate interface with its larger density-degree cost.

The new complex captures a leading old-variable contraction layer of these equations. It does not supply their lower-degree terms, choose the intermediate polarized targets, or guarantee compatibility between different blocks. The common-root ordering control still refutes inferring global compatibility from separately available local extensions. Even a full normalized NS functional would not finish the PC task: the marked fixed-degree closure records the additional reuse after degree drops. Those conditions have not been identified with a vanishing theorem for this candidate complex.

The cohomological-consistency literature remains relevant, but the interface is not automatic. Ó Conghaile's construction uses compatible integral linear combinations of local sections and detects a particular obstruction to extending a local section (Appendix C); our unknowns are field-valued moments under a degree ceiling, not necessarily distributions on bounded-support satisfying assignments. Wide linear forms can mention the whole board at degree one. A support-size cover can therefore lose the polynomial-degree problem unless a translation is proved. The newer hierarchy lower bounds were screened at abstract level only; no theorem from them is used in the working lemma.

Assessment: one focused follow-up is deserved, a long commitment is not yet justified

What changed. There is now a natural odd-prime complex on the existing chessboard correction spaces, and a proved conditional two-parameter filling statement using projective cohomology. Exact controls show both a real matching-space obstruction and a nearby case where the proposed fiber obstruction vanishes. This goes beyond turning a linear system into a two-term complex. It also pinpoints the characteristic-two shortcut that cannot be copied: square-zero contraction becomes \(p\)-nilpotent contraction.

What did not change. The missing unrestricted implication—simultaneous complete-source removal with an affordable PC degree budget—remains open. The lowest-degree matching test is a preliminary control, not evidence that all mixed moments will extend. This is a working proof and route experiment, with no Lean verification or independent novelty claim.

Recommended next bounded cycle, if authorized. Prove or refute a quantitative amplitude-exactness bound for \(D_\ell,D_\ell^{p-1}\) on matching correction spaces at \(d\ge1\), uniformly over the algebraic closure, using collective row support and robust row-value evaluation hypotheses. Compare it with the existing coded-trade proof before inventing a new mechanism. If the fiber condition is unnecessarily strong, test a directly costed joint-lift criterion instead. A useful outcome must give a general range or a structural counterexample, not just more small ranks. Statement

Work over any field \(k\) of prime characteristic \(p\). On a functional matching board with arbitrary finite row set and label set \(\Omega\), let \(K_r\) be the top moment-correction space: the direct sum over \(r\)-row sets of injection arrays with every ordinary row marginal zero, with \(K_0=k\). For each row \(i\) in an active set \(I\), give a row function \(f_i:\Omega\to k\). Its weighted marginal is \(\delta_i\); put \(D_I=\sum_{i\in I}\delta_i\). These maps commute, \(\delta_i^2=0\), and \(D_I^p=0\).

Fix \(d\ge0\) and \(1\le a\le p-1\), and put \(b=p-a\). Suppose \[ |I|\ge 2d+b,\qquad Q=3d+2b, \tag{PA-room} \] and the evaluation matrix with rows \(1,f_i\) retains rank two after deletion of any at most \(Q\) labels, for every \(i\in I\). Then \[ \ker(D_I^a:K_d\to K_{d-a}) =\operatorname{im}(D_I^b:K_{d+b}\to K_d). \tag{PA-exact} \] Spaces of negative degree are zero. The lift can be chosen linearly. The theorem also holds with forced coded rows as below. It is a working extension of the characteristic-two forced-row proof; when \(p=2\), the predecessor's sharper row threshold \(t>d\) remains available.

Controlled insertion of one coded row

Fix a set \(F\) of forced rows, disjoint from an active set \(J\). Let \(V_r^F\) consist of arrays on row sets containing \(F\), with zero ordinary marginals and also zero \(f_i\)-weighted marginal for each \(i\in F\). All active contractions preserve these constraints. We prove the stronger version of (PA-exact) on \(V_d^F\), under \[ |J|\ge2(d-|F|)+b, \] with the same deletion allowance \(Q=3d+2b\) for all rows in \(F\cup J\).

Choose \(i\in J\). Let \(W_r\) denote the part of \(V_r^F\) avoiding \(i\), and \(U_r\) its part using \(i\). The map \(\delta_i:U_{r+1}\to W_r\) is onto whenever the needed deletion allowance is available. Indeed, the coded-disjoint-trade theorem expands every fixed-row component of a target into tensors whose forced rows have evaluation rank two and all other rows have rank one. Each tensor uses at most \(2r+|F|\) labels, and that theorem needs robustness through \(2r+|F|-1\) deletions. Outside those labels, choose a row-\(i\) vector \(c\) with ordinary sum zero and \(f_i\)-weighted sum one, supported on at most two labels. Its tensor product with the target tensor gives the insertion. The kernel of \(\delta_i\) is exactly the additional forced-row condition. No claim that this insertion commutes with the other contractions is needed.

Put \(A=D_{J\setminus\{i\}}\) and \(\delta=\delta_i\), so \(D_J=A+\delta\). Since \(A\delta=\delta A\) and \(\delta^2=0\), for every \(q\ge1\), \[ (A+\delta)^q=A^q+qA^{q-1}\delta. \tag{PA-binomial} \] Both terms have their literal integer coefficients reduced in \(k\).

Proof by induction on the number of active rows

Write \(e=d-|F|\). If \(e=0\), a target is supported on \(F\) alone. Expand it by coded trades, using at most \(3d\) labels per tensor. Choose \(b\) active rows and, successively outside the used labels, insert ordinary-zero, weighted-one factors. There are at most \(3d+2(b-1)\) forbidden labels at any insertion, within \(Q\). Divide the resulting tensor by \(b!\), which is invertible because \(b<p\). Its \(D_J^b\)-image is the target: precisely the \(b!\) orders deleting the inserted rows contribute. This proves the base case, including \(F=\varnothing,d=0\).

Now \(e>0\). Induct simultaneously for all amplitudes, using the strictly smaller active set \(J\setminus\{i\}\). Let \(z=w+u\in V_d^F\) be a \(D_J^a\)-cycle, with \(w\) avoiding \(i\) and \(u\) using it. The two row-support parts of \(D_J^az=0\) give \[ A^aw+aA^{a-1}\delta u=0,\qquad A^au=0. \] Applying \(A\) to the first equation yields \(A^{a+1}w=0\).

First correction: remove the part avoiding \(i\). If \(a<p-1\), induction at target degree \(d\) and amplitude \(a+1\) gives \(w=A^{b-1}h\), with \(h\in W_{d+b-1}\). The active threshold is \(|J|-1\ge2e+b-1\), exactly what that call needs. If \(a=p-1\), then \(b=1\) and simply set \(h=w\). Insert row \(i\) to choose \(v_1\in U_{d+b}\) with \(\delta v_1=h/b\). Formula (PA-binomial) shows that the part of \(D_J^bv_1\) avoiding \(i\) is \(w\). Therefore \(z'=z-D_J^bv_1\) uses row \(i\) only and remains a \(D_J^a\)-cycle. Its two cycle equations are \[ A^az'=0,\qquad A^{a-1}\delta z'=0, \] since \(a\ne0\) in \(k\).

Second correction: make row \(i\) forced. If \(a=1\), the second equation already says \(\delta z'=0\). If \(a>1\), put \(\eta=\delta z'\in W_{d-1}\). Induction at degree \(d-1\) and amplitude \(a-1\) gives \[ \eta=A^{b+1}h',\qquad h'\in W_{d+b}. \] Here the required active count is \(2(e-1)+(b+1)=2e+b-1\), again available. Insert \(i\) to choose \(u'\in U_{d+b+1}\) with \(\delta u'=h'\), and set \[ v_2=Au'-b h'\in V_{d+b}^F. \] Its first term uses \(i\); its second avoids \(i\). Consequently the avoiding part of \(D_J^bv_2\) is \(-bA^bh'+bA^{b-1}\delta Au'=0\), while \(\delta D_J^bv_2=A^{b+1}h'=\eta\). Thus \(z''=z'-D_J^bv_2\) uses row \(i\), has \(\delta z''=0\), and remains a \(D_J^a\)-cycle. For \(a=1\), take \(v_2=0,z''=z'\).

We now have \(z''\in V_d^{F\cup\{i\}}\) and \(A^az''=0\). Induction with the new forced set gives \(v_3\in V_{d+b}^{F\cup\{i\}}\) with \(A^bv_3=z''\): it needs only \(|J|-1\ge2(e-1)+b\). Because \(\delta v_3=0\), this is also \(D_J^bv_3=z''\). Hence \(v_1+v_2+v_3\) is the required lift. The reverse inclusion in (PA-exact) follows from \(D_J^{a+b}=D_J^p=0\).

Uniform labels and degrees. Every recursive target degree \(d'\) is at most the starting \(d\), and \(d'+b'\le d+b\). Forced rows number at most \(d'\). The largest inserted target \(h'\) therefore requires at most \(2(d'+b')+|F'|\le3d+2b=Q\) labels for its coded tensor. All smaller induction calls have no larger robustness requirement: changing \((d,a)\) to \((d,a+1)\) lowers \(Q\) by two, and changing it to \((d-1,a-1)\) lowers \(Q\) by one. The constant-only evaluation rows retain rank because the active rank-two hypothesis implies \(|\Omega|>Q\). Thus every coded-trade use and insertion is licensed. The output has degree \(d+b\); the construction can use auxiliary arrays through \(d+b+1\), which are contracted before forming the output. There is no iteration-dependent output degree or factor depending on the number of active rows. Fixed bases and insertion right inverses make the construction linear.

For two row-linear forms \(\ell_1,\ell_2\), suppose every nonzero algebraic-closure combination has at least \[ t\ge2d+2p-1 \] active rows and its active constant/predicate evaluation pairs remain rank two after any \[ Q_*=3d+3p-1 \] label deletions. Uniform assembly audit: the complex is a local tool, not yet a complete-source mechanism

21 September 2026 · Evidence-based route review · No uniform complete-source construction obtained; fixed-degree enumeration withdrawn. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Missing implication and stopping point. The odd-prime goal needs exclusion of arbitrary polynomial inventories of complete accuracy-one selector blocks at compiler ceiling \(D=4p-1\). The proposed topological route would have to turn its local matching corrections into one normalized annihilator of the full degree-\(D\) PC space, or another valid complete-source removal. The user's cases-and-examples challenge prompted the preceding review to withdraw a degree-six follow-up. This cycle tests an existing uniform mechanism instead: can simultaneous reweighting exploit the proved complex fillings while avoiding accumulated block cost? Stop when its invariant and degree ledger either connect to the available theorem or expose an unsupported step.

What the topology actually proves

The amplitude theorem is uniform in odd prime and target degree: for \(1\le a<p\), \(\ker D^a=\operatorname{im}D^{p-a}\) on the stated matching layer, assuming its row-width and label-robustness bounds. The ternary endpoint theorem handles a collectively wide pair at every target degree. These are general working proofs. The earlier checks at particular small degrees were controls on those arguments, not their asserted scope.

These results do not provide corrections in the simultaneous kernels of every already imposed global selector and fresh-coefficient constraint. The coded-row induction permits its specified local row conditions; an arbitrary augmented ENS source is not such a condition. Reapplying the theorem on the bare old matching space after adding global constraints silently discards the invariant the next filling would have to preserve. The three-selector construction proves that the stronger proposal to extend every partial design satisfying currently active equations is false, even with pairwise collective width. It leaves existence of a suitably chosen full design open.

The existing whole-level repair genuinely assembles, but its proved cost does not fit

The historical whole-level exact repair lemma already handles arbitrary many same-level blocks. It maintains a weight \(W\) of nonzero old functional value. Whenever it repairs a block, it multiplies \(W\) by a cofactor and a nonzero-value indicator and chooses constant fresh coefficients. A repaired block then has an actual field-ideal vanishing identity. Later multiplications preserve that identity; uncommitted zero specializations are tested against the final weight. Thus the proof contains the simultaneous compatibility invariant rather than assuming it.

Its sufficient old NS budget is \[ B=D+\sum_a c_a(D),\qquad c_a(D)=\max\bigl(\{0\}\cup\{D-e_{ai}+(p-1)\delta_{ai}:e_{ai}\le D\}\bigr). \] For nonconstant literal selectors \(g_{ai}=1-L_{ai}^{p-1}\), accuracy one gives \(\delta_{ai}=p-1\) and \(e_{ai}=2p-1\). At \(D=4p-1\), the displayed general lemma gives \(c_a(D)=p^2+1\). Hence its stated bound is \(D+(p^2+1)M\) for \(M\) such blocks. Selector-specific identities may reduce this constant, and the actual proof charges only repaired blocks; neither observation supplies a bound on their number for arbitrary tuples. For the polynomial inventories needed to rule out every proof-size exponent, the stated bound need not fit the linear old PHP degree budget. This is a failure of the available guarantee, not a lower bound on the cost of all possible repairs.

Replacing a repair weight by an arbitrary low-degree moment correction from the complex does not preserve the field-ideal vanishing identities used by that proof. No theorem obtained here makes that replacement legitimate. Moreover the historical repair lemma constructs an NS design. A new full-source PC conclusion needs its own closure or replay argument; old matching PC=NS cannot simply be transferred to the augmented system.

Existing alternatives do not fill that step automatically

The common-feature conditioning lemma uses one shared weight and costs \((p-1)\sum_\nu\deg f_\nu\). This avoids a cost per block when a small common feature description is actually supplied. It does not show that arbitrary selector families have one. The branch's probe-plus-sparse-support construction instead gives simultaneous coefficient substitutions, with a maximum local degree cost and a full PC replay. That is a proved complete-source endpoint under its explicit profile hypothesis, not a consequence of complex exactness.

The single-parent survival criterion correctly chooses a new retained functional and therefore avoids demanding extension of arbitrary old choices. Its proof explicitly leaves persistence of the input-window premise and affordable simultaneous choices for many parents open. It cannot be iterated by citing the one-predicate complex theorem on the unchanged old base.

The earlier source-module nonextension control already distinguishes failure of one chosen design from failure of existence. The ordering-source control separately shows that growing local families can share an old marginal and still fail to assemble. That control is not PHP and does not prove the present route impossible; it means a general gluing claim must use an additional PHP-specific property and prove coherent compatibility, not just individual solvability.

Decision and contribution to the goal

No uniform assembly mechanism was obtained. The amplitude and pair theorems remain useful local tools, but this audit does not advance the required implication for arbitrary complete selector families. Automatic extension is obstructed; existence of an appropriately chosen PC annihilator is unresolved. There is no evidence here that a sequence of higher fixed-degree calculations will bridge that gap. Topology is therefore deprioritized as the immediate route to the lower bound, without retracting its proved local statements or claiming an impossibility theorem about all topological approaches.

A degree-budgeted augmented complex avoids charging once per block

21 September 2026 · Working graded-complex construction and uniform degree bound · No homology-vanishing theorem or new unrestricted lower bound. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Assignment and change of direction. This cycle began by reading the existing multiscale rank/profile and probe-removal controls; no new restriction theorem was obtained. The user then asked whether a better complex could account for added blocks without the sequential costs. This is a valid distinction. The preceding audit rules out treating the available local fillings as an already proved assembly theorem, but does not justify deprioritizing constructions of a different augmented object on the basis of the sequential repair cost alone. The present task is to construct that object, preserve original degrees and PC semantics, and determine whether its degree bookkeeping intrinsically charges the total number of blocks. Stop at a precise construction and scope assessment; do not infer exactness just from having a complex.

Setup and working proposition

Fix a prime \(p\), put \(\delta=p-1\) and \(e=2p-1\), and use a finite complete accuracy-one selector family. Scalar zero/unit input cases can be removed by the existing direct maps. Every remaining nonconstant literal selector has original degree \(\delta\), and every original companion has degree \(e\). Let \(A_0\) be the old homogeneous PHP presentation algebra, keeping the homogenizing variable \(z\) and the original generators, as in the marked-algebra construction. Nothing is saturated. For each block \(a\), define \[ B_a=A_0[r_{ai}]_i/(r_{ai}^p-z^\delta r_{ai})_i,\qquad q_{ai}^{\rm h}=z^\delta-(L_{ai}^{\rm h})^\delta, \] \[ H_a=z^p-\sum_i r_{ai}q_{ai}^{\rm h},\qquad K_a=(q_{ai}^{\rm h}H_a)_i\subseteq B_a,\qquad A_a=B_a/K_a. \] Every variable has internal degree one, so \(H_a\) has degree \(p\), and the companion degree is exactly \(e\). Let \(B=\bigotimes_{A_0,a}B_a\), the old algebra with all fresh fields and no companions.

Proposition. Choose a minimal homogeneous free resolution \(F_{a,\bullet}\to A_a\) over \(B_a\), with \(F_{a,0}=B_a\). Extend it to \(B\), and form the total tensor complex \[ \mathcal T_\bullet=\bigotimes_{B,a}\bigl(B\otimes_{B_a}F_{a,\bullet}\bigr). \] Its zeroth homology is the complete original homogeneous source algebra \[ H_0(\mathcal T)=B/\sum_a K_aB. \] A summand of homological degree \(h\) that uses positive resolution degrees from \(j\) distinct blocks has every basis shift at least \[ je+h-j. \tag{DB-shift} \] Consequently its internal-degree-\(D\) piece vanishes unless \(je+h-j\le D\). At the compiler ceiling \(D=4p-1\), at most two distinct blocks can have positive resolution degree in a term. Terms with two such blocks occur only at total homological degrees two or three; terms with one can occur only through homological degree \(2p+1\). These bounds are independent of the total block inventory.

Construction and proof, including the original costs

The algebra \(B_a\) is connected and nonnegatively graded, with degree-zero field \(\mathbb F_p\). Its companion ideal is generated in degree \(e\). If this ideal is zero, use just \(F_{a,0}\). Otherwise choose a basis of \((K_a)_e\) from the supplied companions. Constant linear dependencies are removed without changing their common original cost; that basis generates \(K_a\) as an ideal. Thus \(F_{a,1}\) has all basis shifts \(e\).

For each later kernel, choose minimal homogeneous generators and map the free module on them onto the kernel. This recursively constructs a minimal resolution: the kernel of each minimal free cover is contained in the positive-degree maximal ideal times its domain. To see this, a relation with a nonzero constant coefficient would give a dependence between the chosen generator classes modulo the maximal ideal, contrary to their being a basis. Therefore every matrix entry in a later differential has positive degree. Induction gives a minimum shift \(e+i-1\) in \(F_{a,i}\) for \(i\ge1\). This is a degree bound, not an assertion that the resolution is short or easy to compute. The rings are Noetherian, so the modules in each homological degree can be taken finite.

Monic division in the fresh field equations gives \(B\) a free \(B_a\)-basis of monomials in the other blocks' coefficients, with exponents below \(p\). Hence extending \(F_a\) to \(B\) preserves exactness. The tensor differential is the signed sum of the factor differentials, with sign \((-1)^{i_1+\cdots+i_{a-1}}\) in position \(a\); thus its square is zero over odd characteristic as well. Its degree-zero term is \(B\), and the image into that term is exactly \(\sum_aK_aB\). This proves the assertion about \(H_0\), without assuming that the higher tensor homology vanishes.

If a tensor summand has positive degrees \(i_1,\ldots,i_j\), summing the minimum shifts gives \[ \sum_{\nu=1}^j(e+i_\nu-1)=je+h-j. \] The remaining coefficients lie in a nonnegatively graded ring and cannot lower this degree. Since \(h\ge j\), nonzero internal-degree-\(D\) terms require \(je\le D\). At \(D=4p-1\), \(3e=6p-3>D\), so \(j\le2\). When \(j=2\), the sharper inequality gives \(h\le D-2e+2=3\). When \(j=1\), it gives \(h\le D-e+1=2p+1\). This proves the uniform bound. For heterogeneous blocks the same argument uses \(\sum_{\nu=1}^j e_{a_\nu}+h-j\); no uniform-cost simplification should be made when actual original degrees differ.

Why a raw Koszul complex is not enough

One could start with a free generator \(\varepsilon_i\) of degree \(e\) for each companion and differential \(d\varepsilon_i=q_i^{\rm h}H_a\). But simply wedging these generators does not generally resolve \(A_a\). There are already common-factor syzygies \[ q_j^{\rm h}\varepsilon_i-q_i^{\rm h}\varepsilon_j \] of internal degree \(e+\delta=3p-2\), whereas a wedge of two companion generators has degree \(2e=4p-2\). In addition, the old Boolean equations imply \[ (L_i^{\rm h})^p=z^\delta L_i^{\rm h},\qquad (q_i^{\rm h})^2=z^\delta q_i^{\rm h} \] inside \(A_0\). Frobenius proves the first identity from \(X^p=z^\delta X\); expanding the square gives the second. Thus \((q_i^{\rm h}-z^\delta)\varepsilon_i\) is another first syzygy at cost \(e+\delta\). These formulas describe relations in the raw presentation; they need not be independent or form a generating list after minimal generators are chosen.

The full \(F_a\) retains all syzygies, including any arising from the old presentation and the coefficient fields. Using a resolution rather than declaring the naive Koszul complex exact is essential. Higher positive homology of \(\mathcal T\) then records interactions of the complete factors, rather than omitted within-block relations. This is the chain-level version of the earlier tensor-factor geometric object; the new contribution is the explicit internal-degree bound, not a novelty claim for derived tensor products.

The uniform term bound is not a pairwise-gluing theorem

Although a term has at most two positive-resolution factors at the compiler ceiling, its coefficient belongs to \(B\), which includes every block's fresh variables. A cycle is a sum of terms and may use arbitrarily many block indices across that sum. Degree-zero factors and coefficient monomials are not absent constraints. The result therefore does not imply that checking every two-block subsystem suffices, that a contradiction has a bounded-block witness, or that the tensor factors are flat.

In particular, the three-selector obstruction can live entirely within one \(F_a\), and is not excluded by the bound on distinct blocks. The generic ordering control still forbids inferring global compatibility from separate local solutions. The earlier nonflatness result also remains in force. We do not ask for vanishing of every higher Tor group: harmless fresh-variable phenomena can coexist with preservation of the old lower bound.

How this object retains the PC question

At internal degree \(D\), \(H_0(\mathcal T)_D=B_D/V_0\), where \(V_0=(\sum_aK_aB)_D\). Homogenizing a polynomial of degree at most \(D\) to degree \(D\) identifies this quotient with the quotient by original-generator NS consequences. In particular \(z^D\notin V_0\) is only an NS nonrefutation statement.

Retain the marked multiplication maps by \(z\), old variables and every fresh coefficient variable on the graded object. The exact PC closure construction, now written modulo the old and fresh-field presentation, is \[ V_{t+1}=V_t+\sum_{y\ne z} y\{u\in B_{D-1}:zu\in V_t\}. \tag{DB-PC} \] The old field-only ideal is homogeneous, so quotienting the original formula by it gives this formula exactly: changing a lift by an old relation changes its multiples by old relations. Thus a degree-\(D\) PC refutation exists precisely when the class of \(z^D\) belongs to the stabilized \(V_\infty\). No saturation by arbitrary powers of \(z\) is used.

The remaining target is to protect this marked old unit through (DB-PC), possibly using a filling or homological-transfer argument on \(\mathcal T\) together with the old chessboard contractions. The present construction does not prove that protection. In particular, fixed internal degree does not bound the number of PC closure iterations or rule out chains of cancellations across many blocks. Ordinary tensor homology or its unmarked dimensions alone are not a substitute for that step.

Assessment and next bounded test

The user's objection changes the assessment: the accumulated cost in sequential repair is not evidence that every augmented complex must pay that cost. Here is a uniform augmented object whose internal-degree terms have a bounded number of positive-resolution factors, regardless of the inventory. This removes that particular bookkeeping objection to studying a larger complex. It does not remove the actual missing lower-bound implication, and no new unrestricted source case is proved.

Further work on this specific construction is deserved. For odd-prime-clause-transfer, next identify the relative obstruction to preserving \(z^D\) under one step of (DB-PC), including the within-block syzygies above and the mixed two-factor terms. Determine whether an old chessboard filling can be lifted while respecting those maps with an inventory-independent degree bound. Stop at a proved sufficient preservation mechanism or an explicit failure of the proposed mechanism. Do not replace that test by more fixed-degree examples, assume arbitrary partial moments extend, demand full flatness, or claim that constructing the object establishes its required homology.

Focused review and process. Checked original companion shifts, freeness of the field-only base change, minimal-resolution shifts, tensor signs, zeroth homology and the exact fixed-ceiling PC operation. The claims are proved symbolically; no numerical sweep or independent novelty search was required. The initial restriction reading yielded no new result and the later user steering is recorded explicitly. The prior route assessment is preserved and qualified here rather than silently rewritten.

Filter the augmented complex, retaining multiplication as well as persistence

21 September 2026 · Working filtered-complex bridge and exact barcode control · No unit-preservation theorem; Spin paused after this cycle. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. Resume the goal by locating the obstruction to extending old chessboard fillings through the complete block complex. During the cycle the user proposed a filtration and persistent homology, then requested quick completion to conserve the weekly limit. Record the precise filtration, its relation to PC cancellation, and a falsifying test for whether ordinary persistence alone suffices. No further experiment or cycle is started. Initial commentary and resume part one preceded timing; the previous goal turn made progress by constructing and committing the degree-budgeted object.

A filtered complex and its degree-fall obstruction

Use the preceding notation: \(B\) is the old homogeneous PHP algebra with all fresh field equations, \(\mathcal T\) is the tensor complex of complete block resolutions, and \(A=H_0(\mathcal T)\) is the full original homogeneous source algebra. Assume multiplication by \(z\) on \(B\) is injective through degree \(D\). For functional PHP this holds in the recorded old stable-filtration range, and extends to \(B\) by its fresh-monomial free basis. It is not asserted outside that range.

At fixed internal degree \(D\), define an increasing filtration by subcomplexes \[ F_d\mathcal T_{*,D}=z^{D-d}\mathcal T_{*,d},\qquad 0\le d\le D. \] The maps are injective under the stated hypothesis, since each term is a direct sum of nonnegative shifts of \(B\). They commute with the differential. Thus \(H_i(F_d)\simeq H_i(\mathcal T)_d\), and the persistence maps are multiplication by \(z\). In degree zero the persistent module is \[ A_0\xrightarrow{z}A_1\xrightarrow{z}A_2\longrightarrow\cdots. \] The marked unit starts at degree zero; its image at \(d\) is \(z^d\). Its death is exactly the original-generator NS refutation degree. This gives a genuine bounded filtration, not merely a list of unrelated complexes.

Put \(\overline{\mathcal T}=\mathcal T/z\mathcal T\). There is a natural isomorphism \[ \frac{H_1(\overline{\mathcal T})_D} {\operatorname{im}(H_1(\mathcal T)_D\to H_1(\overline{\mathcal T})_D)} \ \simeq\ \ker(z:A_{D-1}\to A_D). \tag{FC-obstruction} \] Proof. Lift a cycle \(\bar v\) to \(v\in\mathcal T_{1,D}\). Its boundary has the form \(dv=zu\), uniquely in \(\mathcal T_{0,D}=B_D\). Send the class to \([u]\in A_{D-1}\). Changing the lift by \(zw\) changes \(u\) by \(dw\); changing a cycle by a boundary has the same harmless effect. Every class killed by \(z\) arises this way. If \([u]=0\), write \(u=dw\); then \(v-zw\) is a cycle upstairs, precisely the stated kernel. This proves the isomorphism directly.

Let \(V_0=(\sum_aK_aB)_D\subset B_D\), and let \(V_1\) be the space after one step of the fixed-ceiling PC closure. Then \(V_1/V_0\subset A_D\) is exactly the image of \[ \bigoplus_{y\ne z}\ker(z:A_{D-1}\to A_D)\longrightarrow A_D, \qquad (u_y)_y\longmapsto\sum_y yu_y. \] Indeed \(zu\in V_0\) is precisely the condition that the degree-\(D\) consequence has dropped actual degree and may be multiplied by a variable. Formula (FC-obstruction) therefore locates the first PC enlargement in the filtered complex. Subsequent closure steps must still be controlled; ordinary NS persistence does not already perform them.

The existing source control has a genuine persistent obstruction

In the ternary three-selector source, write \(T=a-b\), \(H=z^3-\sum_i r_iq_i^{\rm h}\), and \(u=TH\), of degree four. The exact identities are \[ \sum_iq_i^{\rm h}=T^2,\qquad T^3=z^2T,\qquad d\!\left(T\sum_i\varepsilon_i\right)=z^2u. \] The prior proof gives \(zu\ne0\) in \(A_5\), but \(z^2u=0\) in \(A_6\). Hence the reduced degree-six cycle has a nonzero obstruction under (FC-obstruction). A class born no later than degree four survives through five and dies at six. This reuses the previously proved control; it is not a new small-board experiment. It refutes vanishing of all obstruction groups throughout the window, not every possible theorem about the final ceiling. The block remains removable by known low-feature methods, so this homology is not itself evidence of a refutation.

Even identical marked persistence can have different PC degree

The following exact control tests the general hypothesis that the NS persistence module, including its marked unit, determines PC degree. Over \(\mathbb F_3\), with the same field equation \(x^3-x\), take \[ \mathcal F_+=\{x^2,\ x^2-x,\ x^3-1,\ x^3-x\}, \quad \mathcal F_-=\{x^2-1,\ x^2-x-1,\ x^3-1,\ x^3-x\}. \] All supplied degrees are respectively \(2,2,3,3\). Their original homogeneous presentation algebras are \[ A_+=k[x,z]/(x^2,xz,z^3),\qquad A_-=k[x,z]/(x^2-z^2,xz). \] For the second algebra, \(z^3=0\) follows by multiplying \(x^2-z^2\) by \(z\) and using \(xz=0\); also \(x^3=0\). Thus the two cubic supplied generators add no further relation. The first displayed presentation follows directly by subtracting the two quadratics and then reducing the cubic.

Both algebras have graded basis \(1,x,z,z^2\). As graded \(k[z]\)-modules, with the unit distinguished, both are \[ k[z]/(z^3)\ \oplus\ (k[z]/(z))(-1). \] Their full persistence barcodes are identical: \([0,3)\) and \([1,2)\), with the unit generating the first interval. Both have NS refutation degree three.

Nevertheless \(\deg_{\rm PC}(\mathcal F_+)=3\) and \(\deg_{\rm PC}(\mathcal F_-)=2\). For \(\mathcal F_+\), every axiom active at degree two is satisfied by \(x=0\), so no degree-two refutation exists; \(x\cdot x^2-(x^3-1)=1\) gives degree three. For \(\mathcal F_-\), subtract the quadratics to derive \(x\), multiply that completed line by \(x\), and subtract \(x^2-1\), all through degree two. The difference invisible to persistence is multiplication by \(x\): the \(z\)-torsion class \(x\) satisfies \(x\cdot x=0\) in \(A_+\), but \(x\cdot x=z^2\ne0\) in \(A_-\). These are field-domain algebraic controls, not PHP instances.

Thus even the complete zeroth persistence module with the unit marked does not determine PC degree. One must retain the variable-multiplication maps or equivalent chain-level data. The control does not refute a richer filtered complex with those maps, nor assert that every possible higher-homology invariant is insufficient.

Use the stronger existing elimination result as the baseline

The historical one-block PC elimination theorem and its proof were reread. It removes an arbitrary complete block at additive cost \((p-1)\delta\), using weighted specializations to derive its inputs and then reusing their completed lines in the zero-specialized proof. For selector degree \(\delta=p-1\), iterating gives \(D+(p-1)^2M\). This is a stronger PC baseline than the sequential NS repair budget inspected in the preceding assembly audit, although its uncontrolled inventory dependence remains. One-block unit preservation is therefore not a missing theorem to re-prove.

The ordering construction also retains its warning that generic old PC hardness and cheap local interactions do not supply global preservation. The filtered approach must use a specific PHP filling property. No such uniform multiplicative lifting has been proved in this cycle.

Sources, evidence and decision

The module viewpoint agrees with the abstract-level description in Skraba–Vejdemo-Johansson; no theorem beyond that terminology is imported here. Stacks, Section 12.24, supplies the standard filtered-complex and associated spectral-sequence framework. Its construction does not imply degeneration for our source. The older Zomorodian–Carlsson author PDF was inaccessible through the web tool; its full text was not needed for the elementary arguments above. All asserted identities and the barcode comparison are proved explicitly; no numerical experiment was performed.

Claude Code (Opus 5, high reasoning) completed the checkpoint under the same timing session at the user’s request. Before registering the claims, it independently rechecked the lift-and-divide proof of (FC-obstruction), including the use of \(z\)-injectivity on \(B\) and well-definedness under changes of lift and of cycle, the identification of \(V_1/V_0\), and both algebras of the \(\mathbb F_3\) control: their bases \(1,x,z,z^2\), their marked barcodes, and the PC degrees three and two. No fresh-context reviewer was run, because the user asked for prompt completion. The preparation time below includes about 1 h 35 min of idle waiting between the usage-limit stop and the resumed checkpoint; this cannot be separated retroactively.

Assessment. A filtration is more informative than a single leading-degree snapshot and exactly records delayed NS relations. The new obstruction map shows where PC uses those relations, while the same-barcode control proves that forgetting multiplication loses essential information. This sharpens the object and rules out an inadequate invariant; it does not establish the unrestricted lower bound or a new family-wide removal theorem.

Compare the resulting shared cost with \(D+(p-1)^2M\); success must improve the arbitrary-family bound, not merely reproduce one-block elimination or an equivalent description of PC closure. Route review: complexes add no PC invariant beyond two degrees of the source algebra

21 September 2026 · Route review with a working descent corollary · Complex/filtration line parked; next step moves to intermediate-rank dense blocks. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Opening and route check. The user asked for one research cycle. The preceding entry proposed a PHP-specific lift of chessboard contractions that respects the variable actions on the filtered block complex. That task advances the top-level item odd-prime-clause-transfer. The missing implication for the goal is unchanged: for polynomially many complete accuracy-one selector blocks, including dense high-rank blocks, the old unit survives fixed-ceiling PC closure through \(4p-1\), possibly after a restriction. The last three entries on this item (the assembly audit, the block complex and its filtration) audited, built and filtered one complex without moving that implication. Before attempting the lift, this cycle therefore tests whether the object can carry the information the lift would need. The chance that completing this line advances the goal was judged low at the outset: the complex had so far produced exact bookkeeping, not a mechanism. No numerical estimate is given, because there is no calibrated method.

The line's general claim. A derived or filtered complex over the complete source, with its multiplication maps, can certify preservation of the old unit through PC closure at a cost independent of the block inventory, using a PHP-specific filling property.

What the goal needs from it. The complex would have to supply, for dense blocks, what the existing endpoints do not. Sparse and probe-sparse blocks are already handled at polynomial inventory by the shared-support and mixed-profile endpoints: one common random matching restriction, with a union bound over the blocks, followed by per-block interpolation whose degree is set by the per-block cover or probe size. The cost is not additive in the number of blocks, but it depends on the inventory exponent, and the mixed-profile endpoint also needs supplied degree-preserving old certificates. The one-block elimination theorem pays \((p-1)^2\) per block. Over \(\mathbb F_3\), for complete old-quadratic blocks on the separated functional graph, the graph criterion handles blocks of low or dense projected rank and leaves intermediate projected ranks open. For \(p\ge5\) no dense-rank criterion is recorded.

Falsification attempt: fixed-ceiling PC closure descends to two degrees of \(H_0\)

Working corollary (a refinement of recorded results). The descent below is the one-line argument already used for the field-only quotient in (DB-PC) of the block-complex entry, applied to the full ideal \(J\). Its first step is the enlargement recorded in the filtered-complex entry. The new content is the sufficiency statement that closes the open remark of the same-barcode control. Let \(S\) be the polynomial ring in the variables \(y_1,\ldots,y_v\) and the homogenizing variable \(z\), let \(J\) be generated by the actual homogenizations of the supplied generators, and let \(A=S/J\). Fix \(D\ge1\). In \(A_D\) define \[ U_0=0,\qquad U_{t+1}=U_t+\sum_{i=1}^v y_i\,(U_t:_Az),\qquad (U:_Az)=\{a\in A_{D-1}: za\in U\}. \] Let \(\pi:S_D\to A_D\) be the quotient map and \(W_t\) the closure of the exact PC criterion. Then \(W_t=\pi^{-1}(U_t)\) for every \(t\). Consequently a PC refutation at ceiling \(D\) exists exactly when \(z\cdot[z^{D-1}]\in U_\infty\). No \(z\)-injectivity is assumed. This condition depends only on the finite-dimensional datum \[ \mathcal K_D(A)=\bigl(A_{D-1},\ A_D;\ z,y_1,\ldots,y_v:A_{D-1}\to A_D;\ [z^{D-1}]\bigr), \] a marked representation of the generalized Kronecker quiver with \(v+1\) arrows. Only the linear span of the maps \(y_i\) matters, because \(\sum_iy_i(V)\) is the image of \(V\) under that span. Two data are therefore equivalent when isomorphisms of \(A_{D-1}\) and \(A_D\) intertwine the \(z\)-maps, carry one span of \(y\)-maps onto the other and preserve the marked class; the number and labelling of variables are irrelevant. Dually, in the terminology of the historical duality lemma, a normalized ceiling-\(D\) PC annihilator exists exactly when there is a closed annihilator family: a subspace \(\Phi\subseteq A_D^*\) that satisfies \(y_i^*\Phi\subseteq z^*\Phi\) for every \(i\) and contains a functional \(\varphi\) with \(\varphi(z^D)\ne0\).

Proof. Induct on \(t\). For \(t=0\), \(W_0=J_D=\ker\pi\). Suppose \(W_t=\pi^{-1}(U_t)\), and let \(\pi':S_{D-1}\to A_{D-1}\) be the quotient map. Since \(\pi(zu)=z\pi'(u)\), \[ (W_t:z)=\{u\in S_{D-1}:zu\in W_t\}=\pi'^{-1}\bigl((U_t:_Az)\bigr). \] Also \(\pi(y_iu)=y_i\pi'(u)\), so \(\pi(W_{t+1})=U_{t+1}\). Finally \(W_{t+1}\supseteq W_t\supseteq\ker\pi\), hence \(W_{t+1}=\pi^{-1}(U_{t+1})\). The refutation criterion \(z^D\in W_\infty\) of the recorded proposition becomes \(\pi(z^D)\in U_\infty\).

For the dual form, put \(\Phi_\infty=U_\infty^\perp\). Write \(m_y:A_{D-1}\to A_D\) for multiplication by a variable. Then \((m_z^{-1}U)^\perp=m_z^*(U^\perp)\) in \(A_{D-1}^*\), and \(U\) is closed exactly when \(m_{y_i}(m_z^{-1}U)\subseteq U\), which holds exactly when \(m_{y_i}^*(U^\perp)\subseteq m_z^*(U^\perp)\). A subspace \(\Phi\) with the stated property has a closed annihilator containing \(U_0=0\), hence containing \(U_\infty\). So \(\varphi(z^D)\ne0\) for some \(\varphi\in\Phi\) forces \(z^D\notin U_\infty\). Conversely, \(\Phi_\infty\) itself qualifies whenever \(z^D\notin U_\infty\). This is linear algebra on finite-dimensional spaces. A single normalized annihilator need not itself satisfy the closure condition; the family \(\Phi_\infty\) does.

Consequence for the complex line. The block complex \(\mathcal T\) has \(H_0(\mathcal T)=A\) for the complete source. Two presentations, complexes or filtered complexes whose \(H_0\) have isomorphic marked data \(\mathcal K_D\) have the same ceiling-\(D\) PC refutability. Higher homology \(H_i(\mathcal T)\), \(i\ge1\), and the \(z\)-persistence module outside degrees \(D-1,D\) add no information about that refutability. Degrees below \(D-1\) enter only through \(J_{D-1}\) and \(J_D\). The data must still be iterated, up to \(\dim A_D\) closure steps, so this yields no cheap invariant. Higher homology can serve only to compute \(\mathcal K_D(A)\) and its closure steps: (FC-obstruction) computes \(\ker(z:A_{D-1}\to A_D)\), and every later step needs the relative version \((U_t:_Az)\) for a growing \(U_t\). This is a statement about invariants, not about methods. Chain-level data of \(\mathcal T\), such as block-local resolutions or filling maps, could still suggest a construction. But the lift proposed in the preceding entry must, whatever its construction, produce a closed annihilator family \(\Phi\) with \(y_i^*\Phi\subseteq z^*\Phi\) and \(\varphi(z^D)\ne0\). The complex supplies no such family and no property that forces one to exist. The same-barcode control is consistent with this: its two algebras have different \(\mathcal K_2\), since \(x\cdot x=0\) in one and \(x\cdot x=z^2\ne0\) in the other.

The degree-budgeted term bound does not change this. At most two blocks have positive resolution degree in a term, but \(A_{D-1}\) and \(A_D\) contain coefficient monomials from every block, and \(U_\infty\) is computed on all of them at once. The bound constrains the shape of \(\mathcal T\), not the size or coupling of \(\mathcal K_D(A)\). The three-selector obstruction already lies inside one block, where no bound on the number of interacting blocks applies.

The base in the filtration hypothesis

The filtration assumes \(z\) is injective on the field-only algebra \(B\) through \(D\), justified for the functional PHP base. The ordinary target compiles over the weak base \(\Gamma_{\rm w}\) (weak-base compiler). This is not a gap for the complex line. The injectivity is claimed on \(B\) only, in the recorded stable-filtration range, which contains the constant ceiling \(4p-1\) for large \(N\). The complete-board transfer already compiles ordinary unary PHP over the full functional linear-row base, and adding generators can only lower the PC degree, so a lower bound over the functional base with the compiled blocks implies one over \(\Gamma_{\rm w}\). The recorded restriction applies only to removal maps certified for the weak base alone: those must be applied before any strengthening.

Assessment of this line

The complex and filtration line produced correct bookkeeping: the H₀ identification, the inventory-independent term bound, and the first-step obstruction. It also produced a useful negative control. By the descent corollary, the complex adds no PC-relevant invariant beyond \(\mathcal K_D(A)\) and its closure, the object recorded in the socle criterion before the complex existed. The line is parked for three reasons: no PHP-specific construction of a closed family \(\Phi\) has been proposed, the line has not touched dense blocks where the goal's obligation lies, and the assembly audit found no uniform assembly mechanism. It should be reopened only with a concrete PHP-specific statement about \(\mathcal K_D(A)\), for example a design family \(\Phi\) built from matching designs and block data, whose cost can be compared with \(D+(p-1)^2M\) and with the interpolation endpoints.

Next step on the highest-risk item

This cycle first drafted a restriction dichotomy as the next step: one random matching restriction would put every dense-support ternary block into the low or dense range of the graph criterion. The reviewer showed that the record already defeats it. Take one tuple of \(\lceil100L\ln L\rceil\) random full-support forms for each dyadic scale \(L\le n\), which is only \(O(\log n)\) blocks. Under a matching restriction the surviving coefficients of a random form remain uniform, and matched cells only add constants, which change a selector \(1-F^2\) by affine terms. So at residual size \(L\) the scale-\(L\) tuple behaves like the two-size control's tuple on an \(L\)-hole board: projected rank above \(L\), hence above \(L^\sigma\operatorname{polylog}L\), and at most \(O(L\log L)\), below \(Q_*(L)\). Every residual size therefore leaves an intermediate block. I checked the restriction step. The conclusion also requires three routine steps that are not written out: rerunning the control's union bound at each scale; rounding, by using for residual size \(L\) the dyadic scale \(L'\le L<2L'\), whose rank lies above \(L'\ge L/2\) and at most \(O(L'\log L')\), still below \(Q_*(L)\); and averaging over the random coefficients with Markov's inequality, to pass from a fixed restriction to a fixed inventory under a random restriction. It is therefore recorded as a calibration argument, not a registered claim. The same restriction test was the next task of the assembly audit, and the following cycle obtained no restriction theorem; the notebook already stated that no general restriction dichotomy follows.

The next step is therefore the intermediate-rank endpoint itself, resuming the parked test of the exact-image entry and the geometry-survey route decision. For \(p=3\), bound the image of the actual separated space \(W_k\) modulo a degree-bounded span generated by the selectors and old graph relations, with explicit NS certificates for every reducer. The sum of image dimensions over all blocks must stay below \(\dim W_k\), and the weighted certificates must stay inside the graph's PC ceiling. Test the criterion first on the recorded common-factor, two-column and reserve-coordinate controls, and on the dyadic random inventory above. The exact-image barrier already excludes Boolean-only completion. For \(p\ge5\) a dense-rank criterion must be established before any intermediate-rank endpoint.

Verification gate. Re-read from the notebook: the exact PC criterion, the block complex with (DB-PC), the filtered complex, the same-barcode control, both compilers, the ternary graph criterion and the two-size control. Claim searches covered closure, socle, quotient, Kronecker, truncated closure, design and restriction dichotomy. A standing fresh-context reviewer found the descent correct over every field, reported that the record gives it in substance (hence the corollary label), and required three precisions, all adopted: invariance up to the span of the \(y\)-maps, no \(z\)-injectivity hypothesis, and the annihilator terminology. A second review of the full draft required: weakening the claim from "no remaining lever" to "no additional PC invariant"; correcting the endpoint costs and the prime scope of the graph criterion; and replacing the drafted next step, which the dyadic inventory defeats and which repeated an earlier task. All changes were made. The reviewer also ran the recursion on the \(\mathbb F_3\) control at \(D=2\), recovering no refutation for \(A_+\) and a refutation for \(A_-\), and confirmed the base-monotonicity argument with its caveat on weak-only maps. No computation was needed.

Process assessment. The cycle was opened as the promised construction. Reading the recorded PC criterion first showed that its closure already carries the variable actions, so the cycle became a route review. The prerequisite about the weak base was raised in conversation and resolved from existing records. The first drafted next step repeated a task the assembly audit had already set and failed on. It was drafted after searching the claim index but before reading the parked items on the same route item, the order that CLAUDE.md prescribes the other way round. The standing reviewer caught it.

A closed moment tower reduces to the recorded mixed-moment system

21 September 2026 · Negative test of a proposed object; reformulation of recorded results · The three-selector obstruction is removed only by saturation, which reproduces the mixed-moment system. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question and stopping rule. The route review parked the resolution-side complex. In conversation the user asked whether a functional-side object in the spirit of the bit-PHP chessboard argument could do better. There, the unknown moments are chessboard chains, the marginal equations are their boundary, and homology vanishing gives extension. The success criteria were fixed before starting. (1) The object must have a vanishing condition that implies PC hardness at ceiling \(4p-1\). (2) The three-selector obstruction must appear as a nonzero class, and a filtration, degree window, restriction or saturation must remove it without circularity. (3) Only after that, new reach. This cycle tests (1) and (2) on route item odd-prime-clause-transfer. The existing functional-side parts are the augmented moment complex, the one-predicate theorem and the pair theorem; the proposed new ingredient was PC closure together with the block product \(P\).

The object

Let \(\Gamma\) be the functional linear-row PHP base, a legitimate strengthening for the ordinary target by the route review. Take one complete accuracy-one block with inputs \(q_i=1-L_i^{p-1}\), product \(P=1-\sum_jr_jq_j\) of degree \(p\), companions \(E_i=q_iP\) and fresh fields. Write src for \(\Gamma\) with fields and companions, and cond for \(\Gamma\) with fields and the selectors \(q_i\) themselves, in which every input is nonzero. Let \(C_d\) be the PC consequence space at ceiling \(d\), and \[ O_d=\frac{C_{d+1}\cap\mathcal P_{\le d}}{C_d}. \] A normalized annihilator of \(C_d\) extends to \(C_{d+1}\) exactly when it kills \(C_{d+1}\cap\mathcal P_{\le d}\); if all \(O_d\) vanish below \(D\) and \(1\notin C_0\), there is no refutation at ceiling \(D\). This is the historical duality lemma applied degree by degree. Without blocks, vanishing in the stable range is the matching filtration theorem that the bit-PHP paper derives from chessboard homology. Nonvanishing for sources is what the record calls failure of raw augmented filtration stability, already shown by the singleton control. Criterion (1) therefore holds only as an exact restatement.

Two maps connect the systems. Multiplying a cond derivation by \(P\) gives \(P\cdot C_c(\text{cond})\subseteq C_{c+p}(\text{src})\): axioms \(q_i\) become companions, old and field axioms \(a\) become \(aP\) derived monomial by monomial, and multiplication steps commute with \(P\). This is historical Lemma 1.4 with weight \(P\). Setting the fresh variables to zero maps \(C_d(\text{src})\) into \(C_d(\text{cond})\), as the recorded coefficient maps do. Multiplication by \(P\) thus induces \(\pi_P:O_d(\text{cond})\to O_{d+p}(\text{src})\).

The three-selector test

A nonzero transferred class. In the recorded control, (TF-source) is \(P\) times (TF-linear), so \(TP=\pi_P(T)\) with \(T\in C_3(\text{cond})\). Also \(T\notin C_2(\text{cond})\), since otherwise the transfer would give \(TP\in C_5(\text{src})\), contrary to the recorded equality \(C_5=I_5\) for that source. (The record proves only \(T\notin I_2\); this is the PC statement.) Hence \([TP]=\pi_P[T]\ne0\) in \(O_5(\text{src})\): the class is a genuine conditioned fall transported by \(P\).

Degree windows do not remove it. The fall lies between ceilings five and six, inside the compiler window \(4p-1=11\) at \(p=3\).

Restrictions preserve the derivation. Over \(\mathbb F_3\), for all affine \(A,B\), \[ (1-A^2)+(1-B^2)+(1-(A+B)^2)=3-2(A^2+AB+B^2)=(A-B)^2 , \] so every partial matching restriction keeps \(T'P'\in C_6\), using the Boolean certificate of \(T'^3-T'\). Nonmembership in \(C_5\) on a residual board is not asserted. It needs a residual degree-two design separating \(T'\), which the record builds from joint-lift hypotheses on the full label board, together with the stable range and the four-row trade. A restriction can also make \(T'\) zero or a nonzero constant.

Saturation removes it, but not cheaply. Quotienting by the old and field ideal and by conditioned consequences multiplied by \(P\), \[ \overline O_d=\frac{C_{d+1}(\text{src})\cap\mathcal P_{\le d}}{\bigl(C_d(\text{src})+P\cdot C_{D-p}(\text{cond})+I_D(\Gamma+\text{fields})\bigr)\cap\mathcal P_{\le d}}, \] kills \([TP]\) through \(g=T\). The old and field ideal is needed. For example, the accuracy-one analogue of the singleton fall \(q(1-r)=Pq+r(q^2-q)\) leaves the Boolean remainder \(r(q^2-q)\) after taking \(g=q\). This accuracy-one version is derived here, not cited. The denominator still lies in \(C_D(\text{src})\).

Why this is circular for one block and known for many. Specialization alone gives: a source refutation implies a conditioned refutation, with no vanishing hypothesis. For one block the two regimes, a hard conditioned system via the coefficient map or a refutable one via selector substitution, are the recorded coefficient-map and one-block elimination pair, at additive cost \((p-1)\delta\). So a single-block vanishing statement for \(\overline O\) would add nothing about hardness. For many blocks the saturation must use products \(P_S=\prod_{a\in S}P_a\) and mixed conditioned systems for every block subset. That is the historical mixed-moment system. Historical Example 6.5 shows that separate block feasibility does not give a joint solution, and the assembly audit records the whole-level repair cost.

Assessment and next step

The test fails in the sense fixed in advance. The three-selector class is a conditioned fall transported by \(P\), so no degree window inside the compiler ceiling removes it, and restrictions preserve its derivation. The only modification that removes it is saturation by conditioned consequences. For one block that saturation adds nothing beyond one-block elimination, and for many blocks it is the recorded mixed-moment system with its recorded failure of joint feasibility. The functional-side tower is a faithful dual of the problem, but it gives no new mechanism, because the chessboard argument's key feature, an unconditional vanishing theorem, has no analogue once blocks are present. The one new observation is that the obstruction class factors through \(\pi_P\); it is recorded here without a separate claim.

The next step is unchanged from the route review: the intermediate-rank endpoint for \(p=3\), with the dyadic calibration inventory. A functional-side object should be reopened only with a proposed mechanism that controls the mixed-moment system across block subsets at a cost below the whole-level repair.

Verification gate. Re-read the three-selector review, the augmented moment complex entry and the relevant parts of the one-predicate and pair theorems; searched the claim record for raw filtration stability, conditioned filtrations and mixed-moment results. The standing reviewer checked every statement. It identified prior coverage (historical Lemmas 1.2, 1.4, 6.6 and Example 6.5, the singleton observation), and required four corrections, all adopted: the restriction claim limited to membership; the old and field ideal added to the saturation; the single-block conjecture dropped, because specialization already gives its only consequence; and the verdict reframed around the mixed-moment system. No computation was run. A further review pass was skipped to limit reviewer cost, since the final text only removes or weakens drafted claims.
