Route review: the one weakening-free route to dense tuples found shields them, and shielding may decide the window calibration

22 September 2026 · Route review of derivation-aware alternatives · Weakening junk is removable; the one weakening-free gadget found shields its dense forms. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

The line's general claim. The window review and the row-collapse check left old-variable weights heuristically unable to handle the ternary window. The remaining alternative named there is this: the lines of an actual \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_3})\) refutation are not an arbitrary inventory. Some property of derivations would either exclude the thick dyadic inventory, or supply a mechanism that inventory-only methods lack. What the goal needs is an exclusion of the compiled source, at ceiling \(11\), for every inventory that polynomial-size refutations of ordinary unary PHP actually produce. If every polynomial inventory is produced, derivation structure can matter only through relations between lines. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer.

What the record offers

Searches for proof-order designs, line invariants, closure along derivations and weakening found no derivation-aware construction in either notebook. The binary endpoint, the unrestricted \(\mathrm{Res}(\oplus)\) theorem, is inventory-only: it restricts the actual proof to the graph and compiles every line into a registry slot. The published derivation-aware technique is the closure of Efremenko, Garlík and Itsykson, which keeps a path of lines consistent with PHP under their linear constraints. In the record it appears as Corollary SL: safe systems of rank \(a\) with \(4(a-1)<n\) keep the base hard, at degree \(n/2-a+1\). The window reaches projected rank about \(1140N\), far above \(n/4\), and even blocks below \(n/4\) add their ranks under a common restriction. So a closure argument along a DAG meets the recorded subspace wall, where techniques stop at rank of order \(n\) (imported context: literature). One block at a time is not the difficulty: Corollary SL and the affine-core kernel handle single systems of moderate rank. The window is a simultaneous problem across many blocks. A common restriction adds their ranks, and a common weight pays counting.

Falsification attempts

F1. Weakening realizes every inventory, but is removable. The recorded rules (Part–Tzameret, audited here) include weakening. Given an initial clause \(A\) and equations \(\ell_1=0,\dots,\ell_h=0\), weaken \(A\) to \(X_1\), where \(X_j=A\vee\bigvee_{i\ge j}(\ell_i=0)\), and to \(Y_j=A\vee(\ell_j-1=0)\). Resolving \(X_j\) with \(Y_j\) on \(\ell_j\), with coefficients \(1,-1\), gives the false constant \(1=0\). Simplification deletes it, and contraction gives \(X_{j+1}\). After \(h\) steps the chain returns \(A\), which can replace a later use of the initial. So every tuple appears in a line that is an ancestor of the empty clause, at a cost of \(O(h)\) lines (at least \(3h\) when each weakening adds one equation). This does not make the thick inventory a calibration, because weakening can be eliminated syntactically, exactly as in resolution. Map each line \(C\) to a subline \(C^\circ\), with \(C^\circ=C\) on initials and \((C\vee E)^\circ=C^\circ\) on weakening. For resolution of \(C\vee(f=0)\) with \(D\vee(g=0)\), take the resolvent of the images, with the same \(\alpha,\beta\), if both contain the resolved equations, and otherwise the image lacking its equation, which is a subline of the resolvent. Simplification and contraction map to the same rules or to nothing. The image of the empty clause is empty, the image proof has no more lines and no larger written size, which is the measure of the source, and its lines are sublines of the originals. So without loss of generality refutations are weakening-free, and the chain above collapses to \(A\).

F2. Weakening-free derivations still carry dense forms, shielded. From the Boolean axioms \(B_i=(x_i=0)\vee(x_i-1=0)\) alone, resolving \(L_t=\bigvee_{i\le t}(x_i-1=0)\vee(\textstyle\sum_{i\le t}c_ix_i=0)\) on its last equation with \(B_{t+1}\) on \(x_{t+1}=0\), with coefficients \(1,c_{t+1}\), gives \(L_{t+1}\). Here \(L_1=B_1\) and \(c_1=1\). Ordering the support with a chosen variable \(x_1\) first gives every linear form with \(x_1\) in its support, up to scaling. Now fix \(U\ni1\) and \(X=\bigvee_{i\in U}(x_i-1=0)\). Let \(M=X\vee(\ell=0)\), and let \(L(\ell')=X\vee(\ell'=0)\) be the chain built along an ordering of \(U\) with \(1\) first, so \(\operatorname{supp}\ell'\subseteq U\), the coefficient of \(x_1\) in \(\ell'\) is one, and its shield is exactly \(X\). Resolve \(M\) on \(x_1-1=0\), coefficient \(\alpha\ne0\), with \(L(\ell')\) on \(\ell'\), coefficient one. The result keeps \(X\), because the second premise still contains \(x_1-1=0\), and adds \(\ell'+\alpha x_1-\alpha=0\). For a target linear part \(\lambda\) this forces \(\alpha=\lambda_1-1\), so \(\lambda_1\ne1\) is needed (after scaling \(\lambda\), possible for \(p\ge3\)), and the new equation is \(\lambda-\lambda_1+1=0\): the constant is not free. Repeating gives, in \(O(ht)\) lines without weakening, a line whose equations are the shield \(X\) together with \(h\) prescribed linear parts. It is a Boolean tautology, being soundly derived from the Boolean axioms. Since every support lies in \(U\), on the face \(x_U=0\) every dense equation is a constant: the first, homogeneous one is true and every added one is false. So the line holds because of \(X\) or the first equation, and its dense part carries no information anywhere. That is what "shielded" means here. Whether the recorded mechanisms exclude such blocks cheaply was not checked, and the gadget was not made an ancestor of the empty clause.

Coordinate shields are not preserved. Resolving a shielded line on \(x_1-1=0\) with a hole-exclusion clause \((x_1=0)\vee(x_k=0)\), coefficients \(1,-1\), replaces the shield equation \(x_1=1\) by \(x_k=0\) and leaves the dense equations untouched. The new shield no longer covers their support. The line is still shielded relative to the initials, because \(x_k=1\) with the hole axiom forces \(x_1=0\). So a useful notion of shielding must be semantic relative to the initials, not syntactic coverage of the support.

F3. Unshielded dense forms are expected, but structured ones. Counting derivations, with lines stating that a row sum or hole sum lies in \(\{0,1\}\), are expected to produce dense forms without a shield; no such derivation was written out here. Their forms are row and hole sums, not random tuples. The recorded row obstruction class of the row-collapse entry is the projected form of exactly these equations.

Assessment of this line

Weakening can be eliminated at no cost, so derivation structure does constrain which lines matter. The one weakening-free route to arbitrary dense tuples found here shields them, and the only unshielded dense forms considered are structured counting forms. One gadget and one counting family do not show anything about all derivations. Conditional on a definition of shielding, still to be given, the question divides the line. If some polynomial-size weakening-free refutation contains unshielded random dense tuples of window rank among the ancestors of the empty clause, derivation structure gives no leverage on the inventory. The window must then be handled as a simultaneous gluing problem across blocks. That problem is the historical mixed-moment system, whose pairwise-to-joint failure is Example 6.5, and whose one assembling repair has a cost that does not fit. If no refutation does, the calibration must be restated for shielded tuples, structured counting forms and partly shielded mixtures. It was too pessimistic only if those are cheaper to exclude, which is unchecked. The line's prospects are open: its decisive question is new and not yet attempted. The alternatives are either heuristically excluded (weights) or meet a recorded wall (closure).

Next step on the highest-risk item

Route item odd-prime-clause-transfer. Decide the shielding question. First define shielding semantically relative to the initials: a subset of a line's equations whose simultaneous falsity, together with the initials, forces a restriction on which the tuple's selectors are constants. Test the definition on the three recorded cases: the F2 gadget and its hole-clause variant must count as shielded, and the counting lines of F3 as allowed structured forms. Then either construct a polynomial-size weakening-free derivation, from the ordinary unary PHP initials over \(\mathbb F_3\), of an ancestor of the empty clause containing an unshielded random dense tuple of projected rank at least \(N/(4.4\times10^7)\), or find an invariant preserved by resolution with the initials, including the hole-exclusion clauses, and by simplification. If an invariant forces shielding, the next cycle checks whether shielded blocks fall under the affine-core kernel or exact prefixes on the graph base.

Sheaf check

This is the first object in the cycle with a locality that comes from derivations rather than from a chosen cover. A shielded line is informative only where its shield is false, a face cut out relative to the initials. Blocks would then be sections over the poset of coordinate faces, glued by restriction, and the site is the restriction poset, not the block-subset complex. Whether that presheaf has a vanishing property depends on the shielding question. If shielding fails, the only gluing site left is the block-subset complex, the mixed-moment system, whose recorded pairwise-to-joint failure stands.

Verification gate. Re-read Corollary SL with its proof, the recorded Part–Tzameret rules and the weakening step of the compiler, historical Example 6.5 and the whole-level repair of the assembly audit. Searches covered derivation-aware constructions, weakening elimination, shields, closure along derivations and the binary endpoint; none records weakening elimination or shielding. No computation was run. A narrowly briefed fresh-context reviewer checked the weakening chain, the elimination argument in every case and the gadget, which were verified only by this review. It required changes, all adopted: the chain cost, written size in the elimination, the gadget's hypotheses and exact constants, the precise meaning of shielding, the hole-clause obstruction to coordinate shields, softening the title and assessment, making the dichotomy conditional on a definition and not presuming shielded blocks easy, a semantic definition in the next step, and comparing ranks with Corollary SL.

Shielding made precise: resolving with a line true on the test set adds no information

22 September 2026 · Working observation (one step); assessment of the shielding question · The question looks no cheaper than a critical-assignment structure theorem. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. The derivation review asked whether weakening-free refutations must shield random dense tuples of window rank, and asked first for a semantic definition of shielding relative to the initials. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The definition cannot use all points satisfying the initials, because PHP has none, and every line is then vacuously implied. This cycle fixes a test set, proves the one-step fact behind the definition, and assesses whether the question is cheaper than the goal.

Definition and setting

Work over \(\mathbb F_3\) with the recorded rules, and with weakening-free refutations, which the review showed costs nothing. Let \(W\) be a set of Boolean points on which every initial except the row clauses is true. The main example is the critical assignments of ordinary unary PHP with \(N+1\) rows and \(N\) holes, the matchings that leave exactly one row unmatched. On it the Boolean axioms and the hole-exclusion clauses are true, and a row clause is falsified exactly where its row is unmatched. For a line \(C\), a disjunction of equations, let \(\mathrm F_W(C)\) be the set of points of \(W\) at which every equation of \(C\) is false. Call \(C\) a \(W\)-tautology if \(\mathrm F_W(C)=\varnothing\), and call two lines \(W\)-equivalent if they have the same \(\mathrm F_W\). A set \(E\) of equations of \(C\) is shielded in \(C\) if \(C\) is \(W\)-equivalent to \(C\setminus E\), and informative otherwise. In the realizability question, the line must be an ancestor of the empty clause.

The one-step observation

Observation. Let \(P_1=C\vee(f=0)\) and \(T=T'\vee(g=0)\), with \(T\) a \(W\)-tautology, and let \(R=C\vee T'\vee(\alpha f+\beta g=0)\) be their resolvent under the recorded rule. If \(\alpha\ne0\), then \(\mathrm F_W(R)=\mathrm F_W(C\vee T'\vee(f=0))\). If \(\alpha=0\), then \(R\) is a \(W\)-tautology.

Proof. Let \(w\in W\) falsify \(C\vee T'\). Since \(T\) is true at \(w\), \(g(w)=0\). So \((\alpha f+\beta g)(w)=\alpha f(w)\), which vanishes exactly when \(f(w)=0\) if \(\alpha\ne0\), and always if \(\alpha=0\). Points at which \(C\vee T'\) is true lie in neither set. \(\square\)

So resolution with a \(W\)-tautology shrinks the falsification set by the added disjuncts \(T'\), and its new equation can be replaced by the old \(f\) without changing \(\mathrm F_W\). (Deleting it would in general change \(\mathrm F_W\).) Simplification and contraction do not change \(\mathrm F_W\).

Conjecture-level extension, not proved. In a weakening-free derivation, every line should be \(W\)-equivalent to a line whose equations are built from the row-clause coordinates by resolutions between two \(W\)-falsifiable lines. That would need an induction: later steps resolve on \(\alpha f+\beta g\), not on \(f\), and resolution is not a congruence for \(W\)-equivalence, although at points falsifying the other disjuncts the scaling agrees. The claim is false with weakening, which adds any equation that holds somewhere on \(\mathrm F_W\) of the line.

The recorded cases

  • The Boolean-axiom gadget. Take as \(E\) its \(h\) added equations. Then \(C\setminus E=X\vee(\ell_1=0)\) is the chain line \(L(\ell_1)\), a Boolean tautology, so \(E\) is shielded. If \(E\) also contains the first, homogeneous equation, it is not shielded, since \(X\) alone is falsified on the face \(x_U=0\).
  • Its hole-clause variant. Resolving \(X\vee(\ell_1=0)\) with the same hole clause, in the same way, gives exactly \(C\setminus E\) of the resolved gadget line. It is a \(W\)-tautology on critical assignments, since both premises are, so \(E\) is again shielded.
  • Counting lines. Take \((s=0)\vee(s=1)\) for a row sum \(s\). It is a \(W\)-tautology, but no nonempty set of its equations is shielded, since the row is matched in some critical assignments and unmatched in others. For a hole sum, \((s=0)\) is shielded and \((s=1)\) is informative. What holds for all counting lines is the Observation: they are inert as resolution partners. The row equation \((s=1)\), derived from them and the row clause in several steps, is falsified exactly where row \(i\) is unmatched. It is informative, and it is the recorded row class. F3 of the review said counting derivations give unshielded dense forms; under this definition that holds for such row and hole equations, and they are structured.

What the shielding question becomes

If the conjecture-level extension holds, the dense forms that matter are those of \(W\)-falsifiable lines, generated by resolutions between two \(W\)-falsifiable lines. The review's question then asks which forms can be informative in \(W\)-falsifiable lines of small weakening-free \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_3})\) refutations. This is an analogy, not a reduction: it has the shape of a critical-assignment structure theorem, like the width argument for resolution, or the closure of Efremenko, Garlík and Itsykson for \(\mathrm{Res}(\oplus)\), which is proved only for bottom-regular proofs and which meets the recorded subspace wall in general. No implication in either direction between the shielding question and a lower bound is shown. For the other direction, realizability can presumably only be relative, since polynomial-size refutations are conjectured not to exist: from a refutation \(\pi\), build \(\pi'\) of size polynomial in \(|\pi|\) whose ancestors of the empty clause contain an informative random tuple. The Observation blocks one obvious insertion. Adding a random form to a line \(K=C\vee(f=0)\) of \(\pi\) through a two-equation partner \((f=0)\vee(g=0)\) with dense \(g\) is informative only if that partner is itself \(W\)-falsifiable. General partners \(T'\vee(g=0)\) were not analyzed.

Assessment and next step

Shielding is now defined relative to a test set, and the recorded gadget and its hole-clause variant are shielded, by short checks. The question the review called cheap does not look cheap. In my assessment, deciding it in the direction that helps the route, that informative tuples in small refutations are structured, would take a critical-assignment structure theorem for \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_3})\) of the kind the closure methods attempt, and I see no reason it would avoid the wall. So derivation structure does not appear to offer a shortcut past the window, and the inventory-based formulation with the thick calibration remains the working one. Together with the heuristic exclusion of weights and the wall for closure, the record currently contains no mechanism that looks likely to handle the window. Next step (odd-prime-clause-transfer): secure what the recorded mechanisms do prove. The record has no end-to-end corollary of the low-or-dense exclusion, whose index entry notes that full-board and graph-restricted ranks are not identified. State a superpolynomial lower bound for ordinary unary PHP in \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_3})\) for refutations whose lines satisfy a rank hypothesis stated on the proof itself, for example every line's forms spanning rank at most a small multiple of \(N\), after checking that the graph restriction and projection do not raise rank. Write it as a lemma naming one probability space and one graph, with the exact accounting.

Sheaf check

In my assessment, the natural candidate is the assignment of falsification sets to lines, evaluated on critical assignments, with Observation-type steps acting by intersection with \(\mathrm F_W(T')\). The good property a glued object would need, low rank of informative forms on small patches, is the structure question above, and gluing does not supply it.

Verification gate. Re-read the derivation review, including the gadget and the hole-clause variant, and the recorded Part–Tzameret rules. Searched the record for falsification sets, critical assignments and tautology resolution. The matches, switching and decision-tree rows such as the two-role switching theorem and the wide-rounds transfer, do not contain the Observation. No computation was run. A narrowly briefed fresh-context reviewer confirmed the Observation in every case, including \(\alpha=0\) and \(\beta=0\). It rejected the draft's claim that new forms are informative only through two falsifiable premises, since that needs an induction and fails with weakening; that claim is now a conjecture-level extension. It corrected the three recorded cases, the counting case substantially. It required the hypotheses on \(W\), the field, weakening-freeness and ancestry to be stated, and the analogies and assessments to be labelled as such. All changes were adopted.

Ternary Res(Lin) refutations need lines with many independent nonlocal forms

22 September 2026 · Working proof (composition of recorded results) · Extends the row- and column-local corollary to nonlocal dimension \(N^{1/2-\varepsilon}\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. The shielding entry found no live mechanism for the ternary window and asked to secure what the recorded mechanisms prove end to end. The row- and column-local corollary is the only recorded \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_3})\) endpoint on this thread. It needs every equation form to be local. The quotient-rank exclusion allows sublinear nonlinear rank per block, but no proof-system statement was drawn from it. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. A plain bound on the linear rank of lines cannot be the hypothesis, because every row clause has rank \(N\). The right measure counts only forms whose selectors are not affine.

Statement

Call an affine form on the \((N+1)\)-by-\(N\) board local if, modulo the linear row equations, it is supported in a single row or a single column, constants included. For a line of a \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_3})\) refutation, its nonlocal dimension is the dimension of the span of the linear parts of those of its equations \(L=0\) whose form \(L\) is not local.

Corollary ND. Fix \(0<\varepsilon\le1/2\) and \(K>0\). For all sufficiently large \(N\), ordinary unary \(\mathrm{PHP}^{N+1}_N\) and its functional variant have no standard syntactic \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_3})\) refutation with at most \(N^K\) lines in which every line has nonlocal dimension at most \(N^{1/2-\varepsilon}\). Clauses may have arbitrary width, and subproofs may be shared without a depth restriction.

Proof

Suppose such a refutation has \(S\le N^K\) lines. The complete-board transfer at \(p=3\) gives a complete accuracy-one selector source over the full functional linear-row PHP base, with at most \(S\) blocks, at most \(\binom{v+2}{2}\) inputs per block, \(v=N(N+1)\), all coefficient fields, and an ordinary PC refutation through \(D=11\). Each input is literally \(q=1-L^2\) for an equation \(L=0\) of the source line of its block: by the selector compiler that the transfer specializes, a block's inputs are a basis subset, chosen by compression, of the selectors of that one line, and resolution uses the premises' completed values without adding their selectors as inputs. So \(V_a\) below lies in the span of the line's selectors. Both variants of PHP land on the full functional linear-row base, which is the base of the quotient-rank theorem and of the affine classification, with the same degree-two consequence space \(I_2\) over \(\mathbb F_3\).

Fix a block \(a\). In the notation of the quotient-rank theorem, let \(V_a\) be the span of its selectors in \(Q_2=\mathcal P_{\le2}/I_2\), let \(A_a=V_a\cap\overline{\mathcal P_{\le1}}\), and \(r_a=\dim(V_a/A_a)\). Since \(A_a\) is the intersection of \(V_a\) with the affine classes, \(V_a/A_a\) embeds into \(Q_2/\overline{\mathcal P_{\le1}}\), so \(r_a\) is at most the dimension of the span of the selector images there.

  • For a local form \(L\), the affine classification (\(N\ge4\)) gives an affine \(A\) with \(1-L^2-A\in I_2\). Its image is zero.
  • For a nonlocal form, write \(L=\ell+c\) with \(\ell\) linear and \(c\) constant. Then \(1-L^2=(1-c^2-2c\ell)-\ell^2\), whose image is that of \(-\ell^2\). Here \(\ell\) lies in the span \(U\) of the nonlocal linear parts of the line, of dimension \(r\le N^{1/2-\varepsilon}\). Hence \(\ell^2\) lies in the span of the products \(u_su_t\) of a basis of \(U\), of dimension at most \(r(r+1)/2\).

So \(r_a\le r(r+1)/2\le N^{1-2\varepsilon}\) when \(r\ge1\), and \(r_a=0\) when \(r=0\). The inventory is polynomial, the degree \(11\) is polylogarithmic (after the rank-one step inside that theorem its ceiling is \(\max(D,7)=11\)), and \(0\le\sigma=1-2\varepsilon<1\). Initial clauses have local forms only and cost nothing. The quotient-rank theorem, with no logarithmic factor needed, excludes the PC refutation for sufficiently large \(N\), where "sufficiently large" depends on \(K\) and \(\varepsilon\). \(\square\)

Scope

  • The case of nonlocal dimension zero is the recorded row- and column-local corollary. The new content is that any polynomial-size refutation needs, in some line, more than \(N^{1/2-\varepsilon}\) independent nonlocal forms, regardless of how many local forms it contains.
  • The bound \(r(r+1)/2\) is where the square root enters. The theorem applies to any line through \(r_a\) itself; the corollary uses only the linear bound, to keep a hypothesis stated on the proof itself.
  • This does not touch the window. Lines with nonlocal dimension above \(N^{1/2-\varepsilon}\) remain open. Their \(r_a\) is not determined by the dimension: it can be small or as large as \(r(r+1)/2\).

Assessment and next step

This is a proof-system statement with a hypothesis on the proof itself. It moves the recorded endpoint from no nonlocal forms to \(N^{1/2-\varepsilon}\) independent ones per line, for every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\). It is a partial result, not progress on the window. Next step (odd-prime-clause-transfer): this line has now had a route review, two negative tests of derivation structure and this consolidation. The derivation review and the window review leave no recorded mechanism for the window. Hold a route review of the whole odd-prime thread: compare continuing on the ternary window with a publishable write-up of the recorded partial endpoints, and with the thread's other route items.

Sheaf check

No gluing is involved: the corollary uses one common weight, through the quotient-rank theorem. No sheaf with a new property appeared.

Verification gate. Re-read the statements of the complete-board transfer, the affine classification with its necessity and sufficiency proof, the quotient-rank theorem with its basis conversion, and the recorded row- and column-local corollary with its source reduction. Before drafting, a fresh-context reviewer checked whether the record already implies the statement and found that it does not: the local corollary is the case \(r=0\), and the related row-remainder and occupancy theorems allow different perturbations. No computation was run. A second narrowly briefed fresh-context reviewer checked the proof, reading the selector compiler's inventory argument to confirm that block inputs come from one line only, and found no mathematical gap. It required the citation of that compiler, an explicit statement of the common base, and the removal of three overclaims in the scope: an unproved example of small quadratic span, an unproved graph version at \(\varepsilon=0\), and the range of the open case. All changes were adopted.

Route review of the odd-prime thread: the partial endpoints are secured, and the ternary window has no recorded mechanism

22 September 2026 · Route review of the whole odd-prime thread · Recommends consolidating the partial endpoints before any further window attempt. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

The line's general claim. The binary endpoint, the unrestricted \(\mathrm{Res}(\oplus)\) theorem, compiles every line into a complete block and excludes the whole source with one common weight on a separated graph. The thread's claim is that this route extends to \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) for every fixed odd prime \(p\). The compiler extends (complete-board transfer, degree \(4p-1\)). What the goal needs is the exclusion step for every polynomial inventory of complete accuracy-one blocks on selectors \(1-L^{p-1}\). Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer, the highest-risk item; the other two items, composition bookkeeping and review, depend on it.

What is secured

  • All primes, affine inputs: the all-prime affine exclusion.
  • \(p=3\), proof-system endpoints: every form row- or column-local (local corollary); every nonlocal part of each line of dimension at most \(N^{1/2-\varepsilon}\) (Corollary ND).
  • All primes, source level: forms on at most \(n^\alpha\operatorname{polylog}n\) rows, \(\alpha<1/5\) (row-support exclusion, with its recorded restricted-query \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) consequence), with the probe and occupancy variants.
  • \(p=3\), source level on a separated graph: projected nonlinear rank at most about \(N/(4.4\times10^7)\) or at least \(Q_*=O(N^{3/2}\sqrt{\log N})\) (low-or-dense criterion), lowered to about \(N\log N\) for clique heads, with the dyadic band removed by additive elimination.

The source-level results on the graph are not yet proof-system statements, because graph-projected ranks are not identified with ranks on the proof.

Falsification attempts

Is the target easy? With onto axioms it is. Deriving the row sums \(\sum_jx_{ij}=1\) and the hole sums \(\sum_ix_{ij}=1\), and adding them, gives \(0=1\) over \(\mathbb F_p\) in polynomial size, because \(N+1\ne N\). This standard counting argument needs the onto axioms. Ordinary PHP only gives hole sums in \(\{0,1\}\), and a sum of \(N\) such values modulo \(p\) cannot be compared with \(N+1\) without tracking it beyond \(p\). The thread's window review found no cheap refutation of the thick inventory's source either. The target is therefore not refuted by counting.

Is the window an artifact of the method? Every tested line says no so far. Old-variable weights miss it heuristically: a sign ambiguity \(L\in\{1,2\}\) makes each block's false set a union of flats, so the Macaulay gain is quadratic in \(k\) like the separator's loss (ceiling, review). The only alignment found is a small-degree row collapse. Sign variables are definable. Mixtures and product designs reproduce the historical mixed-moment failure. Topological and sheaf objects reduced to recorded mechanisms (complex review, moment tower, matching sheaf). Closure along derivations meets the recorded subspace wall, and derivation structure does not appear to help. The two main uncertainties remain as the window review stated them: the semi-regular model and general position are heuristics, and proving them for random quadrics would touch the open Fröberg-type questions.

Assessment of this line

The binary route extends as far as the flat structure of the false sets allows, and stops where the sign ambiguity starts. Within the thread, progress in the last two days has been partial endpoints and precise obstructions, not movement on the window. The evidence against old-variable weights in the window is heuristic but consistent, and no recorded mechanism of another kind survives testing. The prospects of the window, by the methods in the record, are weak. The partial endpoints are real and currently scattered across entries and levels (source or proof system, graph or complete board).

Next step on the highest-risk item

Route item odd-prime-clause-transfer remains the highest risk, and no cycle on the window is proposed until a new mechanism is named. The next step consolidates, under route item scope-and-review: state in one place every proof-system consequence the recorded source exclusions give for \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\), with exact hypotheses stated on the proof. That means the local corollary, Corollary ND and the recorded row-support consequence, checked for mutual implications and combined where a line may mix their hypotheses. Record which graph-level statements do not yet have one. A new window attempt is worth a cycle only if it names a mechanism that is not an old-variable weight, a closure along derivations or a gluing of local designs, and tests it first on the thick inventory.

Sheaf check

Across the thread, every glued object tried (the block complex, the moment tower, the matching sheaf, the falsification-set presheaf) either computes the recorded PC data or needs a structure theorem that gluing does not supply. No sheaf with a vanishing property beyond the recorded mechanisms has appeared. A new one would have to handle the sign ambiguity itself. A double cover by sign variables does not, since the window review showed those variables are definable at degree two, and none is proposed here.

The recorded odd-prime Res(Lin) endpoints form three incomparable classes, and mixing them across lines is open

22 September 2026 · Consolidation with separating examples · Three incomparable proof-line classes; no statement covers refutations mixing them. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. The thread route review asked to state in one place every proof-system consequence of the recorded source exclusions, with hypotheses on the proof, and to check mutual implications. Route item: scope-and-review. Throughout, the object is ordinary unary \(\mathrm{PHP}^{n+1}_n\), and the recorded functional variants are noted where they are stated. "Superpolynomial" means that for every \(K\), refutations with at most \(n^K\) lines are excluded for large \(n\). Forms are taken modulo the linear row equations. All four results below compile through the complete-board or weak-base transfer, whose block inputs are selectors of one line.

The recorded classes

  1. Remainder class, every fixed \(p\) (sublinear row-remainder exclusion). Fix \(\alpha<1\). Each line has at most \(c_0\log_pn\) affine probes \(U_j\), and each of its forms is \(\ell+\sum_jb_jU_j\) with \(\ell\) supported on at most \(n^\alpha\operatorname{polylog}n\) rows. The probes may differ between lines. This contains the row-support and log-probe classes.
  2. Nonlocal-dimension class, \(p=3\) (Corollary ND). Fix \(\varepsilon>0\). In each line, the forms that are not row- or column-local span dimension at most \(n^{1/2-\varepsilon}\). This contains the local corollary, the case of dimension zero.
  3. Occupancy class, every fixed \(p\), weak base (occupancy-shifted columns). Each form is a global affine column-occupancy statistic plus an arbitrary perturbation inside one column. Statistics and columns may differ between forms.

Mutual relations

The three classes are pairwise incomparable. The separating lines are elementary. In each, the property shown is the one the other class needs, checked against its definition.

  • ND but not remainder. A line with \(n^{0.4}\) independent random dense forms over all cells has nonlocal dimension \(n^{0.4}\), which is within ND for \(\varepsilon<0.1\). For the remainder class, the forms modulo any \(O(\log n)\) probes span a space of dimension at least \(n^{0.4}-O(\log n)\). With high probability each such residual still involves almost every row.
  • Remainder but not ND. Take the forms \(x_{1,j}+x_{2,j+1}\), \(j=1,\dots,n-1\). Each reads two rows, so it lies in the remainder class with no probes. None is local: it has two rows and two different columns, and reducing modulo the row equations changes neither. They are independent, so the nonlocal dimension is \(n-1\).
  • Occupancy versus the others. A line whose forms are distinct column-occupancy statistics, independent in number \(n^{0.9}\), lies in the occupancy class. It is outside ND because its nonlocal dimension is too large. It is outside the remainder class when the statistics involve most rows and are independent beyond \(O(\log n)\) probes. Conversely, random dense forms lie in neither the occupancy class nor its perturbations.

Within the classes, the local corollary is the dimension-zero case of ND. The remainder class with \(t=0\) and one row contains the row-local forms. Column-local forms lie in ND at no cost. In the remainder class each counts as a probe, so a line may contain only \(O(\log n)\) independent column-local forms.

What is not covered

  • Mixing across lines. Each result assumes its hypothesis for every line of the refutation. A refutation whose lines fall into different classes, some in the remainder class and some in ND, is covered by none of them. The exclusion mechanisms differ: the remainder class uses a matching restriction, switching and a reader coefficient map, while ND uses one weight through the quotient-rank theorem. Combining them would need one design that handles both kinds of block. A matching restriction is compatible with a common weight in the graph construction, which suggests a combined statement may be within reach. That is untested.
  • Graph-level statements. The low-or-dense criterion and its clique extension are stated on graph-projected ranks. They have no proof-system form, because projection can lower rank and the dense side is not inherited from the proof.
  • The window itself. Lines with many independent nonlocal forms spread over many rows, in number beyond \(n^{1/2}\) and beyond logarithmically many probes, fall under none of the classes.

Assessment and next step

The recorded proof-system endpoints are three incomparable classes. None of them states that a refutation may mix classes across lines, and that is the most direct strengthening available from the recorded mechanisms. Next step (odd-prime-clause-transfer): test whether ND and the remainder class combine. Every block in a mixed inventory is either of ND type (nonlocal quotient rank at most \(n^{1-2\varepsilon}\)) or of remainder type. Check whether the matching restriction of the remainder proof preserves the quotient-rank hypothesis of the ND blocks, and whether the quotient-rank theorem's weight survives on the restricted board. The smallest nonvacuous inventory has one block of each type. The count to make first is the degree budget: \(sD_*=n^{\alpha+o(1)}\) for the remainder blocks against the quotient-rank theorem's degree requirement on the restricted board of size \(N=n^\beta\).

Sheaf check

The mixing question is a gluing question in the literal sense. There are two local exclusion mechanisms, each valid on its class of blocks, and the task is to glue them over one inventory. It is the first gluing problem on this thread where both local pieces are proved theorems. Whether they glue depends on the common restriction, which is the next step's test.

Refutations mixing row-support lines and low-nonlocal-dimension lines are still excluded

22 September 2026 · Working proof (one combined replay of recorded maps) · Mixed endpoint for row support \(n^{\alpha}\), \(\alpha<1/5\), and nonlocal dimension \(n^\eta\), \(\eta<(1-\alpha)/8\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. The consolidation found the recorded proof-system classes pairwise incomparable, and no statement covering refutations whose lines fall into different classes. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. This cycle tests whether the row-support class and the nonlocal-dimension class combine. The two exclusions use different mechanisms: a matching restriction with switching and an old-only reader map, and a common weight on a robust graph. The question is whether one replay can use both. The recorded precedent of a failed composition, the heavy-round composition gap, concerned two switching arguments on different families. Here only one switching argument is used.

Statement

Forms are taken modulo the linear row equations, and "local" and "nonlocal dimension" are as in Corollary ND.

Proposition MX. Fix \(0\le\alpha<1/5\), \(0\le\eta<(1-\alpha)/8\) and \(K>0\). For all sufficiently large \(n\), ordinary unary \(\mathrm{PHP}^{n+1}_n\) and its functional variant have no standard syntactic \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_3})\) refutation with at most \(n^K\) lines in which every line satisfies at least one of:

  1. every equation form of the line is supported on at most \(n^\alpha\operatorname{polylog}n\) rows, with a fixed logarithmic exponent;
  2. the line has nonlocal dimension at most \(n^\eta\).

Different lines may satisfy different alternatives.

Proof

Parameters. Choose fixed \(\beta\) and \(\sigma\) with \[ \max(\alpha,2\eta)<\beta<\frac{1-\alpha}4,\qquad \frac{2\eta}{\beta}<\sigma<1 , \] which is possible because \(\alpha<1/5\) and \(2\eta<(1-\alpha)/4\). Put \(N=\lceil n^\beta\rceil\) and fix an integer \(s>2K/(1-\alpha-4\beta)\). The polylogarithmic factor of \(R\) is absorbed into the \(o(1)\) of the switching exponent, and "sufficiently large" depends on \(\alpha\), \(\eta\), \(K\) and that fixed polylogarithmic exponent.

Compilation. The complete-board transfer gives at most \(n^K\) complete accuracy-one blocks over the full functional linear-row base on the \((n+1)\)-by-\(n\) board, with an ordinary PC refutation \(\Pi\) through \(D=11\). By the selector compiler, a block's inputs are selectors \(q=1-L^2\) of equations of one line. Call a block of type (i) or (ii) according to an alternative its line satisfies, choosing (i) when both hold.

Row-local expansion, charged to the axioms only. For each input of a type-(i) block, (RL-expansion) of the row-local expansion lemma gives an exact coefficient-one sum \(G\) of pairwise incompatible matching terms with \(q-G\in I_C\), where \(C=\max(2,R,1)\) and \(R=n^\alpha\operatorname{polylog}n\). The source is not replaced. The identity is used only below, to certify axiom images.

One restriction. Apply the empty-aware switching estimate, exactly as in the row-support exclusion, to the ordered disjunctions of the terms of the type-(i) blocks only. Their term width is at most \(\max(1,R)\), and there are at most \(n^K\) of them. With these parameters, a uniform partial matching leaving an \((N+1)\)-by-\(N\) board gives every type-(i) block a residual tree of height below \(s\), except with probability \(o(1)\). Fix such a restriction \(\rho\). It is a ring map sending the old functional axioms of the large board to old axioms of the residual board or to zero, as in that proof, so every old certificate survives with its degree.

Type-(ii) blocks after \(\rho\). Restriction is affine on forms. A row-local form becomes row-local or constant, a column-local form becomes column-local or constant, and the span of the images of the nonlocal linear parts has dimension at most \(n^\eta\). So, exactly as in the proof of Corollary ND on the residual functional board (\(N\ge4\)), every type-(ii) block has certified nonlinear quotient rank \(r_a\le n^{2\eta}\le N^{\sigma}\) for large \(n\). Apply the quotient-rank theorem's degree-certified basis conversion and rank-one representation to the type-(ii) blocks only. This rewrites the proof with ceiling \(\max(D,7)=11\), which is the \(D\) used below. The conversion is blockwise, its certificates are over the old residual base, and type-(i) axioms pass through it unchanged. The type-(ii) coefficient images below are the linear pull-back \(r_i=\sum_j\beta_{ji}t_j\) composed with the semantic map. The rank condition is needed after the graph restriction and row projection. As in the quotient-rank theorem, restriction and projection do not increase the number of nonlinear basis positions, so the power-range parameters are bottom exponent \(0\) and parent exponent \(\sigma\), with \(0+\sigma<1\).

Graph and weight. On the residual board choose a robust graph and row projection as in the power-range corollary, and restrict \(\Pi\) further to it. The converted type-(ii) blocks form a two-level source with bottom rank at most one and parent quotient rank at most \(N^\sigma\operatorname{polylog}N\). The two-level semantic map for these blocks alone gives one weight \(f\) of degree at most \(k=N^{1/2}\operatorname{polylog}N\) and coefficient images of degree at most \(T=O(N^{1/2}\operatorname{polylog}N+N^\sigma\operatorname{polylog}N)\). Every weighted companion and field image of these blocks is certified through \(Te+k\) and \(3T+k\) (its step 4). The weight \(f\) and its degree \(k\) are built only from the parent affine cores and unused bottom tuples of the converted type-(ii) blocks, an inventory of at most \(n^K=N^{K/\beta}\) blocks, polynomial in \(N\). Type-(i) blocks add no cores, and the graph does not depend on them.

Type-(i) coefficient map. For a type-(i) block, the complete matching-reader interface on its residual tree of height \(t<s\), applied to its expanded inputs \(g_i=\rho(G_i)\) of degree at most \(R\), gives old polynomials \(v,\beta_i\) of degree at most \(t\) with \[ 1-v-\sum_i\beta_ig_i\in\mathcal I_{t+R},\qquad g_iv\in\mathcal I_{t+R},\qquad \beta_i^3-\beta_i\in\mathcal I_{3t}. \] Map the original coefficient \(r_i\) of input \(q_i\) to \(\beta_i\). Write \(\bar q_i=\rho(q_i)\). The product image is \(1-\sum_i\beta_i\bar q_i=v+(1-v-\sum_i\beta_ig_i)+\sum_i\beta_i(g_i-\bar q_i)\), and \(g_i-\bar q_i\in\mathcal I_C\). Therefore each companion image satisfies \[ \bar q_i\Bigl(1-\sum_j\beta_j\bar q_j\Bigr)=g_iv+(\bar q_i-g_i)v+\bar q_i\Bigl[(1-v-\textstyle\sum_j\beta_jg_j)+\sum_j\beta_j(g_j-\bar q_j)\Bigr]\in\mathcal I_{C+t+2}, \] since \(C\ge R\) and \(\bar q_i\) has degree two. Field images lie in \(\mathcal I_{3t}\). These are ideal memberships over the old residual base. The graph restriction is a ring map on the old axioms, and the affine row projection \(\Psi\) of the projection lemma maps every old graph axiom to one with an old projected proof through degree two. Applying both to \(v\), the \(\beta_i\) and every membership keeps them over the projected base \(\Gamma'_H\) with the same degrees, and PC proofs over \(\Gamma'_H\) with ceiling at least two lift back to \(\Gamma_H\).

One replay. Substitute all coefficient variables of \(\Pi\) by their images: the type-(ii) images of degree at most \(T\), and the type-(i) images of degree at most \(t<s\). Multiply every line by \(f\). Work over \(\Gamma'_H\), as in step 4 of the semantic map. That step certifies each axiom image separately, and the only fact it uses about the base is that weighted old projected graph axioms are legal multiples. Separation holds against the old graph ideal, not only Booleanity. So axioms whose images are old-ideal members, rather than zero on the whole cube, are admissible. The type-(ii) axiom images are certified by that step. A type-(i) axiom image lies in \(\mathcal I_{C+t+2}\), so its weighted multiple is derivable through \(C+t+2+k\). The substituted proof derives \(f\) over the old graph base through \[ B=\max\bigl(\max(T,s)D,\ C+s+2\bigr)+k=O\bigl(N^{1/2}\operatorname{polylog}N+N^{\sigma}\operatorname{polylog}N+n^{\alpha}\operatorname{polylog}n\bigr). \] Since \(\sigma<1\) and \(n^\alpha=N^{\alpha/\beta}\) with \(\alpha/\beta<1\), this is \(o(N)\), so \(B\le N/10^6\) for large \(n\), inside the graph's linear separation range. Separation is needed through \(B\), not through the map theorem's \(TD+k\). This is why step 4 is rerun here, instead of citing the map theorem or the power-range corollary as a black box. Lifting the projected proof back to the graph base contradicts separation. \(\square\)

Scope

  • It recovers the \(\mathbb F_3\) Res(Lin) consequence of the row-support exclusion (only type-(i) lines), though not that theorem's polylogarithmic-degree PC statement over every prime, and Corollary ND in a weaker range (\(\eta<1/8\) instead of \(1/2\)). The loss is the restriction to a board of size \(n^\beta\), \(\beta<1/4\), which the switching step needs.
  • The replay differs from the row-support proof: it uses the original degree-eleven proof and charges the expansion cost \(C\) to the axiom images only, instead of replaying a converted proof at degree \(\max(D,2C+1)\). Charging \(C\) to the axioms keeps \(B\) additive, of order \(11T+C+k\). Replaying the converted proof at degree \(\max(D,2C+1)\) would give about \(N^{1/2}n^\alpha\), which can exceed \(N\).
  • The probe and sublinear-remainder refinements (\(\alpha<1\)) and the occupancy class are not included. Their mechanisms add a preliminary restriction or a column freezing, whose interaction with the weight was not checked.
  • This is still a restricted class. A line with many independent nonlocal forms spread over many rows lies in neither alternative.

Assessment and next step

The first gluing of two proved local mechanisms on this thread succeeds: a restriction chosen for one class and a weight chosen for the other coexist in one replay, because the old-only reader images of the first class become weighted multiples of old consequences, at a cost \(C+t+2+k\) that fits the weight's separation range since \(n^\alpha=o(N)\). The price is the smaller board. Next step (odd-prime-clause-transfer): test whether the sublinear-remainder refinement, with its preliminary restriction and logarithmically many probes per line, combines in the same way. That would give \(\alpha<1\) for type (i). Then assess whether mixing within one line, with some forms of each kind, is reachable by splitting the block's inputs. The window itself is unchanged.

Sheaf check

This is a genuine gluing with a good property: two local exclusion mechanisms, each proved on its class of blocks, glue along one restriction and one weight, and the glued object excludes the mixed source. What made it glue is that one mechanism's local sections, the reader images, lie in the old ideal. They are therefore compatible with a weight whose separation range contains their cost \(C+t+2+k\). That property is specific to old-only maps, so it does not suggest a way to glue two weighted mechanisms, which is what the window would need.

Verification gate. Re-read the statement and proof of the row-local expansion lemma, the row-support exclusion with its switching parameters, the empty-aware reader interface (EH-profile), the quotient-rank conversion, and steps 2 to 5 of the two-level semantic map with its power-range corollary. Before drafting, a fresh-context reviewer checked the record and found no statement covering mixed inventories. It noted the heavy-round composition gap as a precedent, which concerns two switching arguments and does not apply here. No computation was run. A narrowly briefed fresh-context reviewer attacked the parameters, the replay degree, the type-(i) map on unconverted inputs, the reader interface after restriction, the compatibility with the weighted replay, and the type-(ii) rank after restriction. Its verdict: the proof holds with fixes, and no mathematical gap was found. Its required changes were all adopted: the row projection and lifting, explicit use of step 4 against the old graph ideal, separation through \(B\), the concrete inventory behind the weight, the order of conversion and rank checks, the dependence of "sufficiently large", and three scope and wording corrections.

The mixed exclusion extends to every sublinear row-remainder exponent with logarithmically many probes

22 September 2026 · Working proof (one combined replay of recorded maps) · Proposition MX′: \(\alpha<1\) with \(O(\log n)\) probes per line, nonlocal dimension \(n^\eta\), \(\eta<(1-\alpha)/8\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Proposition MX excluded refutations mixing row-support lines, with \(\alpha<1/5\), and lines of nonlocal dimension at most \(n^\eta\). Its next step asked whether the sublinear row-remainder exclusion, with a preliminary restriction and logarithmically many probes per line, combines with the weight in the same single replay. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The test is whether its probe interpolation is a coefficient substitution whose images the weighted replay accepts. It is: the recorded map (PL-map) substitutes \(r_i\mapsto\sum_u\chi_uR_{u,i}\) with exact identities.

Statement

Proposition MX′. Fix \(0\le\alpha<1\), \(0\le\eta<(1-\alpha)/8\), and constants \(c_0,K>0\). For all sufficiently large \(n\), ordinary unary \(\mathrm{PHP}^{n+1}_n\) and its functional variant have no standard syntactic \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_3})\) refutation with at most \(n^K\) lines in which every line satisfies at least one of:

  1. there are old affine probes \(U_1,\dots,U_t\), \(t\le c_0\log_3n\), depending on the line, such that every equation form \(L\) of the line satisfies \(L\equiv\ell+\sum_jb_jU_j\) modulo the row equations, with \(\ell\) supported on at most \(n^\alpha\operatorname{polylog}n\) rows (fixed logarithmic exponent);
  2. the line has nonlocal dimension at most \(n^\eta\).

With no probes and \(\alpha<1/5\), this is Proposition MX.

Proof

The proof is that of Proposition MX, with the type-(i) handling replaced by the sublinear-remainder route. Compilation, the graph, the weight, the projection and the single weighted replay through step 4 of the two-level semantic map are as there.

Parameters. Choose fixed \(\beta_1,\beta_2,\sigma\) with \[ \beta_1<1-\alpha,\qquad \beta_2<\tfrac14,\qquad 2\eta<\beta_1\beta_2\sigma,\qquad \sigma<1, \] possible because \(2\eta<(1-\alpha)/4\). Put \(n_1=\lceil n^{\beta_1}\rceil\) and \(N=\lceil n_1^{\beta_2}\rceil\). Fix integers \(m>C/(1-\alpha-\beta_1)\), with \(C\) the exponent of the support count below, and \(s>2(K+c_0)/(\beta_1(1-4\beta_2))\). "Sufficiently large" depends on \(\alpha,\eta,c_0,K\) and the fixed polylogarithmic exponent.

Order of operations. Compression of the type-(i) blocks; the first restriction \(\rho_1\); the probe interpolation on the \(n_1\)-board; row-local expansion of the branch inputs; the second restriction \(\rho_2\); the type-(ii) conversion on the final board; graph restriction and row projection \(\Psi\); and last, the substitution of the branch coefficients by reader polynomials and the weighted replay.

Compression and first restriction. Apply the sublinear-remainder proof's compression to type-(i) blocks only: each keeps a basis of actual selector positions, and the nonselected coefficients are set to zero as part of the substitution. Since the kept inputs are actual selectors, the probe representation is preserved, and the number of local support sets is at most \(n^C\) for a fixed \(C\). Without compression this count would fail, because a line may list unboundedly many equations. By (RT-tail) and the union bound, one uniform partial matching \(\rho_1\) leaving an \((n_1+1)\)-by-\(n_1\) board leaves fewer than \(m\) live rows in every local remainder \(\ell\) of every type-(i) input, since \(n^Cn^{-m(1-\alpha-\beta_1)+o(1)}=o(1)\). The representation (i) becomes a certified identity modulo the residual row equations, with the same number of probes. Type-(ii) blocks keep nonlocal dimension at most \(n^\eta\), as in MX.

Probe interpolation. For each type-(i) block, the log-probe map (PL-map) introduces, for each \(u\in\mathbb F_3^t\), a branch tuple \(q_{u,i}=1-(\ell_i+\sum_jb_{i,j}u_j)^2\) with formal coefficients \(R_{u,i}\), and sets \(\Phi(r_i)=\sum_u\chi_uR_{u,i}\), where \(\chi_u\) is the residue indicator of degree \(d=2t=O(\log n)\). The exact identities (PL-companion) and (PL-fields) express every original companion and field image as old-ideal terms plus \(\chi_u\) or \(\chi_u^3\) times branch companions or branch fields, through \(d+5\) and \(3d+3\). These are memberships in the ring that includes the formal \(R_{u,i}\). There are \(3^t\le n^{c_0}\) branches per block. A branch input that has become constant is handled per branch: coefficient zero for a zero selector, and the unit map (coefficient one on it, zero on the others) for a unit selector, whose branch companions then vanish exactly.

Second restriction and reader maps. Each nonconstant branch input reads fewer than \(m\) rows modulo rows. Row-local expansion gives \(q_{u,i}-G_{u,i}\in\mathcal I_C\) with \(C=\max(2,m-1)\), a constant. Apply the empty-aware switching estimate on the \((n_1+1)\)-by-\(n_1\) board, with local exponent zero and term width below \(m\), to the branch disjunctions only. There are at most \(n^K3^t\le n_1^{(K+c_0)/\beta_1}\) of them. By the choice of \(s\), a matching \(\rho_2\) leaving \((N+1)\)-by-\(N\) gives every branch a residual tree of height below \(s\), with probability \(1-o(1)\). Extend \(\rho_2\) to fix the formal \(R_{u,i}\). The identity \(\sum_u\chi_u=1\) is a polynomial identity, so it survives every ring map. The memberships \(E_{u,i}\in\mathcal I_{d+2}\), the witnesses for \(\chi_u^3-\chi_u\) and the expansion identities are old-ideal memberships. They are carried with their degrees by \(\rho_2\), which sends old axioms to old axioms or zero, by the graph restriction and by \(\Psi\), and projected proofs through degree two lift back. The reader interface on the final base gives old polynomials \(\beta_{u,i}\) of degree below \(s\), with every branch companion image in \(\mathcal I_{C+s+2}\) and every branch field image in \(\mathcal I_{3s}\), by MX's computation applied to the branch tuples.

Composite images. Substituting \(R_{u,i}\mapsto\beta_{u,i}\) last is a ring map fixing old generators. Each original type-(i) coefficient receives the old image \(\sum_u\chi_u\beta_{u,i}\), of degree at most \(d+s\). In (PL-companion) the term \(q_i\Delta\) becomes \(-q_i\sum_{u,j}\beta_{u,j}E_{u,j}\in\mathcal I_{d+s+4}\), the term \(\sum_uE_{u,i}P_u\) becomes a member of \(\mathcal I_{d+s+4}\), and \(\sum_u\chi_u(q_{u,i}P_u)\) becomes a member of \(\mathcal I_{d+C+s+2}\). By (PL-fields), field images lie in \(\mathcal I_{3d+3s}\).

Replay. The type-(ii) blocks are converted on the final residual board after both restrictions, as in MX. Restriction and projection do not increase the number of nonlinear basis positions, so the only rank check needed is \(n^{2\eta}\le N^\sigma\), which holds for large \(n\) by the choice \(2\eta<\beta_1\beta_2\sigma\). Over the projected graph base on the final board, multiply by the common weight of the type-(ii) blocks. The type-(ii) images are certified by step 4 of the semantic map, and the type-(i) images are weighted multiples of old-ideal members. With \(T=O(N^{1/2}\operatorname{polylog}N+N^\sigma\operatorname{polylog}N)\) for the type-(ii) map, the replay derives the weight through \[ B=\max(T,d+s)\cdot11+\max(d+C+s+2,\ 3d+3s)+k=o(N), \] since \(\sigma<1\) and \(d=O(\log n)=O(\log N)\). This contradicts separation. \(\square\)

Scope

  • MX′ recovers the \(\mathbb F_3\) Res(Lin) consequence of the sublinear-remainder exclusion (only type-(i) lines), not that theorem's polylogarithmic-degree PC statement over every prime. It extends Proposition MX from \(\alpha<1/5\) to \(\alpha<1\), with probes. Type (ii) keeps MX's reduced range \(\eta<(1-\alpha)/8\), not Corollary ND's \(\eta<1/2\), and it shrinks as \(\alpha\) grows.
  • The occupancy class is still not included, and one line may not mix the two alternatives among its forms.
  • The window is untouched: a line with many independent nonlocal forms spread over most rows lies in neither alternative.

Assessment and next step

The combined replay absorbs the probe interpolation, because that interpolation is a coefficient substitution with exact identities, at the price of a second restriction that shrinks the board to \(n^{\beta_1\beta_2}\). Over \(\mathbb F_3\), and in the reduced range \(\eta<(1-\alpha)/8\), the recorded proof-system classes other than occupancy now glue across lines. Next step (odd-prime-clause-transfer): mixing within a line. A line whose forms split into a type-(i) part and a low-nonlocal part gives one block whose inputs are of both kinds. Test whether a block-splitting identity separates such a block into a probe-and-remainder part and a quotient-rank part at a controlled degree. Test it first on the smallest mixed block, one row-remainder input and one dense input.

Sheaf check

Lines mixing remainder forms and low-nonlocal forms are still excluded: the block product splits

22 September 2026 · Working proof (product split in one weighted replay) · Proposition MX″: each line's equations split into a probe-and-remainder part and a part of nonlocal dimension \(n^\eta\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Proposition MX′ lets different lines satisfy different alternatives. Its next step asked for mixing within one line, where one block has inputs of both kinds and a single product \(P\). Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The obstruction named there is that both parts share \(P\), so the two coefficient maps cannot be chosen independently. The idea tested here is to scale one part's coefficients by the other part's product image, so that \(P\) factors. This is the device of the packed product (LPF-value) in the two-level semantic map, whose first row carries the affine-core product times a bin product.

Statement

Proposition MX″. Fix \(0\le\alpha<1\), \(0\le\eta<(1-\alpha)/8\), and constants \(c_0,K>0\). For all sufficiently large \(n\), ordinary unary \(\mathrm{PHP}^{n+1}_n\) and its functional variant have no standard syntactic \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_3})\) refutation with at most \(n^K\) lines in which the equations of every line split into two sets \(\mathcal A\) and \(\mathcal B\) such that:

  1. for some old affine probes \(U_1,\dots,U_t\), \(t\le c_0\log_3n\), depending on the line, every form in \(\mathcal A\) is, modulo the row equations, a combination of the probes plus a remainder on at most \(n^\alpha\operatorname{polylog}n\) rows (fixed logarithmic exponent);
  2. the subtuple \(\mathcal B\) has nonlocal dimension at most \(n^\eta\), as defined in Corollary ND: its equations whose forms are not row- or column-local have linear parts spanning dimension at most \(n^\eta\).

Taking \(\mathcal A\) or \(\mathcal B\) empty in every line gives Proposition MX′.

The product split

Consider one complete accuracy-one block with inputs \(q_i\), \(i\in\mathcal A\), and \(q_j\), \(j\in\mathcal B\), coefficients \(r\), and \[ P=1-\sum_{i\in\mathcal A}r_iq_i-\sum_{j\in\mathcal B}r_jq_j . \] Let \(\Theta\) map the \(\mathcal B\)-coefficients to their images under MX′'s type-(ii) map applied to the subtuple \(\mathcal B\) alone. Write \(P_{\mathcal B}\) for the resulting image of \(1-\sum_{\mathcal B}r_jq_j\). The two-level parent is the \(\mathcal B\)-subtuple alone, as a complete accuracy-one block, so one row carries all its nonlinear factors and \(P_{\mathcal B}\) is the full packed product (LPF-value) up to the conversion error below. The weight \(f\) is built from the affine cores of the \(\mathcal B\)-subtuples only; \(\mathcal A\)-inputs never enter a parent. The quotient-rank conversion, its error \(E\) with \(\varphi(1-\sum_{\mathcal B}r_jq_j)=P_f+E\), and the new bottom blocks of the rank-one representation depend only on \(\mathcal B\)-data: the pull-back is linear in the \(\mathcal B\)-coefficients, and bottom companions vanish on the whole cube independently of the parent. Let \(\gamma_i\) be the images of the \(\mathcal A\)-coefficients under MX′'s type-(i) composite map applied to the subtuple \(\mathcal A\) alone, and \(P_{\mathcal A}=1-\sum_{\mathcal A}\gamma_iq_i\). Define \[ \Theta(r_i)=P_{\mathcal B}\,\gamma_i\quad(i\in\mathcal A). \] Then, exactly, \[ \Theta(P)=P_{\mathcal B}-P_{\mathcal B}\sum_{i\in\mathcal A}\gamma_iq_i=P_{\mathcal B}\,P_{\mathcal A}. \tag{SPLIT} \] Now the axiom images, all under the final restrictions, graph restriction and projection, are as follows.

  • \(\mathcal B\)-companions. \(q_j\Theta(P)=(q_jP_{\mathcal B})P_{\mathcal A}\). In MX′, \(f\,q_jP_{\mathcal B}\) equals a polynomial vanishing on the whole Boolean cube (the step-4 packed image, by the pointwise argument of that step) plus an old-ideal member carrying the conversion error \(E\) and the replacement of \(q_j\) by its converted input modulo the row equations. Multiplying both by \(P_{\mathcal A}\) keeps the first vanishing on the cube, certified by Boolean division, and the second in the old ideal. The degree is MX′'s \(\mathcal B\)-certificate degree, including \(E\), plus \(\deg P_{\mathcal A}\le d+s+2\).
  • \(\mathcal A\)-companions. \(q_i\Theta(P)=P_{\mathcal B}\,(q_iP_{\mathcal A})\). MX′ certifies \(q_iP_{\mathcal A}\) in the old ideal through \(D_{\mathcal A}=\max(d+C+s+2,\,d+s+4)\). Multiplying by \(P_{\mathcal B}\) and \(f\) keeps it in the old ideal, through \(D_{\mathcal A}+\deg P_{\mathcal B}+k\).
  • \(\mathcal B\)-fields are unchanged from MX′.
  • \(\mathcal A\)-fields. \(P_{\mathcal B}\gamma_i\) is an \(\mathbb F_3\)-polynomial in Boolean old variables, so \((P_{\mathcal B}\gamma_i)^3-P_{\mathcal B}\gamma_i\) vanishes on the whole cube pointwise. Boolean division certifies it through \(3(T+1+d+s)\), with no weight needed.

Here \(\deg P_{\mathcal B}\le T+1\) and \(\deg\gamma_i\le d+s\), in the notation of MX′.

Proof of MX″

Run the proof of MX′ with each block's inputs divided into its \(\mathcal A\)- and \(\mathcal B\)-subtuples. The compression basis for type (i) is chosen inside the \(\mathcal A\)-subtuple, so nonselected \(\mathcal A\)-inputs are combinations of selected ones and their companions are combinations of certified \(\mathcal A\)-companions. The unit-selector branch map acts within \(P_{\mathcal A}\) only. An equation whose form fits both parts is assigned to one of them, and the split is a fixed partition of the line's equations, so no input is counted twice. The first restriction, the probe interpolation, the second restriction and the reader maps act on the \(\mathcal A\)-subtuples. The switching union bound counts at most \(n^K3^t\) branch disjunctions, as before. The type-(ii) rank check, conversion and weight act on the \(\mathcal B\)-subtuples, whose inventory is again at most \(n^K\) blocks. Restriction does not increase the nonlocal dimension of a \(\mathcal B\)-subtuple and keeps local forms local. The two subtuple maps are the ones MX′ uses. The quotient-rank conversion of a \(\mathcal B\)-subtuple is the linear pull-back on the \(\mathcal B\)-coefficients only, and its product identity holds for the partial product \(1-\sum_{\mathcal B}r_jq_j\), since it is linear in those coefficients. Combine them by (SPLIT). Every coefficient image has degree at most \(T+1+d+s\). Every weighted axiom image is certified as above. The replay derives the weight through \(B\) at most the maximum of: \(11(T+1+d+s)+k\) for the replayed lines; \(D_{\mathcal A}+T+1+k\) for \(\mathcal A\)-companions; MX′'s \(\mathcal B\)-certificate degree plus \(d+s+2\) for \(\mathcal B\)-companions; and \(3(T+1+d+s)\) for \(\mathcal A\)-fields. Each is \(o(N)\), with \(T=O(N^{1/2}\operatorname{polylog}N+N^\sigma\operatorname{polylog}N)\) and \(d=O(\log N)\). This contradicts separation. \(\square\)

Scope

  • MX″ contains MX and MX′. In each line, forms may be of three kinds: probe-and-remainder forms (remainders on \(n^\alpha\operatorname{polylog}n\) rows, \(\alpha<1\) fixed, plus \(O(\log n)\) shared probes), row- and column-local forms (free), and at most \(n^\eta\) further independent nonlocal directions, with \(\eta<(1-\alpha)/8\). It is incomparable with Corollary ND, which allows \(\eta<1/2\) without remainders, and with the occupancy class.
  • The occupancy class is still not included.
  • The window is untouched: a line needing many independent directions spread over most rows, beyond logarithmically many probes, satisfies neither part.

Assessment and next step

Within-line mixing of the two kinds costs only an additive degree, because the block product splits exactly under a scaled substitution. The limits of the combined class are the occupancy class, which is not included; the reduced range \(\eta<(1-\alpha)/8\) instead of Corollary ND's \(1/2\); and the restriction to \(\mathbb F_3\). Splitting does not reach the window. Every \(\mathcal B\)-part carries its own affine-core product, of degree at least about \(N^{1/2}\operatorname{polylog}N\), and a part of quotient rank near \(N^\sigma\) costs \(N^\sigma\operatorname{polylog}N\). So only \(o(N^{1/2})\) parts fit the budget, with total nonlocal rank far below the \(\Theta(N)\) of a random dense window block. Only a two-part split is proved in any case. Next step (odd-prime-clause-transfer): test whether the occupancy class's column freezing on the weak base is compatible with the weighted replay. That is the last recorded class outside the combined statement. If it is not, or once it is done, the thread's remaining work is the window, for which no mechanism is named, and a route review should decide whether to pause the thread.

Sheaf check

(SPLIT) is a gluing of two local sections inside one block: the product image is the product of the two parts' images, and each part's axioms are certified by its own mechanism. It is the gluing rule with a vanishing statement that the loop asked for, but it is multiplicative. Each weighted part adds at least about \(N^{1/2}\) to the degree, so at most \(o(N^{1/2})\) parts glue within the linear budget. That is far from the \(\Theta(N)\) independent directions of a window block.

Verification gate. Re-read Proposition MX′ with its review, (LPF-value) and step 4 of the two-level semantic map, the quotient-rank conversion's product identity, and the log-probe identities. Ran tools/search-claims.py on block splitting, product factorization and scaled coefficients. Its top hits were the fresh-block degree lemma, the costed-partition semantic map and the two-level semantic map. The nearest recorded device is the latter's packed product, cited. No computation was run. A narrowly briefed fresh-context reviewer checked (SPLIT) and the four certifications. Its verdict: the proof holds with fixes, with no gap in MX″. It corrected the \(\mathcal B\)-companion justification, which must carry the conversion error \(E\), and simplified the \(\mathcal A\)-fields to direct Boolean division. It required the parent to be the \(\mathcal B\)-subtuple alone, compression inside \(\mathcal A\), the defined notion of nonlocal dimension and explicit degrees. It also replaced the overclaims in scope, assessment and next step with the per-part cost count, which shows that splitting cannot reach the window. All changes were adopted.

The occupancy class does not join the combined exclusion by composition: column freezing spreads the distinguished row

22 September 2026 · Negative test with an explicit line · The global freezing map sends row-local forms on the distinguished row to column-sum forms of rank about \(N\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Proposition MX″ combined the remainder and nonlocal-dimension classes. Its next step asked whether the occupancy class, the last recorded class outside it, is compatible with the single weighted replay. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The occupancy proof applies the recorded column-freezing map globally, before anything else. So composition requires that this map keep every MX″ line inside MX″'s hypotheses.

The map

At \(p=3\) the map takes \(K=2\). It makes a small matching prefix, relabels the remaining rows as two copies of \(N+1\) residual rows plus one distinguished row \(*\), and relabels the columns as two empty columns and two copies of \(N\) residual columns, with \(N=\lfloor n/2\rfloor-1\). A copied cell maps to the residual cell \(y_{ij}\). A cell of the distinguished row in residual column \(j\) of either copy maps to \(q_j=1-\sum_iy_{ij}\). Empty columns and off-copy cells map to zero. It is one global affine map on old variables, valid on the weak base.

A line that leaves the combined class

Let \(x_{*,j}\) denote the cell of the distinguished row in residual column \(j\) of the first copy. Consider a line containing the equations \(x_{*,1}+x_{*,j}=0\), for \(j=2,\dots,N\). Before the map, each form is row-local, supported in the single row \(*\). The line satisfies both alternatives of MX″: its remainders read one row, and its nonlocal dimension is zero. After the map the forms become \[ q_1+q_j=2-\sigma'_1-\sigma'_j,\qquad \sigma'_j=\sum_iy_{ij}. \]

  • They are nonlocal. Modulo residual row equations, row \(i\) of the linear part is \(e_1+e_j+c_i\mathbf 1\). It is never zero, so the form is not row-local. For \(N\ge4\) it is not supported in one column unless \(c_i=0\) for all \(i\), and then its support is two columns. So the form is not column-local either.
  • Their nonlocal dimension is at least \(N-2\). Modulo rows, \(\sum_j\sigma'_j\) is constant, so the \(\sigma'_j\) span a space of dimension \(N-1\). The forms \(\sigma'_1+\sigma'_j\) for \(j\ge2\) span a subspace of codimension at most one.
  • They violate alternative (a). Differences \(\sigma'_j-\sigma'_k\) of two such forms would have to lie in the span of \(O(\log n)\) probes plus forms on about \(2n^\alpha\) rows. Restricted to the rows outside those remainders, the differences span dimension about \(N-2\), which \(O(\log n)\) probes cannot contain.

So one line of MX″'s class maps outside both alternatives. Composition through the global freezing map fails.

The distinguished row can be chosen, but only once for the whole refutation. A refutation may contain lines like this for every row, so no choice avoids them. The occupancy exclusion may still combine with the others by an argument that does not freeze globally, but none is recorded or proposed here.

Assessment and next step

Gluing the recorded classes has reached its natural end: the remainder and nonlocal classes glue, within lines and across them, and the occupancy class stays separate because its mechanism changes coordinates globally. Next step (odd-prime-clause-transfer): hold the route review planned in MX″. The window has no named mechanism, splitting cannot reach it, and the partial endpoints are now consolidated. The review should decide whether to pause the thread, and name what a restart would need.

Sheaf check

This is a failure of restriction compatibility. The freezing map is not a morphism of the site on which the other mechanisms glue, since it does not send local forms to local forms. The occupancy section therefore lives on a different site. Gluing across sites would need a common refinement, and none is available.

The example was checked against those definitions in the text. No computation was run. No reviewer was used, since the entry states only a negative example whose checks are elementary.

Route review: pause the ternary window; extend the partial endpoints to every odd prime

22 September 2026 · Route review of odd-prime-clause-transfer · Pauses window work until a restart condition holds; next: all-prime form of Corollary ND. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

The line's general claim. Every polynomial inventory of complete accuracy-one ternary selector blocks can be excluded at compiler degree \(11\) by the recorded route: compilation, restriction and one common weight. What the goal needs is this claim in full, and then its analogue for every odd prime. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer, since the window is its only open part at \(p=3\).

Evidence since the thread review

  • The partial endpoints were consolidated and glued: Corollary ND and Propositions MX, MX′ and MX″. Each passed a fresh-context review.
  • The occupancy class does not join them by composition.
  • No step touched the window.

Falsification attempt: can gluing reach the window?

This is the last live idea from the recent cycles, so it was tested by a count. Split a window block of nonlocal rank \(h\ge N/(4.4\times10^7)\) into parts handled by the weight, glued by the product split (SPLIT). A part of quotient rank at most \(N^\sigma\) has nonlocal dimension about \(N^{\sigma/2}\), because quotient rank is quadratic in nonlocal dimension. So about \(h/N^{\sigma/2}\) parts are needed. Each part adds at least the affine-core cost of about \(N^{1/2}\) to the degree of the product image, since the product is multiplied part by part. The total is at least about \(hN^{(1-\sigma)/2}\ge hN^{1/4}\) for \(\sigma\le1/2\), and at least \(hN^{\sigma/2}\) for larger \(\sigma\). Both far exceed the linear budget \(N/10^6\). Only two-part splits are proved in any case. Gluing cannot reach the window at these costs.

Every other tested line is recorded as negative or heuristic-negative in the thread review: weights, alignment, sign variables, mixtures, complexes and sheaves, closure and derivation structure.

Assessment of this line

The recorded route has reached the limit of its mechanisms at \(p=3\). Its partial results are consolidated and reviewed. The window's prospects by recorded methods are weak, as the thread review already found. Further cycles on the window without a new mechanism would repeat reformulations, which the workspace rules count against a line. The decision is to pause window work.

Restart conditions

Window work should restart only if one of these holds:

  1. a proposed mechanism excludes a single random dense ternary block of nonlocal rank \(\Theta(N)\), jointly with the recorded weight, at degree \(o(N)\) on the separated graph (this is the decisive calibration: no recorded mechanism does it);
  2. a proof, or a usable published bound, for the semi-regular or general-position behaviour of Boolean quadratic selector systems modulo PHP, which would turn the window review's heuristic verdict into a theorem and so tell which way to go;
  3. external progress on DAG-like \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) lower bounds for PHP-type principles that supplies a mechanism for the sign ambiguity \(L\in\{1,2\}\).

Next step

Redirect to route item scope-and-review, "establish every fixed odd prime", for the partial endpoints. Corollary ND is stated only for \(p=3\), because the affine classification and the quotient-rank conversion are ternary. For \(p\ge5\), the selector \(1-L^{p-1}\) of a nonlocal form lies in the degree-\((p-1)\) span of its nonlocal directions, of dimension about \(r^{p-1}/(p-1)!\). The all-prime power-range corollary then suggests nonlocal dimension \(n^{1/(p-1)-\varepsilon}\). Check first which steps are ternary-specific: the classification of forms whose selector has an affine representative, and the certified quotient conversion in degree \(p-1\). The row-local expansion and column reduction already work over every prime, which suggests that local forms are again free.

Sheaf check

The loop's question has a definite answer for this thread. The one gluing with a good property found here, the product split across and within lines, is multiplicative in degree. Every weighted part costs at least \(N^{1/2}\), so it glues boundedly many rank-limited pieces and not the \(\Theta(N)\) independent directions of a window block. A sheaf that could reach the window would need additive gluing costs for weighted pieces, which none of the recorded weight mechanisms has.
