Every odd prime: quotient-rank exclusion in degree \(p-1\) and Res(Lin) lines of nonlocal dimension \(n^{1/(p-1)-\varepsilon}\)

22 September 2026 · Working proof · Extends the quotient-rank exclusion and Corollary ND to every odd prime. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. The pause review redirected effort to route item scope-and-review, "establish every fixed odd prime", for the partial endpoints. Corollary ND is stated for \(p=3\) only. Its two ternary steps are the affine classification of local selectors and the quotient conversion in degree two. This entry checks each step for general odd \(p\).

Statements

Fix an odd prime \(p\) and put \(\delta=p-1\). On the full functional linear-row base of the \((n+1)\)-by-\(n\) board, let \(I_\delta\) be the degree-\(\delta\) consequence space and \(Q_\delta=\mathcal P_{\le\delta}/I_\delta\). For a complete accuracy-one selector block \(a\), let \(V_a\) be the span of its selectors \(q=1-L^{\delta}\) in \(Q_\delta\), let \(A_a=V_a\cap\overline{\mathcal P_{\le1}}\), and let \(r_a=\dim(V_a/A_a)\). The board parameter is \(N=n\).

Theorem QRp. Fix a polynomial block inventory, a polylogarithmic PC degree bound \(D\), and \(0\le\sigma<1\). If every \(r_a\le N^\sigma\operatorname{polylog}N\), with a fixed logarithmic exponent, then for sufficiently large \(N\) the complete accuracy-one selector source over the full functional base has no ordinary PC refutation through \(D\). All companions and coefficient fields are included. Internally the replay ceiling is \(\max(D,2p+1)\), still polylogarithmic.

Corollary NDp. Fix \(0<\varepsilon\le1/\delta\) and \(K>0\). For all sufficiently large \(n\), ordinary unary \(\mathrm{PHP}^{n+1}_n\) and its functional variant have no standard syntactic \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) refutation with at most \(n^K\) lines in which every line has nonlocal dimension at most \(n^{1/\delta-\varepsilon}\). Nonlocal dimension is as in Corollary ND: the dimension of the span of the linear parts of the line's equations whose forms are not row- or column-local modulo the row equations. At \(p=3\) this is Corollary ND.

Proof of Theorem QRp

The proof of the ternary quotient-rank theorem is written with degree two in three places, and each generalizes to degree \(\delta\).

  1. Basis conversion. Choose affine representatives for a basis of \(A_a\) and extend by \(r_a\) actual selector positions to a basis \(f_j\) of \(V_a\). There are constant matrices with \(q_i=\sum_j\alpha_{ij}f_j+u_i\) and \(f_j=\sum_i\beta_{ji}q_i+v_j\), where \(u_i,v_j\in I_\delta\). Map \(r_i=\sum_j\beta_{ji}t_j\) for a new complete block on the \(f_j\) with product \(P_f\). Then \(\varphi(P_q)=P_f+E\) with \(E=\sum_jt_jv_j\in I_{\delta+1}\), and \[ q_i\varphi(P_q)=\sum_j\alpha_{ij}f_jP_f+u_iP_f+q_iE . \] Scalar blocks are cleaned first, as in the ternary proof. Here \(\deg P_f\le\delta+1\). The first term is a combination of new companions \(f_jP_f\) of degree \(2\delta+1\). The second term is certified through \(2\delta+1\), since \(u_i\in I_\delta\). The third is too, since \(v_j\in I_\delta\) makes \(E=\sum_jt_jv_j\) certified through \(\delta+1\). This equals the original companion degree \(\delta+(\delta+1)=2p-1\), so source refutations transfer without degree increase. Coefficient fields map by Frobenius: \((\sum_j\beta_{ji}t_j)^p-\sum_j\beta_{ji}t_j=\sum_j\beta_{ji}(t_j^p-t_j)\), because \(\beta\in\mathbb F_p\).
  2. Rank-one representation. Replace the \(r_a\) selected selector positions by products of fresh rank-one affine bottoms, using the rank-one selector bridge, which holds for every odd \(p\). The bridge is stated for parents whose inputs are all selectors. Here parents mix affine basis inputs \(F\) with selected selectors, so the accounting is as follows. The product difference \(A-Q=\sum_is_i(P_i-t_i)\) is certified through \(p+2\). An affine-input companion satisfies \(FA=FQ+F(A-Q)\), through \(p+3\). A selector companion satisfies (RS-parent), through \(2p+1\). The replay ceiling becomes \(\max(D,2p+1)\); at \(p=3\) this reproduces the ternary five, six and seven. Parents then read old affine forms and at most \(r_a\) whole bottom products.
  3. Endpoint. Choose a robust graph and row projection from the power-range corollary, which is stated for every fixed prime with polynomial inventory. (Its proof uses \(\delta\) for a different quantity, not \(p-1\).) The transfer gives at most \(\binom{v+p-1}{p-1}\) inputs per block, and conversion does not increase this. Restriction and projection do not increase the number of nonlinear basis positions, so the parent's nonlinear function-space rank on the restricted cube satisfies \(c_a\le r_a\le N^\sigma\operatorname{polylog}N\), and the bottom ranks are at most one (\(\rho=0\)). Since \(0+\sigma<1\), the corollary excludes the refutation. \(\square\)

Proof of Corollary NDp

Compile with the complete-board transfer at degree \(4p-1\ge2p+1\), obtaining at most \(n^K\) blocks. As in Corollary ND, by the selector compiler, a block's inputs are a compression-chosen basis subset of the selectors of one line, and resolution adds no premise selectors as inputs. So \(V_a\) lies in that line's selector span. Initial clauses have only local forms. Fix a block with nonlocal dimension \(r\le n^{1/\delta-\varepsilon}\).

  • Local forms have affine classes in \(Q_\delta\). A row-local \(L\) has a representative \(L'\) on one row. The row-local expansion with \(t=1\), valid over every prime, gives \(q-G\in I_{\max(\delta,1)}=I_\delta\), where \(G\) is a sum of cells of that row, which is affine. A column-local \(L\) has a representative \(L'\) supported in one column. Then \(L^\delta-L'^\delta=(L-L')\sum_aL^aL'^{\delta-1-a}\), with \(L-L'\) a constant combination of row axioms, which costs degree \(\delta\). The degree-complete column reduction (WC-affine), valid over every prime, gives an affine \(F\) with \(1-L'^\delta-F\in I_\delta(\mathrm{BOOL}+\text{column collisions})\). This weak space lies in \(I_\delta\) of the full functional base, which contains both generator sets. So \(q-F\in I_\delta\).
  • Nonlocal forms contribute a bounded span. Write \(L=\ell+c\) with \(\ell\) in the span \(U\) of the nonlocal linear parts, \(\dim U=r\). Then \(1-L^\delta=1-\sum_{k=0}^{\delta}\binom\delta kc^{\delta-k}\ell^k\). Modulo affine polynomials this is a combination of \(\ell^2,\dots,\ell^\delta\), each in the span of the monomials of degree \(k\) in a basis of \(U\).

Since \(V_a/A_a\) embeds in \(Q_\delta/\overline{\mathcal P_{\le1}}\), \[ r_a\le\sum_{k=2}^{\delta}\binom{r+k-1}{k}\le\binom{r+\delta}{\delta}\le(r+\delta)^{\delta}. \] For \(\delta\le r\le n^{1/\delta-\varepsilon}\) this gives \(r_a\le(2r)^\delta\le2^\delta n^{1-\delta\varepsilon}\), and for \(r<\delta\) it gives \(r_a=O_p(1)\). So Theorem QRp applies with \(\sigma=1-\delta\varepsilon<1\), the constant being absorbed. Both variants of PHP compile to the full functional base, as in Corollary ND. \(\square\)

Scope

  • Theorem QRp and Corollary NDp extend Corollary ND and the ternary quotient-rank theorem from \(p=3\) to every fixed odd prime. The exponent \(1/(p-1)\) comes from the degree-\(\delta\) span of powers of \(\delta\)-th degree in the nonlocal directions.
  • The mixed Propositions MX to MX″ are still stated only at \(p=3\). Their other ingredients (switching, reader maps, log-probe interpolation) are recorded for every prime, but an all-prime MX″ is open, and its rank parameter must be rechecked.
  • For \(p\ge5\) the ternary graph criterion's dense side has no analogue in the record, as before.

Assessment and next step

The ternary-specific steps of Corollary ND were only its degree-two notation: the local classification needs only sufficiency, which the all-prime expansion and column reduction supply, and the quotient conversion carries over to degree \(p-1\) with one new piece of accounting, for mixed parents in the rank-one step. Next step (scope-and-review): transcribe Proposition MX″ to every odd prime, checking the one parameter that changes, the type-(ii) rank bound \(n^{\delta\eta}\le N^\sigma\), and whether any MX step used \(p=3\) beyond notation.

Every odd prime: lines mixing remainder forms and low-nonlocal forms are excluded

22 September 2026 · Working proof · Transcribes Proposition MX″ to every odd prime, with nonlocal exponent \(\eta<(1-\alpha)/(4(p-1))\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Proposition MX″ is stated for \(p=3\). Its nonlocal part now has an all-prime form, Theorem QRp. Route item: scope-and-review. This entry checks every step of MX, MX′ and MX″ for uses of \(p=3\) beyond notation, and recomputes the one parameter that changes.

Statement

Proposition MXp. Fix an odd prime \(p\), \(\delta=p-1\), \(0\le\alpha<1\), \(0\le\eta<(1-\alpha)/(4\delta)\), and constants \(c_0,K>0\). For all sufficiently large \(n\), ordinary unary \(\mathrm{PHP}^{n+1}_n\) and its functional variant have no standard syntactic \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) refutation with at most \(n^K\) lines in which the equations of every line are partitioned into two fixed sets \(\mathcal A\) and \(\mathcal B\) such that: (a) for some old affine probes \(U_1,\dots,U_t\), \(t\le c_0\log_pn\), depending on the line, every form in \(\mathcal A\) is, modulo the row equations, a combination of the probes plus a remainder on at most \(n^\alpha\operatorname{polylog}n\) rows, with a fixed logarithmic exponent; and (b) \(\mathcal B\) has nonlocal dimension at most \(n^\eta\). At \(p=3\) this is MX″.

The changed parameter

Choose \(\beta_1<1-\alpha\), \(\beta_2<1/4\) and \(\sigma<1\) with \(\delta\eta<\beta_1\beta_2\sigma\), which is possible because \(\delta\eta<(1-\alpha)/4\). Put \(N=n^{\beta_1\beta_2}\). Here \(r_a\) is the rank in \(Q_\delta\) over the full functional base of the final \((N+1)\)-by-\(N\) board, as Theorem QRp defines it. Restriction keeps local forms local or constant, and a \(\mathcal B\)-subtuple of nonlocal dimension \(r\le n^\eta\) keeps it after both restrictions. By the rank count of Corollary NDp, \(r_a\le(2r)^\delta\le2^\delta n^{\delta\eta}\le N^\sigma\) for large \(n\), when \(r\ge\delta\), and \(r_a=O_p(1)\) otherwise. The switching exponent condition \(\beta_2<1/4\) at local exponent zero, the choice of \(m\) and \(s\), and the replay bound \[ B\le\max\bigl(D(T+1+d+s)+k,\ D_{\mathcal A}+T+1+k,\ D_{\mathcal B}+d+s+\delta,\ p(T+1+d+s)\bigr)=o(N) \] are unchanged in form. The leading factor \(D=4p-1\) is the ternary \(11\). The constants depend on \(p\). \(\square\)

Scope and next step

MXp is the all-prime form of MX″. At \(p=3\) it has the same range, and in general \(\eta<(1-\alpha)/(4(p-1))\). It recovers the \(\mathbb F_p\) Res(Lin) consequence of the sublinear-remainder exclusion, and contains Corollary NDp's case of remainder-free lines only in this reduced range. The occupancy class and the window are as before. The ternary graph criterion's dense side still has no \(p\ge5\) analogue. The additive gluing exists at Nullstellensatz level; its polynomial-calculus form is fresh-block conservativity, stated here for \(\mathbb F_3\)

22 September 2026 · Formulation and conjecture · Zero-cost PC gluing would follow from ternary conservativity over the PHP base. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. The user overrode the pause. The next step asked to formulate the mixed-moment system of historical Lemma 6.6 as a gluing complex over block subsets. The target was a vanishing statement at additive degree cost, which the product split lacks. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. Missing implication: a gluing of per-block exclusions whose degree cost does not grow with the number of blocks.

The complex, for the compiled source

Take the compiled source at \(p\): blocks \(b\) with selectors \(g_{b,i}=1-L_{b,i}^{\delta}\), \(\delta=p-1\), fresh coefficients \(r_{b,i}\) with fields \(r^p=r\), products \(P_b=1-\sum_ir_{b,i}g_{b,i}\), and companion degree \(e=2\delta+1\). The axioms are the old axioms (Boolean equations and the linear-row PHP base), the fields and the companions \(g_{b,i}P_b\). The product \(P_b\) is not an axiom, as in the compiler. A linear functional \(\Lambda\) on the joint polynomials of degree at most \(D\) splits into components \(\mu_\alpha(q)=\Lambda(qr^\alpha)\) on old polynomials of degree at most \(D-|\alpha|\). Here \(\alpha\) ranges over reduced fresh monomials, with exponents at most \(\delta\). \(\Lambda\) annihilates the degree-\(D\) ideal of the augmented system exactly when:

  • each \(\mu_\alpha\) annihilates the old ideal (Boolean plus PHP) through \(D-|\alpha|\);
  • for every block \(b\), input \(i\), reduced monomial \(\beta\) and old \(q\) with \(\deg q+|\beta|\le D-e\), \[ \mu_\beta(qg_{b,i})=\sum_j\mu_{\beta\oplus e_{b,j}}(qg_{b,i}g_{b,j}), \] where \(\oplus\) adds an exponent and reduces \(r^p\) to \(r\).

Grading by the support \(S(\alpha)\) of blocks gives a Čech-type complex. An equation with \(b\notin S(\beta)\) links support \(S\) to \(S\cup\{b\}\). One with \(b\in S(\beta)\) is a revisit inside \(S\). It is exactly the dual of the augmented degree-\(D\) NS space in fresh-monomial coordinates. Historical Lemma 6.6, parametrized by selected inputs through \(T_{S,J}\), is a sufficient specialization of it. At \(D=4p-1\) and \(e=2p-1\), the equations link supports of up to \(2p+1\) blocks, not two.

The recorded additive gluing, and why randomness helps it

In the historical first mixed band, the exact pair duality (PAIR-dual) shows that pair components exist whenever \(W_a\cap W_b=0\) for the product spaces \(W_b=\operatorname{span}\{[qg_{b,i}g_{b,j}]\}\). It gives a design at the same degree, with no family-count factor. For one pair in that band, the gluing costs nothing. The analogous product spaces here are \(W_b(\beta)\), spanned by the classes of \(qg_{b,i}g_{b,j}\) with \(\deg q\le D-e-|\beta|\), inside the old quotient of degree \(D-|\beta|-1\). For a window block of \(h\le cN\) inputs on \(s=15(N+1)\) coordinates: \[ \dim W_b(\beta)\le h^2\binom{s+D-e-|\beta|}{D-e-|\beta|}, \] which is smaller, by a factor of about \(h^2m^{2\delta}/s^{2\delta}\) with \(m=D-|\beta|-1\), than \(\binom sm\), an upper bound for the quotient. So, heuristically, two independent random window blocks have separated product spaces, by the same general-position reasoning that the window review used against weights. Here randomness helps. The spaces are structured, not random, so this is a heuristic. Pairwise separation settles only the pair case. The deeper complex needs higher-order conditions: each \(W_b\) against the sum of the others, and the revisit equations. Separation fails for blocks that share inputs, which actual inventories have. That is the structured form of the historical Example 6.5, whose two blocks have the same constant input.

The obstruction: this is Nullstellensatz, and the target is PC

A design in the historical sense (foundations) annihilates the degree-\(D\) NS space. The recorded pair transfer says explicitly that it asserts nothing for PC. The compiler produces PC refutations through \(4p-1\). By the standard simulation, PC replays as NS only with degree growing with the derivation's depth. So at fixed \(D\), an NS exclusion reaches only refutations of bounded depth. The PC form needs the closure: a normalized functional annihilating \(\mathcal C_D\), built degree by degree through the fall spaces \(O_d\) of the closed moment tower.

The PC form of zero-cost gluing is conservativity

The record already states the PC-level property, over \(\mathbb F_2\): conj:level-one-fresh-block-conservativity. It says a fresh accuracy-one affine block adds no degree-\(D\) consequence in the existing variables, over Boolean equations plus earlier complete accuracy-one affine blocks. It is open, with about twenty exact checks. Applied block by block over its own base, it would glue any number of blocks at zero cost. That base does not contain PHP. The recorded proved costs are additive: M blocks cost \(M\max(\delta,k)\) (obs:few-fresh-blocks-conservative-over-unary-PHP), or about \((M+1)D\) (thm:fresh-block-conservativity-loss-bound). They fail once \(M\) is about \(N/2\), and the thick inventory has polynomially many blocks. The recorded binary refutation of a stronger form, ex:same-degree-interface-preservation-refuted, needs a second-level base block. Selector blocks are one level over the old variables, so it does not apply here.

Over a Boolean base alone, conservativity is trivial. A complete block is satisfiable at every old point, so every sound old consequence vanishes on the whole cube and lies in the Boolean ideal at its degree. The content lies in the existing fresh variables of earlier blocks, where the base is not degree-exact.

Conjecture C3. Over \(\mathbb F_3\), let a base consist of an old system \(\mathcal F\) together with complete accuracy-one selector blocks. Complete means all companions and fields are present. The inputs are \(1-L^2\) with \(L\) affine, and the axioms are companions and fields only. Let a fresh complete block have forms whose linear parts are linearly independent. Let the existing variables be the old variables and the coefficients of the base blocks, excluding the fresh block's. Then, for every \(D\ge5\), with degree measured jointly, \[ \mathcal C_D(\text{base}+\text{block})\cap\mathbb F_3[\text{existing}]=\mathcal C_D(\text{base})\cap\mathbb F_3[\text{existing}]. \] The two cases are \(\mathcal F\) Boolean (C3-B) and \(\mathcal F\) the functional linear-row PHP base (C3-PHP).

If C3-PHP held, adding the compiled blocks one at a time would keep the old part of the closure equal to \(\mathcal C_{11}(\text{PHP})\cap\mathbb F_3[\text{old}]\). By the all-field old matching barrier, that space does not contain \(1\) for large \(n\). The compiled source consists only of blocks, companions and fields over the old base, and an empty line's block has no axioms. So no refutation through \(11\) would exist. The hypothesis on independent forms is there because the three-selector control uses dependent forms, and the four-line identity \(\sum_\ell(1-\ell^2)=1\) turns a block with dependent forms into a tautology. Whether the three-selector control even violates conservativity is not recorded. Its fall is \(TP\), which contains fresh variables of the same block, not an existing-variable consequence. C3 allows inputs shared across blocks, since independence is required only within a block. Actual lines can contain dependent forms. Compression to a basis of the selector span does not remove dependence among forms whose selectors are independent. So C3 would still leave that reduction step open.

Assessment and next step

The NS formulation gives an exact gluing complex, whose pair case separates at zero cost and heuristically favours random blocks, unlike weights. The NS–PC gap is located, and the PC form that would suffice is conservativity over the PHP base (C3-PHP). Prospects: open. The binary conjecture has consistent checks and no counterexample. The ternary form has not been tested at all. Next step (odd-prime-clause-transfer): test C3 exactly at the smallest nonvacuous sizes, with a GF(3) PC-closure tool built on the recorded bit-sliced elimination.

  • Nonvacuous setting. The base must contain at least one earlier block, because a pure Boolean base makes the test trivial. \(D\ge5\), the companion degree.
  • Size count. With \(v\) old Boolean variables and \(t\) fresh coefficients (exponents at most two), the monomials of degree at most \(D\) number at most \(\sum_{a+b\le D}\binom va\,c_t(b)\), where \(c_t(b)\) counts reduced fresh monomials of degree \(b\). For \(v=8\), two blocks of three inputs (\(t=6\)) and \(D=6\), this is below \(10^5\), well within the tool's range.
  • Controls. The three-selector block with dependent forms, to check whether it breaks conservativity. A block sharing one input with the base block, the structured Example 6.5 case. The binary analogue at the recorded sizes, to reproduce a recorded conservative case.
  • Outcome. A C3 counterexample with independent forms would locate the exact PC obstruction to zero-cost gluing. Consistent conservativity would justify attacking C3 by proof, starting from the recorded binary proofs at rank two (cor:affine-rank-two-same-degree-conservativity).

Sheaf check

No restriction maps are proved here. The candidate is the assignment of augmented closures to block sets, with the passage to existing variables as restriction. Conservativity would say that adding a block changes nothing after restriction. Its NS shadow is the separated mixed-moment system. Whether ternary conservativity holds is the next test.

Verification gate. Re-read historical Lemmas 6.6 to 6.8, Example 6.5 and Corollary 6.9, the first-mixed-band equations and the exact pair duality with its transfer, the foundations' definition of a design, and the closed-moment-tower entry. Searches covered fall additivity, pair feasibility and conservativity. They found the binary conservativity conjecture, its loss bounds, the few-blocks corollary, the second-level refutation and the rank-two conservativity corollary, all cited. No computation was run. A narrowly briefed fresh-context reviewer found the NS formulation essentially sound. It required: the axiom list; Lemma 6.6 described as a sufficient specialization; the depth \(2p+1\); the dimension ratio with its \(m\)-dependence, labelled heuristic; pair separation limited to the pair case; precise definitions in C3; the NS–PC simulation; and cuts to overclaims. All were adopted. Its main objection was that C3 plus induction cannot exclude the compiled source, because the empty clause's block adds the contradiction. That objection assumed the product \(P\) is an axiom. In the compiled source only companions and fields are axioms, so an empty block adds none. The induction is now written out over the PHP base, with the old barrier cited.

Ternary fresh-block conservativity fails over bases with two or more blocks

22 September 2026 · Refutation (finite check) · Conjecture C3 fails over Boolean bases with two or three blocks, at \(D=6\) and \(D=7\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The mixed-moment entry reduced zero-cost gluing at PC level to Conjecture C3. Over the PHP base (C3-PHP), induction over the compiled blocks would then exclude every compiled source with independent forms per line. The missing implication is C3 itself. This cycle tests it with exact closures over a Boolean base (C3-B), whose failure already rules out the inductive use. A sound new existing-variable consequence of a fresh block with independent forms refutes C3. Conservativity in unsaturated instances, defined below, would support it.

Setting and tool

Work in \(R=\mathbb F_3[x_1,\dots,x_v,r_1,\dots,r_t]/(x^2-x,\ r^3-r)\), with joint degree on reduced monomials. A block with affine forms \(L_1,\dots,L_h\) in \(x\) has inputs \(g_i=1-L_i^2\), coefficients \(r_i\), product \(P=1-\sum_ir_ig_i\) and companions \(g_iP\) of degree five. The axioms are the companions only; \(P\) is not an axiom. The closure \(\mathcal C_D\) is the smallest subspace of \(R_{\le D}\) containing the generators and closed under \(f\mapsto yf\) for every variable \(y\) whenever \(\deg f\le D-1\). This is degree-\(D\) PC with the Boolean and field axioms: reduction never raises degree, every correction \(m(x^2-x)\) or \(m(r^3-r)\) used has degree at most \(D\), and reduction commutes with multiplication. The existing variables are \(x\) and the base blocks' coefficients. Setting the fresh coefficients to zero is a ring map that fixes the base generators, kills their field equations and does not raise degree. So \(\mathcal C_D(\text{base})\cap\mathbb F_3[\text{existing}]\) is computed in the smaller ring.

The script conservativity.py iterates \(V\leftarrow V+y\,(V\cap R_{\le D-1})\) to a fixpoint with the recorded bit-sliced GF(3) elimination. Columns are ordered by decreasing degree, so the echelon rows with a pivot of degree at most \(D-1\) span \(V\cap R_{\le D-1}\). A second echelon form with the fresh monomials first gives \(\dim(V\cap\mathbb F_3[\text{existing}])\) as the number of pivots in existing columns. Forms are random, with deterministic seeds, and linearly independent within each block, as C3 requires.

Nonvacuity count

At \(D=5\) a companion cannot be multiplied, so the tests start at \(D=6\). A second count matters more. Every fresh block is satisfiable above every point: where some \(g_i=1\) put \(r_i=1\) and the other coefficients \(0\), so \(P=0\); where all \(g_i=0\), \(P=1\) and every companion vanishes. So every existing-variable consequence of base plus block vanishes on the base's solution set \(S\). Let the semantic dimension be \(\dim\{f\in\mathbb F_3[\text{existing}]_{\le D}: f|_S=0\}\). When \(\dim\mathcal C_D(\text{base})\cap\mathbb F_3[\text{existing}]\) equals it, the base closure is saturated and conservativity at \(D\) is forced by soundness. The gap between the two bounds what any fresh block can add. The script saturation.py computes the semantic dimension by evaluating all monomials on \(S\). The count was made after the first runs, not before, and it changed their reading: every one-block base with two-input blocks was saturated at every degree run (\(D=6,7,8\), and \(D=6,7\) for the dependent control), and all twelve two-block bases run at \(D=8\) were saturated. Those tests decided nothing.

A rise is \(\dim(\mathcal C_D(\text{base}+B)\cap\mathbb F_3[\text{existing}])-\dim(\mathcal C_D(\text{base})\cap\mathbb F_3[\text{existing}])\). No rise exceeded its gap, and none occurred in a saturated instance. Among the unsaturated multi-block instances, 10 of 22 gained new consequences at \(D=6\) and 1 of 8 at \(D=7\). The three-block runs at \(D=7\) and \(D=8\) used only the seeds unsaturated there. Two controls confirm that the tool detects rises: adding a fake old axiom \(x_1x_2x_3\) gives rises of 40 to 60, and adding \(P_B\) as an axiom, which is not a complete block, gives rises of 71 to 180. The full per-instance table is c3_summary.txt.

Witnesses

The script witness.py extracts the new existing-variable elements and checks them independently of the fresh-first bookkeeping. Non-membership in the base closure is tested by rank in the smaller ring's own coordinates. Soundness is tested by evaluation on every base solution. It also finds the least degree at which the base closure contains the element.

  • At \(D=6\), over three two-block bases (seeds 1, 2, 3 of the first family): five new elements of degree 6, with 510 to 1144 terms. All vanish on the base solutions (2070 to 2160 points out of \(2^6\cdot3^4=5184\)), and all lie in \(\mathcal C_7(\text{base})\).
  • At \(D=7\), over one two-block base: one new element of degree 7 with 1418 terms. It vanishes on all 2448 base solutions and lies in \(\mathcal C_8(\text{base})\).

So each witness costs the base exactly one degree more. The rises do not come from linear dependence across blocks: in the \(D=7\) witness and in four of the ten \(D=6\) rising instances, the six linear parts of the base and fresh forms are linearly independent, spanning \(\mathbb F_3^6\).

Claim

Refutation (finite check). Over \(\mathbb F_3\), there are Boolean bases consisting of two complete accuracy-one selector blocks with two inputs each on \(v=6\) variables, and fresh complete two-input blocks whose four base forms and two fresh forms have linearly independent linear parts, such that \[ \mathcal C_D(\text{base}+B)\cap\mathbb F_3[\text{existing}]\supsetneq\mathcal C_D(\text{base})\cap\mathbb F_3[\text{existing}] \] at \(D=6\), and also at \(D=7\). Every new element found lies in \(\mathcal C_{D+1}(\text{base})\). In particular Conjecture C3, stated for every \(D\ge5\), is false in the case C3-B, with independent forms both within and across blocks. The explicit forms and polynomials are stored in the witness files.

Scope

  • C3-PHP is not tested directly. A nonvacuous PHP test needs boards whose PHP refutation degree exceeds \(D\ge6\), far beyond exact closure. The inductive use of C3-PHP needs conservativity over the PHP base plus earlier blocks, and all observed failures have at least two base blocks. The PHP axioms could in principle prevent the new consequences, but no mechanism for that is known.
  • The lag. Every witness enters the base closure one degree higher. A one-degree loss per block, added over polynomially many blocks, would destroy the induction at the fixed degree \(11\). Whether the loss accumulates is almost untestable at these sizes. The script lowgap.py shows that \(\mathcal C_7(\text{base})\cap R_{\le6}\) equals the semantic space in 25 of the 26 multi-block bases at \(D=6\), so containment one degree up is forced there. On the exception (gap 2), accumulate.py added a second random fresh block, in 8 seeds, to the block with the 13-dimensional rise. The existing part stayed 420-dimensional, inside \(\mathcal C_7(\text{base})\): the second block added nothing. The power is low: the existing part could grow by at most 3 dimensions (semantic dimension 423) and leave \(\mathcal C_7(\text{base})\) by at most 2, and the test measures only the variables existing before both blocks, not consequences of the second block in the first block's coefficients. This single case is the only accumulation test.
  • Higher degree. Rises thin out: 10 of 22 unsaturated instances at \(D=6\), 1 of 8 at \(D=7\). The gaps do not always shrink; one three-block base has gap 12 at \(D=6\) and 24 at \(D=7\). At \(D=8\), all twenty one- and two-block bases run are saturated, and seven of eight three-block bases (\(v=5\), 11664 base monomials); the eighth has gap 4. C3 restricted to \(D\ge8\), which is all the induction at \(D=11\) needs, is therefore tested only by that one instance, with 46121 monomials after adding the fresh block. That instance is conservative: rise 0 against gap 4, with the full closure reaching dimension 27198 after nine rounds. The binary refutation goes the other way as \(D\) grows, with one new consequence at \(D=7\) and ten at \(D=8\).
  • Comparison with the binary record. Over \(\mathbb F_2\), a two-input block is provably conservative over any Boolean base. Over a second-level base, binary fresh blocks lose zero degrees at rank two, one at rank three and two at rank four, under the proved loss ceiling. The one recorded binary level-one gain needs mixed accuracies \((2,2,1)\). The ternary failures here have level one, accuracy one throughout and rank two, and still lose one degree. So the ternary case is worse than the binary cases cited here, and the binary level-one conjecture is untouched.
  • One-block bases. The only nonvacuous one-block tests are the three three-input instances at \(D=6\), all conservative. This is too little to support a one-block conservativity statement.

Sheaf check

The candidate assignment, augmented closures with restriction to existing variables, is not stable under adding a block: a block changes the degree-\(D\) sections on the existing variables. The obstruction is concrete, a one-degree lag. A sheaf built from fixed-degree closures would have to charge that lag, and no candidate glues weighted pieces at additive cost.

Assessment and next step

The PC form of zero-cost gluing proposed in the mixed-moment entry fails in its inductive form over Boolean bases. What survives is C3 restricted to \(D\ge8\), a lagged conservativity whose loss does not accumulate, or a statement about all blocks at once over the PHP base, which is close to the original problem. Prospects of the conservativity line: weak, but not closed. Its stated form is refuted. The restricted form at \(D\ge8\) survives its single nonvacuous test, and rises thin from 10 of 22 unsaturated instances at \(D=6\) to 1 of 8 at \(D=7\) and 0 of 1 at \(D=8\). No mechanism explains either the lag or the thinning, and the binary record shows losses growing with \(D\). Nonvacuous tests at \(D\ge8\) are rare at the reachable sizes: one base in 28 was unsaturated at \(D=8\), and larger bases need incremental elimination. Next step (odd-prime-clause-transfer): a route review of the window line after this refutation, as the evidence-based assessment and the rule on failed mechanisms require. It should weigh C3 at \(D\ge8\) and a non-accumulating lag, together with the cost of a nonvacuous test, against the other recorded candidates, rather than refining the refuted mechanism directly.

Verification gate. Re-read Conjecture C3 and its inductive use in the mixed-moment entry, the binary level-one conjecture, the binary rank-two conservativity corollary, the binary same-degree refutation, the rank-dependent binary losses, the binary loss ceiling and the heterogeneous level-one gain. Searched the record with tools/search-claims.py for fresh-block conservativity, second-level refutation and degree lag, and followed the relationships of the binary refutation; the matches are the binary records cited above, and no ternary check exists. Checks run: the controls; the witness extraction with independent rank, soundness and least-degree checks; the saturation and next-degree counts; the accumulation check; and a regression after changing the closure to a bit-packed basis, which reproduced the two-block results exactly. The count against the statement under test was made after the first runs. It showed that the results for one-block bases with two-input blocks, and for the bases run at \(D=8\) before the count, were vacuous, and they are reported as such. A narrowly briefed fresh-context reviewer checked the closure, the existing-part count, the block generators and the witness tests. Its verdict: no bug that could produce a spurious rise; the refutation at \(D=6\) stands. It required recording the one-degree lag, the need for two base blocks, the untested accumulation and whether base forms may overlap the fresh span. C3 allows that overlap, and rises occur without it. A second narrowly briefed fresh-context reviewer checked the bit-packed closure, the saturation, next-degree, accumulation and summary scripts, and every number in this entry against the stored files. Its verdict: the code is exact, the numbers match and the refutation is supported. It required five corrections of overclaimed wording: the extent of the \(D=8\) saturation, the thinning of gaps, an unsupported monomial count, the vacuity of the one-block tests, and causal wording about two base blocks. It also asked for the power of the accumulation test. All were adopted, and the \(D=8\) count for three-block bases was run as it suggested. The binary comparisons, outside its brief, were checked against the claim records. The \(D=8\) run came after both reviews. It used the reviewed code with the OpenMP build of the same elimination routine, and it adds one data point, not a new claim.

Route review after the C3 refutation: test one block over a nontrivial base before gluing

22 September 2026 · Route review of odd-prime-clause-transfer · Separates the single-block calibration from gluing; next: one fresh block over unsaturated random-equation bases. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

The line's general claim. The ternary window can be closed by adding the compiled blocks to the PHP base one at a time, each adding nothing, or nothing that accumulates, to the existing-variable part of the degree-\(11\) closure. This is Conjecture C3 over the PHP base, or a lagged form of it. What the goal needs from this line is that statement at \(D=11\) for every compiled block over PHP plus all earlier blocks. Its first case, a single dense block over PHP alone, is the conservative form of the decisive calibration in the pause review: exclude one random dense block of rank \(\Theta(N)\) at degree \(o(N)\).

Evidence

The refutation entry found that over Boolean bases with two or three blocks, a fresh two-input block adds sound existing-variable consequences at \(D=6\) and \(D=7\), each one degree before the base proves it. Rises thin from 10 of 22 unsaturated instances at \(D=6\) to 1 of 8 at \(D=7\) and 0 of 1 at \(D=8\). Accumulation was tested only once, with low power. The binary record has one-degree losses as well, growing with \(D\) and with rank.

Falsification attempts

  1. Does the refutation already defeat the line at \(D=11\)? No. At \(D=11\) the slack above the companion degree is six, and the failures seen so far occur with slack one or two. The thinning favours the line; the binary growth with \(D\) counts against it. Neither is a mechanism.
  2. Is the failure about gluing at all? Not necessarily. In the multi-block tests the existing ring contains the earlier blocks' coefficients, and those blocks make the base nontrivial on it. A single block over a nontrivial old base has the same shape without any gluing, and it was never tested: a pure Boolean base makes the test trivial, and one-block bases with two-input blocks were saturated. If single blocks already add consequences, the conservativity approach fails even for the calibration, and gluing is not the issue.
  3. Can that shape be tested without vacuity? The companion degree five forces \(D\ge6\), so the base must stay unsaturated at degree six or more. The script proxy_count.py shows that Tseitin bases over \(\mathbb F_3\) on \(K_{3,3}\), the cube \(Q_3\) and the Petersen graph (9 to 15 variables) are saturated at \(D=6,7,8\) with consistent charges, and contain \(1\) with inconsistent ones. Hardness above degree six needs dozens of variables, beyond exact closure. Another script, proxy_count2.py, finds usable proxies: a single random quadratic or cubic equation on 10 or 12 Boolean variables is unsaturated at \(D=6\), with gaps from 106 to 827. A cubic on 12 variables is also unsaturated at \(D=7\) (gaps 1088 and 1124), as is one of two quadratics on 12 variables (gap 376). Two quadratics are mostly saturated. The reason is that every polynomial vanishing on \(\{f=0\}\) is a multiple of \(f\), but the natural multiplier has degree \(\deg f+D\). With a fresh block of two or three inputs, the spaces have 3690 to 27950 monomials, which is feasible.

Assessment of this line

Weak. Its inductive form is refuted, no mechanism explains the one-degree lag or its thinning, and its single-block case is untested. The next test can at least separate the two possible failure modes. If one block over an unsaturated random-equation base adds old consequences, conservativity fails without gluing, including in the calibration's conservative form, and the line should be dropped in favour of mechanisms that tolerate block consequences. If single blocks stay conservative in every nonvacuous instance, the failure is specific to multi-block bases. The single-block calibration would then have finite support in conservative form, and the question becomes a mechanism for it over PHP at \(D=11\), starting from the binary rank-two substitution \(r=(1,1+g_1)\).

Next step

Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. Test single-block conservativity over unsaturated random-equation bases. Base: one random quadratic or cubic equation on \(v=10\) or \(12\) Boolean variables, with deterministic seeds. Fresh block: two or three dense forms with independent linear parts. Degrees: \(D=6\), and \(D=7\) for the cubic on 12 variables. Report the rise against the saturation gap for each instance, and extract witnesses as before. Controls: a fake old axiom, \(P_B\) as an axiom, and a saturated base (two quadratics). The count above bounds the spaces by \(2.8\times10^4\) monomials.

Sheaf check

No gluing is proposed. The review asks whether the restriction of augmented closures to old variables already changes for a single block, before any gluing.

Verification gate. Re-read the pause review with its restart conditions, the window review, the refutation entry and the binary loss records cited there. Searched the record with tools/search-claims.py for single-block conservativity over hard bases and for augmented-PHP closures; the matches are the binary small-board check (8 holes at degree four, low power) and the records already cited, with no ternary single-block test. The counts were run with the reviewed closure code. No reviewer was used for this review, since it adds no mathematical claim.

One fresh block over a nontrivial base: two-input blocks can lose a degree, blocks of three to six inputs stayed conservative at \(D=6\)

22 September 2026 · Finite check · One two-input block over a random quadratic base loses a degree. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The route review asked whether the C3 failures need gluing, or whether one fresh block already adds old consequences over a nontrivial old base. The second case is the conservative form of the pause review's calibration, one dense block over PHP. A rise in an unsaturated instance answers the question. Conservativity in every nonvacuous instance would localize the failures to multi-block bases.

Setting

The ring, closure, blocks and existing-part computation are those of the refutation entry, with no base blocks: the existing variables are the old variables \(x_1,\dots,x_v\). The base \(F\) is one random equation \(f=0\), with uniform coefficients on all monomials of degree at most \(d\in\{2,3\}\), on \(v\in\{10,12\}\) Boolean variables. The fresh block has \(h\) random affine forms with independent linear parts, \(2\le h\le6\). Seeds are deterministic. The script is single_block.py. For each instance it reports the saturation gap, the semantic dimension minus \(\dim\mathcal C_D(F)\), and the rise, \(\dim(\mathcal C_D(F+B)\cap\mathbb F_3[x])-\dim\mathcal C_D(F)\). For each rise it extracts every new element, checks it on all solutions of \(F\), and finds the least \(D'\le D+2\) with the element in \(\mathcal C_{D'}(F)\).

Results at \(D=6\)

Base\(h\)InstancesGapsInstances with a riseRises
quadratic, \(v=10\)24106–1244106, 113, 124, 120: each equals its gap
quadratic, \(v=10\)3, 4, 5, 64, 3, 3, 3106–12400
cubic, \(v=10\)2, 3, 4, 5, 64, 4, 3, 3, 3321–34600
quadratic, \(v=12\)2, 34, 4326–38300
cubic, \(v=12\)2, 34, 4791–85600

All 50 instances are unsaturated. The 4 rises all come from two-input blocks over the quadratic bases on 10 variables. In each, the block fills the whole gap: \(\mathcal C_6(F+B)\cap\mathbb F_3[x]\) is the degree-6 semantic space, which equals the degree-\(\le6\) part of \(\mathcal C_7(F)\). All 463 new elements have degree 6 and 169 to 575 terms. All vanish on every solution of \(F\) (339 to 357 points), and all lie in \(\mathcal C_7(F)\). The other 12 two-input instances and all 34 instances with \(h\ge3\) are conservative. Only the four quadratic bases on 10 variables discriminate between ranks, since over the other bases even two-input blocks never rose. Over them, 13 instances have \(h\ge3\): four with \(h=3\), and three each with \(h=4,5,6\). Controls: a fake old axiom \(x_1x_2x_3\) gives a rise of 63, and \(P_B\) as an axiom gives 508. Two saturated two-quadratic bases serve as soundness checks, since a rise there is impossible, and give none. After a change to packed counting, the controls and the \(D=6\) batch were rerun with the final script and reproduced every value and witness exactly.

A second batch at \(D=7\), over the quadratic and cubic bases on 12 variables with \(h=2,3\) and four seeds each, was stopped by the session host under system-wide memory pressure before finishing. The route review's saturation count found those bases unsaturated at \(D=7\) for the first two cubic seeds (gaps 1124 and 1088) and for one quadratic seed (gap 376). The batch was not rerun in this cycle.

Why two-input blocks are cheap anyway

Lemma FA (first-active substitution). Let \(F'\) be any system in old Boolean variables \(x\) and further variables \(s\) with \(s^3=s\), for example PHP together with other blocks. Let \(B_1,\dots,B_M\) be selector blocks with at most \(h\ge2\) inputs each: inputs \(g=1-L^2\) with \(L\) affine in the variables of \(F'\), and private coefficients \(r\) that occur in no axiom other than their own block's companions and fields. The blocks need not be complete: omitting companions only shrinks the left side below. Then, for every \(D\), with the closure step \(f\mapsto yf\) allowed when \(\deg f\le D-1\), as in the refutation entry, \[ \mathcal C_D(F'+B_1+\dots+B_M)\cap\mathbb F_3[x,s]\subseteq\mathcal C_{2(h-1)D}(F'). \] Proof. Work in \(\mathcal B=\mathbb F_3[x,s]/(x^2-x,\ s^3-s)\), where degree-bounded PC closure with the Boolean and field axioms is the closure used above. Map \(x\mapsto x\), \(s\mapsto s\) and \(r_{b,i}\mapsto\prod_{j<i}L_{b,j}^2=\prod_{j<i}(1-g_{b,j})\). Since \(\mathcal B\) is the ring of \(\mathbb F_3\)-valued functions on the points of the cube and field, and \(L^2\) takes values in \(\{0,1\}\), the images of \(r\) are idempotent. So \(r^3-r\mapsto0\) in \(\mathcal B\), and the map is a ring homomorphism \(\varphi\). By telescoping, \(\sum_ir_{b,i}g_{b,i}\mapsto1-\prod_j(1-g_{b,j})\). So \(P_b\mapsto\prod_j(1-g_{b,j})\), and every companion \(g_{b,i}P_b\mapsto0\), since \(g(1-g)=0\) in \(\mathcal B\). The axioms of \(F'\) contain no \(r\) and are fixed. The image of \(r_{b,i}\) has degree \(2(i-1)\le2(h-1)\), and other variables keep degree one, which is at most \(2(h-1)\) because \(h\ge2\). So \(\deg\varphi(m)\le2(h-1)\deg m\) for every monomial. By induction over the closure steps, \(\varphi(\mathcal C_D(F'+B))\subseteq\mathcal C_{2(h-1)D}(F')\). Generators map to axioms of \(F'\) or to \(0\). A step \(f\mapsto yf\) with \(\deg f\le D-1\) maps to \(\varphi(y)\varphi(f)\), with \(\deg\varphi(f)\le2(h-1)(D-1)\). When \(y\) is not a removed coefficient this is one multiplication, applied to an element of degree at most \(2(h-1)(D-1)\le2(h-1)D-1\), again because \(h\ge2\). When \(y=r_{b,i}\), it is \(2(i-1)\) successive multiplications by affine forms, and the last is applied to an element of degree at most \(2(h-1)(D-1)+2(i-1)-1<2(h-1)D\). Finally \(\varphi\) fixes \(\mathbb F_3[x,s]\). \(\square\)

For two-input blocks the factor is 2, while the losses observed above and in the refutation entry are one degree. Lemma FA is the ternary first-active form of the recorded binary rank-two substitution \(r=(1,1+g_1)\). It complements the degree-factor low-polar transfer, which at \(p=3\) removes level-one blocks with old-affine inputs of rank \(R\) at factor \(3R+1\) but does not treat selector inputs \(1-L^2\). Lemma FA removes blocks with boundedly many inputs and private coefficients from a source at a constant degree factor, and leaves the remaining blocks in the base. It is useless for blocks with about \(N\) inputs.

Assessment

  • Gluing is not needed for failure, at rank two. One two-input block over a single quadratic equation on 10 variables reaches at degree 6 what the base reaches only at degree 7. So conservativity fails without gluing. The four failures are at rank two, where Lemma FA bounds the cost anyway.
  • Rank three and above. No block with three to six inputs rose. The discriminating evidence is only the 13 higher-rank instances over the four bases where two-input blocks rose, with three bases for each \(h\ge4\); the other 21 instances with \(h\ge3\) are over bases where no block rose. The three one-block-base instances of the refutation entry, with three-input blocks, were also conservative. All multi-block failures there also had two-input fresh blocks. A refined route would remove low-rank blocks by substitution first and ask conservativity only for blocks of rank at least three. That refinement is not conjectured here. All the evidence is at \(D=6\), one degree above the companions. In the binary record the loss grows with rank, so higher-rank blocks may simply need more degree to show a loss.
  • Relation to the goal. The window's blocks have rank about \(N\). Suppose the two-input blocks of a compiled source are level-one with private coefficients feeding no other block. Lemma FA then removes them, taking degree \(11\) to \(22\). A multi-block rank-at-least-three form of conservativity, over PHP plus the remaining blocks at degree \(22\), would then suffice, since \(22\) lies far below the PHP degree lower bound. That step leaves the window's blocks of rank about \(N\) untouched, and they are the whole difficulty. Nothing here bears on PHP directly.

Sheaf check

The restriction of augmented closures to old variables changes already for one two-input block over a nontrivial base. For ranks three to six it did not change in any test: 13 discriminating instances, all at \(D=6\).

Next step

Next step (odd-prime-clause-transfer): test the rank-at-least-three form where the evidence is weakest. Run fresh blocks with three and four inputs at \(D=7\) over the bases unsaturated there, and three-input fresh blocks over multi-block bases whose blocks have three inputs, at \(D=6\) and \(D=7\), counting saturation first. Use at most four workers, since the host has 14 GB in total. A rise refutes the refinement. No rise at \(D=7\) makes it worth formulating, with a search for a mechanism that separates rank two from rank three.

Verification gate. Re-read the refutation entry, the route review, the binary rank-two substitution and the low-polar transfer statement. Searched the record with tools/search-claims.py for single-block conservativity over hard bases and for first-active or Fermat-prefix substitutions; the closest records are the binary rank-two substitution, the low-polar transfer (old-affine inputs, degree factor \(pR+1\)) and the constant-row clamp. None treats selector inputs \(1-L^2\), and Lemma FA is labelled as their ternary selector counterpart. Checks run: the controls, their regression after the change to packed counting, and the witness checks. A narrowly briefed fresh-context reviewer checked the new script, every number against the stored files, and the remark with its proof. Its verdict: the code and the counts are right, and the substitution argument is correct. It required a rerun of the \(D=6\) batch with the final script, which reproduced everything. It also required the source of the \(D=7\) gaps, calling the saturated bases soundness checks, and precise hypotheses for the lemma: the step rule, private coefficients, and the remaining blocks placed in the base. It asked for the lemma to be labelled a refinement of the low-polar transfer and registered, for the rank evidence to be narrowed to the 13 discriminating instances, and for conditions on the route sentence. All were adopted. A second fresh-context reviewer, given only the lemma, found no mathematical error. It required stating where \(h\ge2\) is used, weakening the level and completeness hypotheses, a justification of the field images, and a corrected comparison with the low-polar transfer. All were adopted.

Three-input fresh blocks also lose a degree over bases of three-input blocks, at \(D=6\) and \(D=7\)

22 September 2026 · Refutation (finite check) · Refutes the rank-at-least-three refinement of fresh-block conservativity. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The single-block entry found losses only for two-input blocks, which Lemma FA removes at degree factor two. It proposed to test the refinement that fresh blocks with at least three inputs are conservative, where the evidence was weakest: over multi-block bases, and at \(D=7\). A rise in an unsaturated instance refutes the refinement.

Setting and counts

The tool, closure and checks are those of the refutation entry. Each base has two complete three-input blocks on \(v=5\) or \(v=6\) Boolean variables, with forms independent within each block and deterministic seeds. The fresh block has three inputs. The saturation count came first. All twelve bases (six per \(v\)) are unsaturated at \(D=6\), with gaps 12 to 77, and eleven are unsaturated at \(D=7\), with gaps 1 to 105. The full spaces have 19241 and 26584 monomials at \(D=6\), and 43100 and 62341 at \(D=7\). The \(D=7\) runs used the three largest-gap bases on 5 variables (gaps 22, 25, 22) and the two largest on 6 (98, 105).

Results

5666212–354, 1 (others 0)

Every rise is within its gap. The witness script witness2.py checks the new elements with the same tests as before. It vectorizes the soundness check and extracts only the existing-variable rows from a packed echelon form, so that it runs at 62341 monomials. At \(D=6\) it checked three instances (6 variables, seed 4; 5 variables, seeds 2 and 5): 20 new elements of degree 6, with 2043 to 2698 terms, all vanishing on every base solution and all in \(\mathcal C_7(\text{base})\). At \(D=7\) it checked both instances on 6 variables: 10 new elements of degree 7, with 6877 to 7336 terms, all vanishing on every base solution and all in \(\mathcal C_8(\text{base})\). All three witness files were produced by the committed script. An earlier version re-echeloned after every chunk and spanned the same space. On the two instances on 5 variables, the committed script reproduced the reviewed witness.py path exactly, including term counts.

Claim

Refutation (finite check). Over \(\mathbb F_3\), there are Boolean bases of two complete accuracy-one selector blocks with three inputs each on 6 variables, and fresh complete three-input blocks, such that \(\mathcal C_D(\text{base}+B)\cap\mathbb F_3[\text{existing}]\supsetneq\mathcal C_D(\text{base})\cap\mathbb F_3[\text{existing}]\) at \(D=6\) and at \(D=7\). Every checked new element lies in \(\mathcal C_{D+1}(\text{base})\). So the refinement "fresh blocks with at least three inputs are conservative" is false in the multi-block setting that the induction needs.

What the tests now show

  • Every loss verified in these three entries is exactly one degree, for two- and three-input fresh blocks, at \(D=6\) and \(D=7\).
  • Whether a fresh block gains depends on the base, not only on its own rank. Over single random equations, blocks with three to six inputs never gained. Over bases made of blocks, three-input blocks gained in 8 of 12 instances at \(D=6\).
  • At \(D=7\), both instances on 6 variables rose (by 8 and 2, against rises of 5 and 10 at \(D=6\)). None of the three on 5 variables did, including the two that rose at \(D=6\). These five instances were selected by gap, so they indicate no trend.

Assessment

Exact conservativity fails in every tested form: the stated C3, the single-block form (at rank two), and the rank-at-least-three refinement (at rank three). Fresh blocks of rank four or more over bases of blocks were not tested. The route review's decision rule therefore applies: the line gives way to mechanisms that tolerate block consequences. Two such directions remain, and neither has a mechanism. One is a lag that does not accumulate along the induction. The other is a bound for all blocks at once, \(\mathcal C_{11}(\mathrm{PHP}+\text{blocks})\cap\mathbb F_3[\text{old}]\subseteq\mathcal C_{g}(\mathrm{PHP})\) with \(g=o(N)\) uniformly in rank. Lemma FA gives this with \(g=22(h-1)\), which is useless at rank about \(N\). Prospects of the conservativity line: weak. Its exact forms are closed for fresh ranks two and three, and nothing suggests that larger ranks behave better over bases of blocks.

Sheaf check

No restriction map of augmented closures to existing variables is stable under adding a block of rank two or three over a base of blocks. In every witnessed instance the obstruction is one degree.

Next step

Next step (odd-prime-clause-transfer): a route review of the window line now that exact conservativity is closed. It should weigh the two lag-tolerant directions above against the recorded weight and product-split mechanisms and the pause review's restart conditions, and decide which necessary implication the next cycles attack. Among the options is an accumulation test on the three-input bases on 6 variables. They are unsaturated at \(D=7\), but the test is nonvacuous only if the degree-\(\le6\) part of \(\mathcal C_7(\text{base})\) is, and that must be counted first.

Verification gate. Re-read the single-block entry, Lemma FA, the refutation entry and the route review. The saturation count preceded the runs. Witnesses were checked on five of the ten rising instances, at two degrees: 30 new elements, all sound, each entering the base closure exactly one degree higher. The leaner witness path was regression-tested against the reviewed one. A narrowly briefed fresh-context reviewer checked the witness script and every number against the files. Its verdict: the code is right and the numbers match, except the description of the \(D=7\) selection. It required that correction, the provenance of each witness file (all three were then regenerated with the committed script), dropping a trend claim that rested on selected instances, and limiting the scope to fresh ranks two and three. All were adopted.

Route review: after exact conservativity, the one live hypothesis is a uniform one-degree lag, which exact PC tests cannot reach

22 September 2026 · Route review of odd-prime-clause-transfer · No external mechanism; PC lag tests are almost always vacuous; next: Nullstellensatz-level loss against rank. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

The line's general claim. The window can be closed by controlling what the compiled blocks add to the degree-\(11\) closure over PHP. Its exact form, fresh-block conservativity, is closed for fresh blocks of two and three inputs (refutation, single block, rank three). What the goal needs from this line is a bound for all blocks at once, \[ \mathcal C_{11}(\mathrm{PHP}+\text{blocks})\cap\mathbb F_3[\text{old}]\subseteq\mathcal C_{g}(\mathrm{PHP}),\qquad g=o(N), \] uniform in rank, or an induction whose losses do not accumulate. Its first case, one dense block of rank \(\Theta(N)\), is the pause review's decisive calibration. Lemma FA gives the bound only with \(g=22(h-1)\).

Evidence

Every loss verified so far is exactly one degree. That covers fresh blocks with two and three inputs, at \(D=6\) and \(D=7\), over bases of blocks and over single random equations. Blocks with three to six inputs over single random equations did not lose at all. In the binary record, losses over a second-level base grow with rank: zero, one and two degrees at ranks two, three and four.

Falsification attempts

  1. Does outside work supply a mechanism? This is the pause review's third restart condition, and it is not met. A search on 22 September 2026 found the following:
    • Part and Tzameret, Resolution with counting: exponential tree-like \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_F)\) bounds for PHP over every field, and DAG-like bounds over \(\mathbb Q\) for subset sum.
    • Efremenko, Garlík and Itsykson: regular \(\mathrm{Res}(\oplus)\).
    • Impagliazzo, Mouli and Pitassi, PC with extension variables over finite fields: size bounds when each extension variable depends on \(O(\log n)\) original variables.
    • This project's own bit-PHP \(\mathrm{Res}(\oplus)\) paper, over \(\mathbb F_2\).
    The window's block coefficients depend on dense forms of rank about \(N\), outside every one of these.
  2. Can exact PC tests separate a uniform one-degree lag from a lag that grows with rank? Almost never at reachable sizes. A loss of two degrees at \(D=6\) is detectable only if the degree-\(\le6\) part of \(\mathcal C_7(\text{base})\) is below the semantic space. The script lowgap.py finds that part saturated in 25 of 26 two- and three-block bases with two-input blocks, and in 11 of 12 bases of three-input blocks. Each exception has gap 2.
  3. The one probe. On the exception among the three-input bases (6 variables, seed 0), fresh blocks with four and with five inputs were run at \(D=6\). The script witness2.py found 4 and 1 new elements respectively, all sound and all in \(\mathcal C_7(\text{base})\): losses of one degree, where two would have been visible. A three-input block over the same base lost one degree on 5 dimensions. This is consistent with a uniform lag, but it rests on one base with room for only two dimensions.

Assessment of this line

Weak, but not closed. The exact forms are closed. The surviving hypothesis would suffice if true for PHP: adding any number of blocks, of any rank, costs at most one degree. It is consistent with every PC test, but PC tests can almost never falsify it, and it has no mechanism. The binary rank dependence counts against it. Refining the PC experiments further would add cases, not decide the hypothesis.

Next step

Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. Measure the loss against rank at the Nullstellensatz level. There a closure is one span with no iteration, NS spaces saturate later than PC spaces, and the recorded binary coefficient criterion has its ternary form in the mixed-moment system. First count, for bases of three-input blocks, how many degrees above \(D\) the NS spaces stay unsaturated. Then measure the least NS degree containing each new existing-variable consequence of fresh blocks with 2 to 6 inputs. If NS losses grow with rank, a uniform PC lag is implausible, and the line closes. The next review should then turn to the calibration by other means. If NS losses stay at one degree while room for more exists, a uniform NS lag bound becomes a statement worth proving through the mixed-moment system.

Sheaf check

No new gluing. The lag, if uniform, would be the additive cost that the sheaf question asked for: one degree per addition, not per block. That is the only form in which this line still bears on it.

Verification gate. Re-read the pause review's restart conditions, the three conservativity entries, Lemma FA and the binary rank-dependent loss record. The literature search is cited above; no paper was downloaded. The counts and the probe used the reviewed scripts, and the probe's base was checked to be the counted one. No reviewer was used for this review, since it adds no mathematical claim.

Fresh blocks add no Nullstellensatz consequences where polynomial calculus gains: the one-degree losses come from reuse

22 September 2026 · Finite check and working proof · NS rises are zero in all 53 tests, while PC gains on the same instances at \(D=6\); Lemma SB bounds one block's loss by \(2h\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The missing implication is a bound on what the compiled blocks add to the old part of the degree-\(11\) closure that does not accumulate over the blocks. The only surviving candidate is a uniform one-degree lag, and exact PC tests almost never have room to see a larger loss. The route review therefore proposed to measure the loss against rank at the Nullstellensatz level. NS spaces stay far from saturation for several degrees, so losses of several degrees are visible there. Its decision rule was the following. NS losses growing with rank would make a uniform PC lag implausible. NS losses fixed at one degree, with room for more, would make a uniform NS lag bound worth proving.

Setting and counts

Here \(\mathrm{NS}_D(G)\) is the span of the reduced products \(mg\) with \(g\in G\) and \(\deg m+\deg g\le D\), in the ring reduced by the Boolean and field axioms. Each generator is charged at the degree of its reduced form, and some companions reduce below degree 5; base and extension use the same convention. The bases are those of the rank-three entry: two complete three-input blocks on \(v=5\) or \(6\) Boolean variables, with deterministic seeds. A fresh block with \(h\) inputs is added. For each instance the script ns_lag.py computes \(X=\mathrm{NS}_D(\text{base}+B)\cap\mathbb F_3[\text{existing}]\) and finds the least \(D'\le D+4\) with \(X\subseteq\mathrm{NS}_{D'}(\text{base})\). The loss is \(D'-D\). It also checks that \(X\) vanishes at every base solution. Every base solution extends to the block (\(r=e_j\) if some \(L_j\) vanishes there, and \(r=0\) otherwise), so this is necessary. It tests \(X\) only, not the base spaces or the completeness of \(X\).

The counts came first. Let the room at \(D'\) be the semantic dimension (degree-\(\le D\) polynomials vanishing on the base solutions) minus \(\dim\mathrm{NS}_{D'}(\text{base})\cap R_{\le D}\). A loss of \(L\) degrees is visible only if the room at \(D+L-1\) is positive.

Bases\(D\)Room at \(D,\dots,D+4\) (range over bases)Monomials, fresh \(h=2,3\)
12 (\(v=5,6\))6898–1312, 809–1154, 436–780, 98–317, 0–16up to 26584 (\(h=3\))
6 (\(v=5\))84620–5346, 2690–3908, 1163–1945, 261–599, 0–4846121, 84113

So losses of up to four degrees are visible at both \(D=6\) and \(D=8\). The PC closures of the same bases are nearly saturated: PC gaps are 12–77 at \(D=6\) and 0–11 at \(D=8\).

Results

\(D\)Fresh inputs \(h\)NS testsNS risePC on the same instances
62, 3, 4, 5400 in all\(h=3\): gains in 8 of 12, by 1 to 15
82, 3120 in all\(h=2\): no gain on the 4 bases with a PC gap
8410not run
8 (control, \(P\) an axiom)2, 32304 and 87, unsound—

The full spaces have up to 56285 monomials at \(D=6\), and 46121, 84113 and 146454 for \(h=2,3,4\) at \(D=8\) (counts recorded in ns_fresh_forms.json, together with every fresh block used). Eight pairs of a base and a rank at \(D=6\) were skipped. Drawing a fresh block of that rank redraws the base there, so the script refuses the pair. The three-input blocks at \(D=6\) are the fresh blocks of the rank-three PC runs, drawn from the same seeds. The soundness check passed in every test except the control. A rerun with \(h=2,3,4\) at \(D=8\) on all six bases was stopped by the harness under system memory pressure after eight instances, and it was not restarted. Seven of them repeat instances of ns_losses_r3d8.json with identical zero results. The eighth is the only four-input test (5 variables, seed 3). Its log is kept with the results as ns_losses_D8_rerun_partial.txt. The PC twin at \(D=8\) used the committed tester conservativity.py on the same bases and the same two-input fresh blocks.

What the tests show

  • The route review's decision rule does not apply. Both of its outcomes assumed that NS losses exist. There are none in any test, at any rank from two to five, with room for losses of up to four degrees. So the NS level cannot measure how the PC loss depends on rank.
  • The PC losses come from reuse. At \(D=6\), on the same instances with three-input blocks, PC gains in 8 of 12, by up to 15 dimensions, and NS gains nothing. A new PC element is therefore not in \(\mathrm{NS}_D(\text{base}+B)\). Its derivation must multiply lines whose top-degree terms cancelled. The round-by-round probe pc_rounds.py shows how much reuse these closures involve. On the six instances where every nonzero generator has degree 5, the first round of the closure at \(D=6\) is exactly \(\mathrm{NS}_6(\text{base}+B)\), and it holds only 5–7% of the final existing-variable part. On the other six, the first round lacks the higher multiples of the low-degree generators. The closures stabilize after 6 to 9 rounds. The probe reproduces the PC tester's dimensions on all 12 instances. It does not isolate which reuse produces the gain.
  • At \(D=8\) there is no contrast. The PC twin of the NS tests, two-input blocks over the four bases with a positive PC gap (gaps 1, 3, 6, 11), is conservative on all four. So the \(D=8\) tests show only that NS does not lose either.
  • NS is much weaker than PC here. At \(D=6\), \(\dim\mathrm{NS}_6(\text{base})\) is 53 to 239, against PC closures of 901 to 1539. At \(D=8\), \(\dim\mathrm{NS}_8(\text{base})\) is 996 to 2413, against 5642 to 7033. So NS conservativity on these bases says little about PC. It does agree with the binary level-one conjecture, which is an NS statement: no fresh block over a base of level-one blocks has shown an NS loss in either characteristic.
  • A correction to the route review's evidence. The route review counted the binary rank-dependent losses against a uniform PC lag. Those are NS losses over a second-level base, measured by an NS checker. They are not evidence about PC losses over level-one bases, and the ternary NS analogue over level-one bases shows no loss at all. The review's assessment of the line does not rest on this point.

A proved ceiling for one block

Lemma SB (single-block loss, rank-dependent form). Work over \(\mathbb F_3\) with existing variables \(Y\): Boolean \(x\) and further variables \(s\) with \(s^3=s\). Let \(\Gamma_0\subseteq\mathbb F_3[Y]\) be any system. A fresh selector block has inputs \(g_i=1-L_i^2\), \(i\le h\), with \(L_i\) affine in \(Y\), fresh coefficients \(r_1,\dots,r_h\), \(P=1-\sum_ir_ig_i\), and axioms \(g_iP\) and \(r_i^3-r_i\). Let \(\Gamma_1\) be \(\Gamma_0\) with this block. Degrees are joint degrees, and the Boolean and field axioms are available throughout. Then for every \(t\in\mathbb F_3[Y]\): \[ t\in\mathcal C_D(\Gamma_1)\ \Rightarrow\ t\in\mathcal C_{D+2h}(\Gamma_0),\qquad t\in\mathrm{NS}_D(\Gamma_1)\ \Rightarrow\ t\in\mathrm{NS}_{D+2h}(\Gamma_0). \]

Proof. Work in \(\mathcal B=\mathbb F_3[Y]/(x^2-x,\ s^3-s)\), the ring of \(\mathbb F_3\)-valued functions on the points of the cube and field. Each \(L_i\) takes values in \(\mathbb F_3\), so \(L_i^2\in\{0,1\}\), and \(g_iL_i^2=0\) and \(g_i(1-g_i)=0\) in \(\mathcal B\). A product that vanishes in \(\mathcal B\) is a combination of Boolean and field axiom multiples within its own degree.

  1. Specialization. Substitute \(r=c\in\mathbb F_3^h\) in a derivation of \(t\). Lines keep or lower their degree. Multiplication by \(r_i\) becomes multiplication by the scalar \(c_i\), the fields \(r_i^3-r_i\) vanish, the companions become \(g_iP(c)\) with \(P(c)=1-\sum_ic_ig_i\), and \(t\) is unchanged. So \(t\) has a degree-\(D\) derivation (or certificate) from \(\Gamma_0\cup A_c\), with \(A_c=\{g_iP(c)\}_i\).
  2. Weighting. Let \(w\in\mathbb F_3[Y]\) have degree at most \(e\), with \(wa=0\) in \(\mathcal B\) for every \(a\in A_c\). Multiply every line of the specialized derivation by \(w\). An axiom \(a\in\Gamma_0\) becomes \(wa\), which is derived from \(a\) by multiplications within degree \(\deg a+e\le D+e\). An axiom in \(A_c\) becomes \(0\). Linear combinations commute with the weighting, and a step \(f\mapsto yf\) with \(\deg f\le D-1\) becomes \(wf\mapsto y(wf)\) with \(\deg(wf)\le D+e-1\). So \(wt\in\mathcal C_{D+e}(\Gamma_0)\). For a certificate \(t=\sum_km_ka_k\), the same multiplication gives \(wt\in\mathrm{NS}_{D+e}(\Gamma_0)\).
  3. Input annihilation. For \(c=e_j\), \(P(e_j)=1-g_j=L_j^2\) and \(A_{e_j}=\{g_iL_j^2\}_i\). With \(w=g_j\) of degree 2, \(g_j\cdot g_iL_j^2=g_i\cdot g_jL_j^2=0\). So \(g_jt\in\mathcal C_{D+2}(\Gamma_0)\) for every \(j\).
  4. Zero specialization. For \(c=0\), \(A_0=\{g_i\}_i\). With \(w=M=\prod_j(1-g_j)\), of degree at most \(2h\), \(Mg_i=0\). So \(Mt\in\mathcal C_{D+2h}(\Gamma_0)\).
  5. Assembly. Expanding \(M=\sum_S(-1)^{|S|}g_S\) gives \(t=Mt+\sum_{S\ne\varnothing}(-1)^{|S|+1}g_St\). For \(S\ne\varnothing\) take \(j\in S\). Then \(g_St=g_{S\setminus j}\,(g_jt)\) comes from \(g_jt\in\mathcal C_{D+2}(\Gamma_0)\) by \(|S|-1\) multiplications by inputs, each done as \(g_iF=F-L_i(L_iF)\) with two multiplications by the affine form \(L_i\). Every element multiplied along the way has degree at most \(D+2|S|-1\le D+2h-1\), since \(\deg t\le D\). So \(t\in\mathcal C_{D+2h}(\Gamma_0)\). The NS case is the same identity, since NS spaces are closed under multiplication at the cost of degree. \(\square\)

Relation to the record. Lemma SB is a refinement of two recorded results, not a new method. Steps 1–3 are the first stage of the recorded old-consequence transfer at \(\alpha=1\): specialize \(r=e_j\) and weight every PC line. The weight is \(g_j\), of degree 2, instead of \(\chi_1(g_j)=1-(g_j-1)^2\), of degree \((p-1)\delta=4\). This is possible because \(g_j\) takes only the values 0 and 1. Step 4 is that lemma's second stage with the weight \(M\) in place of \(t\). The assembly is the rank-dependent half of the binary specialization bound (\(D+k\delta\), stated there for NS and accuracy \(h\)). Lemma SB differs from that bound in three ways: its inputs must be 0/1-valued, weighting replaces the charged-degree bookkeeping, and it covers accuracy one only. The old-consequence transfer gives a rank-independent PC bound over every \(\mathbb F_p\), \(\max\{D+(p-1)\delta,\ D+\deg t,\ p\deg t\}\), which is \(\max\{D+4,D+\deg t,3\deg t\}\) here. Lemma SB is sharper only when \(2h\) is below \(\max\{4,\deg t,3\deg t-D\}\), that is, for few inputs and targets of high degree. The tested new elements have degree at most \(D\). For them the old-consequence transfer, a PC statement whose second stage reuses a derived line, allows at most \(2D\) extra degrees. Lemma SB allows \(4\) for two inputs and \(6\) for three. At the NS level, which is what the tests below measure, Lemma SB is the only recorded ternary ceiling. Lemma FA treats all blocks at once, at the degree factor \(2(h-1)\). Applied block by block, Lemma SB costs \(2\sum_bh_b\) in total. That is additive in the total rank and useless for the window.

Hypotheses not used. The selector form enters only through \(g_i^2=g_i\) in \(\mathcal B\) and \(\deg g_i\le2\), and affinity of \(L_i\) only through that degree. The fresh field axioms, completeness of the companion set and linear independence of the forms are not used; \(\deg t\le D\) holds automatically.

Precision on the recorded instances

A random form \(ax_k+a\) with \(a\ne0\) never vanishes on the cube. Its input \(1-L^2\) is then identically zero, and its companion vanishes. Every degenerate form found has this shape. The scan covered every recorded instance whose forms are stored: the PC result files, the single-block files, and the NS draws recorded by ns_fresh_forms.py. It found the following.

  • Three bases of the rank-three entry (5 variables, seed 3; 6 variables, seeds 1 and 2), where one of the two base blocks has effectively two inputs. The last two are among the \(D=6\) PC rises, with 3 each. So two of the eight rank-three rises at \(D=6\) are over such a base. The other six, including every witnessed instance, are not.
  • One fresh input in a six-input block of the single-block entry, which did not rise.
  • One fresh input in the small3 instance with seed 0 of the refutation entry, conservative at \(D=6\) and \(D=7\).
  • One fresh input in the fake-axiom control tiny with seed 1, which rose as a control should.

No fresh block of the NS tests is degenerate. Apart from the control, no instance that rose has a degenerate fresh input. The recorded claims stand, since each is witnessed by instances without degenerate inputs.

Assessment

This cycle does not advance the missing implication. It locates the recorded losses: they are PC effects produced by reuse, with no NS counterpart on the tested bases. That removes the NS level as a place to measure the lag. A uniform PC lag remains the one candidate that would suffice. It still has no mechanism, and exact PC tests can almost never falsify it. The proved single-block costs are additive: \(2h\) by Lemma SB, a factor \(2(h-1)\) by Lemma FA, and the old-consequence transfer's rank-independent charge. None is uniform in the number of blocks. Prospects of the conservativity and lag line: weak. Its decisive question is now a PC mechanism for a loss that does not accumulate, and nothing in the tests points to one.

Sheaf check

At the NS level, the restriction of augmented spaces to existing variables does not change in any test. That is the additive gluing the mixed-moment entry found at the NS level. In PC it changes by one degree. So the NS gluing is consistent with these data, and the PC gluing fails.

Next step

Next step (odd-prime-clause-transfer): a route review of the window line. Five cycles have left the same implication untouched: a non-accumulating bound on what the blocks add to the old part of the degree-\(11\) closure. The review should decide whether any PC mechanism for a non-accumulating lag is in sight, or whether the window needs a direct construction instead. A direct construction would be a degree-\(11\) functional on old and block variables that annihilates \(\mathcal C_{11}(\mathrm{PHP}+\text{blocks})\) and gives \(1\) the value \(1\), built from the PHP pseudo-expectation. It should weigh these against the pause review's restart conditions.

Verification gate. Re-read the route review's decision rule, the rank-three entry, Lemma FA, the binary specialization bound, the old-consequence transfer and the binary level-one and rank-dependent-loss records. The rank-dependent loss data were confirmed to come from an NS checker. The NS counts preceded the loss runs. The rewritten ns_lag.py was regression-tested against its earlier sparse version (equal row spans on four spaces, equal counts on all 18 bases). The control with \(P\) as an axiom fires. The round probe reproduces the PC tester on all 12 instances. Before drafting Lemma SB, a fresh-context reviewer confirmed that the record has only the binary NS form, and that the ternary statement is a direct transfer. A second fresh-context reviewer checked the lemma and the code; it also brute-forced tiny instances. Its verdict: the proof is correct in PC and NS, and the code computes what it states. It required several corrections, all adopted: crediting the old-consequence transfer's two stages, degree "at most \(D\)" for the new elements, the reduced-degree NS convention, the stated limits of the soundness check, and withdrawing a claim that the first closure round equals \(\mathrm{NS}_6\) on every instance. A third fresh-context reviewer checked every number against the result files and confirmed all but four points, which were corrected: the shape of the degenerate forms and two unlisted instances with them, the count of instances in the stopped run, an unsupported remark on base rounds, and missing records of the NS fresh blocks, now written by ns_fresh_forms.py.
