Route review: completeness of resolution refutes every block-count-independent conservativity or lag over PHP; the window needs a size-sensitive mechanism

22 September 2026 · Route review of odd-prime-clause-transfer · Completeness refutes C3-PHP and block-count-independent lags; one block costs at most 4 degrees; next: exclusions plus few arbitrary lines. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

The line's general claim. The window can be closed by controlling what the compiled blocks add to the old part of the degree-\(11\) closure over PHP. Its forms were exact conservativity over the PHP base (Conjecture C3, case C3-PHP) and, after the Boolean-base refutations, a uniform lag: any number of blocks of any rank costs a bounded number of degrees. What the goal needs is that no polynomial family of compiled blocks over the full functional linear-row PHP base \(F_N\) has a PC refutation through degree \(11\). The goal is a size lower bound, so the size of the family must enter.

Falsification attempt: completeness

This review asked whether the line's hypotheses are consistent with the completeness of the proof system. They are not. The conclusion below follows at once from the conjecture's own reduction paragraph, which puts no bound on the size of the source. The record never drew it, and the registry still listed C3-PHP as untested.

Observation CR (completeness refutation). Let \(d_N\) be the least \(D\) with \(1\in\mathcal C_D(F_N)\) over \(\mathbb F_3\). By the all-field matching barrier, \(d_N>B\) whenever \(N\ge2B-1\), so \(d_N>11\) for \(N\ge21\). Let \(T_N\) be the number of lines of some resolution refutation of \(\mathrm{PHP}^{N+1}_N\); a complete decision tree gives \(T_N\le2^{N(N+1)+1}\). Then:

  1. there are at most \(T_N\) complete accuracy-one selector blocks over \(F_N\), each with linearly independent single-variable forms, whose union with \(F_N\) has a PC refutation through degree \(11\);
  2. Conjecture C3 fails over the PHP base at every degree \(D\) with \(11\le D<d_N\), for every \(N\ge21\); the degrees \(5\le D\le10\) over PHP and the Boolean case C3-B are untouched;
  3. if \(\mathcal C_{11}(F_N+\text{blocks})\cap\mathbb F_3[\text{old}]\subseteq\mathcal C_{11+f(M)}(F_N)\) holds for every family of \(M\) compiled blocks, then \(f(M_N)\ge d_N-11\), where \(M_N\le T_N\) is the number of blocks in (1). In particular no cumulative bound independent of \(M\) holds. The lag review's hypothesis, that adding any number of blocks costs at most one degree, is such a bound and is false over PHP. Lags that accumulate per block, such as one degree per block or Lemma SB's \(2h\), are not contradicted.

Proof. Take a resolution refutation whose clauses are non-tautological and contain each variable at most once; the decision-tree refutation has this form. It is a standard syntactic \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_3})\) refutation. Read each literal as an equation \(x-a=0\) with \(a\in\{0,1\}\). Resolving \(C\vee(x-1=0)\) with \(E\vee(x=0)\) by the resolution rule with \(h=(x-1)-x\) gives \(C\vee E\vee(-1=0)\). Simplification deletes the false equation, and contraction merges repeated literals. By the complete-board transfer, the refutation yields at most \(T_N\) complete accuracy-one selector blocks over \(F_N\), with a PC refutation through \(4p-1=11\). Each block's inputs are a basis subset of the line's selectors \(1-L^2\). In a line without the false equation, the selectors \(1-(x-a)^2=1-a^2+2ax-x^2\) of distinct variables are linearly independent polynomials, since each has its own \(x^2\) term. So the basis keeps all of them, and their forms \(x-a\) have independent linear parts. The false equation's selector \(1-(-1)^2\) is zero, so it lies in no basis. The line with it therefore has the same block inputs as its simplification. This proves (1). For (2), add the blocks one at a time in line order. Each is fresh over \(F_N\) and the earlier blocks, with independent forms, and its inputs involve old variables only. If C3-PHP held at some \(D\) with \(11\le D<d_N\), induction would give \(\mathcal C_D(F_N+\text{all blocks})\cap\mathbb F_3[\text{old}]=\mathcal C_D(F_N)\cap\mathbb F_3[\text{old}]\), which does not contain \(1\). But \(1\in\mathcal C_{11}(F_N+\text{all blocks})\subseteq\mathcal C_D(F_N+\text{all blocks})\) by (1). For (3), apply the bound to the family of (1) with \(t=1\): \(1\in\mathcal C_{11+f(M_N)}(F_N)\), so \(11+f(M_N)\ge d_N\). \(\square\)

So the conservativity line was false over PHP, at the degrees that matter, from the start. The mixed-moment entry's inference "if C3-PHP held … no refutation through 11 would exist" proves too much: it would exclude refutations of every size. The exact computations tested only the Boolean-base case C3-B, which completeness does not touch, since a Boolean base is satisfiable. Any valid lag bound \(f\) must grow with the number of blocks. With the trivial bound on \(T_N\), \(f\) must reach \(d_N-11\ge N/2-11\) somewhere below \(M=2^{N(N+1)+1}\). What the goal needs is \(f(\mathrm{poly}(N))<d_N-11\).

Falsification attempt: is one dense block the obstacle?

No. The recorded old-consequence transfer with target \(t=1\) removes one fresh block of any rank and accuracy from any base, at a cost of \((p-1)\delta=4\) degrees. Its inputs may be old polynomials of degree at most 2, and its coefficients must be private. So a single random dense block of rank \(\Theta(N)\) is excluded jointly with any exclusion that holds four degrees higher. The pause review's first restart condition, stated for one block, is therefore met by a recorded result, so it does not calibrate what the window needs. The real calibration is the number of window blocks. Removing \(K\) blocks one at a time costs \(4K\), which is additive, as completeness requires.

Assessment of this line

Closed in its block-count-independent forms. Exact conservativity and cumulative lags over PHP are refuted by Observation CR, and the Boolean-base tests could not have detected this. What survives is the correct shape of the problem: a size-sensitive exclusion, with a per-block cost that stays small only for polynomially many blocks. The recorded exclusions are size-sensitive through one matching restriction and a union bound. Examples are subquadratic cell support and sub-fifth row support, both at polylogarithmic degree. Dense window blocks survive such restrictions, and no recorded mechanism replaces the union bound for them. Prospects of the window by recorded methods: weak, as before. The review does not change that verdict, but it removes a false hypothesis and fixes the scale. Each window block costs at most 4 degrees, and a polynomial number of them is the whole difficulty.

Next step

Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. Compose the recorded exclusions with the old-consequence transfer. Remove up to \(K\) arbitrary lines' blocks at \(4K\) degrees, then apply an exclusion that holds at degree \(11+4K\). The claim to state and check is an endpoint: polynomial-size refutations in which all but \(K=\mathrm{polylog}(N)\) lines satisfy a recorded exclusion hypothesis, and the remaining \(K\) lines are arbitrary. First search the record for this composition and check that each exclusion holds at degree \(11+4K\) with the block removal preceding its restriction. Then find the largest \(K\) the recorded parameter ranges allow. If the record has no such composition, it would be the first endpoint that admits window lines at all. The gap from polylogarithmically many to polynomially many window lines is then the precise open problem.

Sheaf check

Observation CR says that no gluing with block-count-independent cost exists over PHP, whether for sheaves, conservativity or lags. A good sheaf would have to pay per piece, and the old-consequence transfer is the recorded per-piece gluing, at 4 degrees a block.

Verification gate. Re-read the pause review with its restart conditions, the C3 conjecture and its reduction paragraph, the complete-board transfer and the equation-clause compiler with its rules (resolution, weakening, simplification, contraction and the basis compression of selectors), the all-field matching filtration, the old-consequence transfer, and the NS entry. Searched the record for the completeness argument, for block-count dependence and for few-block results; the closest is the binary additive bound for few fresh blocks over unary PHP, which does not state it. Before drafting, a fresh-context reviewer answered whether the record implies Observation CR and checked the argument. Its verdict: implied by the C3 reduction paragraph but never drawn, and the argument is correct. It required naming the degree range of the refutation, making the clause form explicit, evaluating the bound at the actual number of blocks, and separating cumulative bounds from per-block lags. All were adopted, and the result is recorded as an observation, not a new lemma. No computation was run.

Short refutations of PHP need polynomially many wide lines: per-block elimination composed with the cell-support exclusion

22 September 2026 · Working proof · Polynomial-size refutations of unary PHP need \(\Omega(n^\beta)\) lines of cell support above \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\operatorname{polylog}n\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The missing implication is the exclusion of polynomial-size refutations whose lines include polynomially many window lines. The block-count review showed that any mechanism must use the number of blocks. It also showed that one block of any rank costs at most \((p-1)^2\) degrees. It proposed to test how far per-block elimination, composed with a recorded exclusion, can go. The answer is either an endpoint with a stated number of arbitrary lines, or an obstruction in the composition, for example an exclusion that holds only at polylogarithmic degree.

Removing arbitrary blocks: the recorded elimination

No new lemma is needed here. The recorded old-consequence transfer with target \(t=1\) (so \(k=0\)) turns a degree-\(d\) refutation of \(\mathcal G\cup\mathcal E_U\cup\mathcal R_U\) into one of \(\mathcal G\) of degree \(d+(p-1)\delta\). Here \(U\) is one complete block whose inputs have degree at most \(\delta\), whose coefficients occur in no axiom of \(\mathcal G\), and \(\mathcal G\) may contain other blocks' companions. Applied block by block, it removes \(K\) such blocks at total cost \(K(p-1)\delta\). This is the additive charge of the recorded balanced elimination. The removal is valid only while no remaining block's inputs use a removed block's coefficients (compare the later-dependency example). One-level blocks with old inputs, as produced by the compiler, satisfy this. For compiled selector blocks \(\delta=p-1\), so each removal costs \((p-1)^2\), which is 4 at \(p=3\).

The composition

Theorem Y (cell-support exclusion with exceptional lines). Fix a prime \(p\), \(0<\varepsilon\le1\), \(A\ge0\), \(c>0\) and \(0<\beta<\varepsilon/2\). Let \(k\) be the least integer with \(k(\varepsilon-2\beta)>c+1\), and \(T=\max(1,2(k-1))\). For large \(n\), with \(N=\lceil n^\beta\rceil\), put \[ K_n=\left\lfloor\frac{\lfloor (N+1)/2\rfloor/T-(4p-1)}{(p-1)^2}\right\rfloor=\Theta(n^\beta). \] Every standard syntactic \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) refutation of ordinary unary \(\mathrm{PHP}^{n+1}_n\), or of its functional variant, with at most \(n^c\) lines has more than \(K_n\) lines whose clause has a union of cell supports larger than \(n^{2-\varepsilon}(\log n)^A\).

Proof. Call a line narrow if its union of cell supports has at most \(n^{2-\varepsilon}(\log n)^A\) cells, and wide otherwise. Suppose a refutation has at most \(n^c\) lines, of which at most \(K_n\) are wide.

  1. Compile. The complete-board transfer applies to refutations of ordinary unary PHP and of its functional variant alike, and compiles over the full functional linear-row PHP base. It gives one complete accuracy-one selector block per line, hence at most \(n^c\) blocks, with a PC refutation of degree \(4p-1\). Each input is literally a selector \(1-L^{p-1}\) of an equation of its line, of degree at most \(p-1\), and the input-basis compression selects actual selectors, so a narrow line's block has all inputs on its line's cell set. This is the same observation as in the cell-support exclusion's own corollary.
  2. Remove the wide blocks. Let \(K\) be the number of wide lines' blocks; \(K\le K_n\), since a line with an empty selector basis has no block. The recorded elimination with \(\delta=p-1\) removes them one at a time. At each step the base still contains the wide blocks not yet removed, which the old-consequence transfer allows. The result is a PC refutation of the base plus the narrow blocks only, of degree \(D'=4p-1+K(p-1)^2\le\lfloor(N+1)/2\rfloor/T\).
  3. Restrict and replay. Apply the proof of the cell-support exclusion to this refutation. Its restriction is a uniform partial matching leaving \(N+1\) rows and \(N\) columns. A union bound over the at most \(n^c\) narrow blocks gives one restriction with residual matching number below \(k\) in every block, hence a residual vertex cover of size \(s_a\le2(k-1)\le T\). The large-\(n\) threshold of this union bound depends on \(A\) and \(k\), not on any degree. The recorded proof sets \(T=\max(1,\max_as_a)\), but its replay inequalities \(s_a+\delta+\delta_i\le Te_i\) and \(ps_a\le Tp\) need only \(T\ge\max(1,s_a)\), so the fixed \(T\) above is a valid choice. The restriction and the coefficient substitution depend only on the narrow blocks. The eliminated refutation contains no variable of a removed block, since the old-consequence transfer specializes them to constants. So the exclusion's hypotheses (complete one-level blocks with old inputs, fresh coefficients, all companions and fields, common support) are checked on exactly the narrow blocks. Its coefficient substitution then replays any PC proof of degree \(D'\) as an old functional-PHP proof of degree at most \(TD'\), with no factor for the number of blocks.
  4. Contradiction. Put \(B=\lfloor(N+1)/2\rfloor\). Then \(N\ge2B-1\) and \(TD'\le B\), so the all-field matching barrier excludes the residual refutation.

The recorded exclusion is stated for polylogarithmic degree. Its proof gives the linear replay bound \(TD\) for every \(D\), and the final cutoff \(TD\le B\) is the only place the degree enters. \(\square\) The proof works for every \(0<\varepsilon<2\), and \(c\ge0\) suffices. For \(\varepsilon>1\) the statement is trivial. Every refutation contains all \(n+1\) pigeon clauses as lines: dropping one leaves a satisfiable set, and the system is sound. Each pigeon clause has \(n\) cells, more than \(n^{2-\varepsilon}(\log n)^A\) when \(\varepsilon>1\), and \(n+1>K_n\).

What it gives

  • As far as the record shows, the first endpoint that admits arbitrary lines. The exceptional lines may be window lines, dense lines or anything else. For \(\varepsilon=1\), a polynomial-size refutation needs \(\Omega(n^\beta)\) lines whose cell support exceeds \(n\operatorname{polylog}n\), for every fixed \(\beta<1/2\). The constant depends on \(p\), and on \((c,\varepsilon,\beta)\) through \(T\), which grows as \(\beta\to\varepsilon/2\).
  • Where it stops. The count of tolerated wide lines is at most the residual PHP degree, about \(N/2\le n^{1/2}\), because each removal costs a constant. Observation CR shows that some growth with the number of blocks is unavoidable; per-block removal grows linearly. The window problem is now quantitative: a refutation with polynomially many window lines, more than \(n^{1/2}\), is not excluded.
  • Other exclusions. The same composition applies to any exclusion that meets four conditions. Its restriction and substitution are chosen independently of the proof degree. The compiled narrow blocks meet its block hypotheses. It replays a degree-\(D\) refutation at a degree \(\varphi(D)\) that is monotone in \(D\). And it ends with the barrier at a cutoff \(B\). It then tolerates \(K\) exceptional lines while \(\varphi(4p-1+K(p-1)^2)\le B\). The row-support exclusion's replay degree \(sD_*\) goes through its row-state expansion. How that depends on the proof degree is not checked here, so no count is claimed for it.

Assessment

This is a real but modest step: a quantitative refinement of the cell-support exclusion, proposed with polylogarithmic \(K\) in the block-count review and proved here with \(K=\Theta(n^\beta)\). It turns the review's scale argument into a stated endpoint, and it shows that the cell-support exclusion tolerates a polynomial number of arbitrary lines, not only a polylogarithmic one. It does not touch the window's core. Per-block removal can never absorb more exceptional lines than the residual PHP degree allows. Excluding polynomially many window lines still needs a mechanism that handles many dense blocks together, and none is recorded. Prospects of the window line: weak, unchanged.

Sheaf check

The recorded elimination is the per-piece gluing, at \((p-1)^2\) degrees a piece. Theorem Y glues it to one restriction-based exclusion. The composition works because the removals happen before the restriction and the exclusion's replay is linear in the degree. No gluing of the exceptional pieces among themselves is used.

Next step

Next step (odd-prime-clause-transfer): determine the replay degree of the other recorded exclusions as a function of the proof degree, starting with Corollary ND, whose class, nonlocal dimension below \(N^{1/2-\varepsilon}\) per line, lies next to the window. An exceptional-line count for Corollary ND would say that a polynomial-size refutation needs polynomially many lines of large nonlocal dimension, which are window or dense lines. That is the quantitative form of the window problem. Excluding more than about \(\sqrt n\) such lines needs a mechanism charging a window block less than a constant, for example one that removes many blocks together using structure a single restriction exposes. Random dense forms keep matching number about \(N\) under any matching restriction, so no residual-cover count can supply it.

Verification gate. Re-read the old-consequence transfer (statement, hypotheses and the case \(t=1\)), the balanced-elimination record, the later-dependency example, the complete-board transfer and the equation-clause compiler's compression paragraph, the cell-support exclusion with its full proof, and the all-field matching filtration. Searched the record for the composition under the elimination and exclusion names. A first fresh-context reviewer, asked whether the record implies the result, found the per-block elimination already recorded, so it is cited rather than restated as a lemma. It also found the composition only proposed, with polylogarithmic \(K\), in the block-count review. It asked to confirm one block per line, accuracy one, input degree \(p-1\) and the functional base for ordinary PHP; all hold and are now stated. A second fresh-context reviewer tried to break the proof and found no break. It required clarifications of the choice of \(T\), the order of elimination and restriction, the count \(K\), the unused hypothesis \(N+1\ge B\) and the role of \(\varepsilon\le1\). It also required replacing an unproved \(n^{1/2-o(1)}\) claim by \(\Omega(n^\beta)\) for each fixed \(\beta\). All were adopted. No computation was run.

Short refutations need about \(\sqrt{n}\) lines of large nonlocal dimension: wide blocks removed after the common weight

22 September 2026 · Working proof · Polynomial-size \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) refutations of PHP need \(\Omega(\sqrt{n/\log n})\) lines of nonlocal dimension above \(n^{1/(p-1)-\varepsilon}\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The missing implication is unchanged: exclude polynomial-size refutations that contain polynomially many window lines. Theorem Y admits \(\Theta(n^\beta)\) arbitrary lines, \(\beta<1/2\), on top of the cell-support exclusion. Its next step asked for the same count for Corollary NDp, whose class, lines of nonlocal dimension at most \(n^{1/(p-1)-\varepsilon}\), lies next to the window. The task is to find how each step of the quotient-rank chain depends on the proof degree, and where the wide blocks are best removed. The test ends with a count, or with a step whose parameters depend on the proof degree.

How the chain depends on the proof degree

Fix an odd prime \(p\) and put \(\delta=p-1\). The chain of Theorem QRp has five steps. Only the last one depends on the proof degree \(D\).

  1. The complete-board transfer gives one complete accuracy-one selector block per line and a PC refutation through \(4p-1\).
  2. The degree-certified basis conversion does not raise the degree when \(D\ge2p-1\). The rank-one representation raises it to \(\max(D,2p+1)\). Both act block by block, and other blocks' axioms pass through unchanged.
  3. The robust graph \(H\) is fixed before the source is seen, in section 4 of the fixed-graph entry: 128 neighbors per row, right degree at most \(\lceil(\ln n)^2\rceil\), boundary expansion \(\delta_H=64\) through \(L=\lfloor\gamma n\rfloor\). Its separation ceiling is \(B_H=\lfloor\delta_HL/(4d)\rfloor\) with \(d=128\), so \(\lambda n\le B_H\le n\) for a fixed \(\lambda>0\) and large \(n\). The restriction to \(H\) and the row projection are ring maps, chosen once.
  4. The two-level semantic map chooses one weight \(f\) of degree at most \(k_n\) and coefficient images of degree at most \(T_n\). By the fixed-graph theorem, \(k_n=\lceil\sqrt{s\ln(16(M+1))/A_0}\rceil\), where \(s\le128(n+1)\) is the number of nondistinguished edges, \(A_0=2d\Delta\ge256\), and \(M\) is the number of parent affine cores and unused bottom tuples. The map degree is \(T_n=\max\{\tau,\,T_A+1+\delta'\max_a(\ell_a-1)_+\}\) with \(T_A=(p-1)(4A_0+1)k_n\). These depend on the graph, on \(M\) and on the blocks' quotient ranks, not on \(D\).
  5. Step 4 of that map, the global substitution, replays a degree-\(D\) proof as a derivation of \(f\) over the projected graph base through \(T_nD+k_n\). Separation needs \(T_nD+k_n\le B_H\). Coefficient fields cost \(pT_n+k_n\), which is at most \(T_nD+k_n\) because \(D\ge4p-1\ge p\), so there is no further additive term.

So the degree enters only through the replay \(T_nD+k_n\). There are two places to remove the wide blocks. Removing them before the map, as in Theorem Y, costs \(\delta^2\) proof degrees per block, and each proof degree costs \(T_n\) after the map. This gives the count \(n^{\min(1/2,\delta\varepsilon)}/\operatorname{polylog}n\), and is not recorded further. Removing them after the map costs only the weight's degree \(k_n\) per block, which is better for every \(\varepsilon\).

The theorem

Theorem NDX (nonlocal-dimension exclusion with exceptional lines). Fix an odd prime \(p\), \(\delta=p-1\), \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(c>0\). There is \(C>0\), depending only on \(p\) and \(c\), such that for all sufficiently large \(n\) the following holds. Every standard syntactic \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) refutation of ordinary unary \(\mathrm{PHP}^{n+1}_n\), or of its functional variant, with at most \(n^c\) lines has more than \(C\sqrt{n/\ln n}\) lines of nonlocal dimension above \(n^{1/\delta-\varepsilon}\). Nonlocal dimension is as in Corollary ND.

Proof. Call a line narrow if its nonlocal dimension is at most \(n^{1/\delta-\varepsilon}\), and wide otherwise. Suppose a refutation has at most \(n^c\) lines, of which \(K\) are wide.

  1. Compile. The complete-board transfer gives at most \(n^c\) complete accuracy-one selector blocks over the full functional linear-row base, one per line, and a PC refutation \(\Pi\) through \(4p-1\). Each block's inputs are selectors \(1-L^\delta\) of equations of its line. Call a block narrow or wide according to its line; at most \(K\) blocks are wide.
  2. Convert the narrow blocks. By the proof of Corollary NDp, each narrow block has \(r_a\le2^\delta n^{1-\delta\varepsilon}\), or \(r_a=O_p(1)\) when its nonlocal dimension is below \(\delta\). For \(\varepsilon\ge1/\delta\) the threshold is below one, narrow lines have only local forms, and \(r_a=0\). Apply the basis conversion and the rank-one representation of Theorem QRp to the narrow blocks only. The wide blocks' axioms pass through unchanged. The ceiling stays \(\max(4p-1,2p+1)=4p-1\).
  3. Restrict, project and map. Restrict \(\Pi\) to \(H\) and apply the row projection \(\Psi\). Both are degree-nonincreasing ring maps. Old axioms go to axioms of the projected graph base \(\Gamma'_H\), each with an old proof through degree two (projection lemma). A wide block goes to a complete one-level block \(W'\) whose inputs are old polynomials of degree at most \(\delta\), with its private coefficients, companions and fields. Build the two-level map from the converted narrow blocks alone, as in the power-range corollary with bottom exponent \(0\) and parent exponent \(\sigma=1-\delta\varepsilon\). Its inventory satisfies \(M\le n^c(1+(2n^2)^{\delta})\). Let \(\sigma\) substitute the narrow coefficients by their images, of degree at most \(T_n\), and fix \(Y\) and every wide-block variable. Replace each line \(\ell\) by \(f\sigma(\ell)\). A monomial with \(j\) narrow coefficient variables and total degree \(e\) maps to degree at most \(jT_n+(e-j)\le T_ne\), since \(T_n\ge1\). So a line of degree \(e\) maps to degree at most \(T_ne+k_n\), and multiplication by any variable, narrow, wide or old, is replayed within \(T_n(4p-1)+k_n\). Narrow companion and field images are certified from \(\Gamma'_H\) through \(T_ne+k_n\) and \(pT_n+k_n\) by step 4. An old axiom or a wide-block axiom \(A\) satisfies \(\sigma(A)=A\), and \(fA\) is a legal multiple of degree \(\deg A+k_n\). This parallels the replay of Proposition MX, which keeps the axiom images of a second block class. The result is a PC derivation of \(f\) from \(\Gamma'_H\) together with the at most \(K\) blocks \(W'\), through \(d_0=(4p-1)T_n+k_n\).
  4. Remove the wide blocks after the map. Apply the recorded old-consequence transfer (BC) with target \(t=f\), to one wide block at a time. The base consists of \(\Gamma'_H\) and the wide blocks not yet removed. BC needs a Boolean or field equation for every old variable. \(\Gamma'_H\) contains Booleanity in \(Y\), and the remaining wide blocks are complete, so their coefficient fields \(r^p-r\) are present. The removed block's coefficients occur nowhere else. Its inputs, like \(f\), lie in \(\mathbb F_p[Y]\), so BC's domain reductions use Booleanity in \(Y\) only. The target is an old polynomial of degree at most \(k_n\). A derivation of degree \(d\ge pk_n\) becomes one of degree at most \(\max\{d+\delta^2,\,d+k_n,\,pk_n\}=d+\max(\delta^2,k_n)\). Since \(T_n\ge T_A\ge k_n\), the starting degree satisfies \(d_0\ge pk_n\). After \(K\) removals, \(f\) is derived from \(\Gamma'_H\) through \(d_K=d_0+K\max(\delta^2,k_n)\).
  5. Contradiction. The ceiling \(d_K\) is at least two, so the proof lifts to \(\Gamma_H\) with the same ceiling. The fixed-graph separation lemma applies at \(k=k_n\) for large \(n\). Its conditions (FG-pairs) hold: \(k_n(A_0+1)/s=O(n^{-1/2}(\ln n)^{5/2})\to0\), \(z=8ed^2\Delta k_n/(\delta_Hs)=O(n^{-1/2}(\ln n)^{5/2})\), \(\xi=emz^{\delta_H/4}=emz^{16}=O(n^{-7}\operatorname{polylog}n)\to0\), and \(k_n\le m-L\) since \(k_n=o(n)\). Also \(B_H\ge d\) for large \(n\). So \(f\), a nonzero combination of good degree-\(k_n\) monomials, is separated from \(\mathcal C_B(\Gamma_H)\) for \(k_n\le B\le B_H\). Since \(k_n\le d_K\), this forces \(d_K>B_H\).
  6. Arithmetic. By the fixed-graph formula, \(k_n\le\sqrt{(c+2p)\,n\ln n}\) for large \(n\), using \(s\le128(n+1)\), \(A_0\ge256\) and \(\ln(16(M+1))\le(c+2\delta+1)\ln n\). Also \(T_A\le5(p-1)A_0k_n=O(\sqrt{A_0s\ln(16(M+1))}+A_0)=O(\sqrt n(\ln n)^{3/2})\), using \(A_0\le256\lceil(\ln n)^2\rceil\). With rank-one bottoms and accuracy one, \(\tau=\max(1,p-2)\), \(\delta'=\delta\) and \((\ell_a-1)_+\le\delta c_a\le\delta r_a\). Hence \(T_n=O_p(\sqrt n(\ln n)^{3/2}+n^{1-\delta\varepsilon})=o(n)\), so \((4p-1)T_n+k_n\le B_H/2\) for large \(n\). Also \(k_n\ge\sqrt{s\ln16/A_0}\ge\sqrt{127(n+1)\ln16/(512(\ln n)^2)}\), which exceeds \(\delta^2\) for large \(n\). Then \(d_K>B_H\) forces \(K>(B_H/2)/k_n\ge(\lambda/2)\sqrt{n/((c+2p)\ln n)}\). Take \(C=\lambda/(2\sqrt{c+2p})\); logarithms are natural. \(\square\)

"Sufficiently large" depends on \(p\), \(c\) and \(\varepsilon\), through \(T_n=o(n)\) and the fixed-graph conditions. Only \(\varepsilon>0\) is used, for \(T_n=o(n)\); values \(\varepsilon\ge1/\delta\) give weaker statements, about lines with a nonlocal form. The count does not depend on \(\varepsilon\), only the threshold does. With \(\varepsilon\) small, a polynomial-size refutation needs \(\Omega(\sqrt{n/\ln n})\) lines whose nonlocal dimension is almost \(n^{1/(p-1)}\). At \(p=3\), these are lines with more than \(n^{1/2-\varepsilon}\) independent nonlocal forms.

The limit of per-block removal

Observation. With the recorded fixed-graph weight and the recorded accounting, neither order of removal certifies more than \(O(\sqrt n\,\ln n)\) exceptional lines. The weight \(f\) is a nonzero combination of good degree-\(k_n\) monomials, so \(\deg f=k_n\). After the map, BC's recorded bound charges at least \(\deg f=k_n\) per removal, through its second stage, which weights every line by the target. The actual degree increase may be smaller, since that stage first sets the removed coefficients to zero, but the proof above cannot certify more. Before the map, BC charges \((p-1)\) times the input degree, which is exactly \(\delta^2\) because wide inputs come from nonconstant forms. After the map each proof degree costs \(T_n\), so the charge is \(\delta^2T_n\ge k_n\). The weight's own counting needs \(A_0k_n^2/s\ge\ln(16(M+1))\ge\ln16\), so \(k_n\ge\sqrt{s\ln16/A_0}\ge c'\sqrt n/\ln n\), using \(s\ge127(n+1)\) and \(A_0\le256(\lceil(\ln n)^2\rceil)\). Since the budget is at most \(B_H\le n\), there are at most \(n/k_n=O(\sqrt n\ln n)\) removals. Theorem Y stops below the same scale for a different reason: its count is at most the residual PHP degree, about \(N/2\) with \(N=\lceil n^\beta\rceil\) and \(\beta<1/2\). This is a limit of these two constructions, not a lower bound for other methods.

What it gives

  • A count for the class next to the window. Theorem Y counts lines of large cell support. Theorem NDX counts lines with many independent nonlocal forms, which is the property of window lines, and it holds at every odd prime. Neither implies the other: a line can have small cell support and large nonlocal dimension, and conversely.
  • Why the order matters. Blocks handled by the common weight cost a maximum over blocks; their number enters only through \(\ln M\) in \(k_n\). Blocks removed one at a time cost a sum. Removing them after the map charges each one the weight's degree instead of the map's multiplier on four proof degrees.
  • What remains. A refutation with polynomially many window lines, more than about \(\sqrt n\), is not excluded. The window is still the whole difficulty.

Assessment

This is a modest step, of the same kind as Theorem Y. It gives the quantitative form of Corollary NDp and shows that removal after the weight beats removal before it. Like Theorem Y, it is a special case: it refines an endpoint without moving the missing implication. Two consecutive cycles now end at the same square-root scale, for different reasons, so per-block removal is not the mechanism the window needs. In the common-weight framework, the window needs dense blocks to be handled by the map, at a cost that is a maximum over blocks. The recorded parent map costs about the nonlinear quotient rank, and a dense line's rank can be quadratic in its nonlocal dimension. Prospects of the window line: weak, unchanged.

Sheaf check

The common weight is one global section over all narrow blocks, and its cost does not add up over them. The wide blocks are glued on afterwards, one piece at a time, and each piece costs the section's degree. That per-piece cost is where \(\sqrt n\) enters. A good sheaf for the window would have to put dense blocks into the global section.

Next step

Next step (odd-prime-clause-transfer): a route review. Theorems Y and NDX are refinements of recorded endpoints that leave the missing implication untouched, which calls for a review under the route-check rule. The review should weigh three options. The first is a per-block map for dense blocks inside the common-weight framework, where cost is a maximum over blocks; the question is whether one dense selector block admits a coefficient map of degree \(o(n)\) on the weight's support. The second is a write-up of the partial endpoints under scope-and-review. The third is the thread's other route items.

Verification gate. Re-read the fixed-graph entry (the pair-counting lemma, the fixed-graph theorem with its \(k\), \(R\), \(T\) and ceiling, and the graph class), the two-level semantic map with its step 4 and power-range corollary, the projection lemma, the rank-one bridge, the ternary quotient-rank theorem, Theorem QRp and Corollary NDp, Corollary ND, Proposition MX's replay, the old-consequence transfer (BC) and Theorem Y. Searched the record for exceptional lines, nonlocal dimension and per-block elimination, and for BC with a weighted target. The closest records are Theorem Y and the binary few-fresh-blocks remark, which removes blocks sequentially over the unweighted base. Before drafting, a fresh-context reviewer was asked whether the record implies the result, for the removal-before-map version. It found the result not recorded and implied only through Theorem Y's unchecked template. It asked to show explicitly that the graph, weight and map degree do not depend on the proof degree, to check for additive terms in the ceiling, to derive the count, and to prove or drop the limit remark. All four are addressed above. After drafting, a second fresh-context reviewer, given the draft and excerpts of the fixed-graph theorem, the two-level map, the projection lemma, BC, Theorem QRp and the rank-one bridge, tried to break the proof. Its verdict: the proof holds, and none of H, f, \(k_n\), \(T_n\) or \(M\) depends on the proof degree. It required the (FG-pairs) check at \(k_n\), the monomial count for the replay with wide variables kept, a self-contained argument for keeping the wide axioms, BC's field equations for the remaining wide coefficients, the field-image cost, and an in-proof bound \(k_n\ge\delta^2\). It also found the hypothesis \(\varepsilon\le1/\delta\) unused and asked for a weaker wording of the limit observation. All were adopted, and \(\varepsilon\le1/\delta\) was dropped. No computation was run.

Route review: per-block removal cannot pass a linear number of window lines, and the window needs a batched mechanism

22 September 2026 · Route review of odd-prime-clause-transfer · Per-block removal is capped at \(O(n)\) window lines; the recorded accounting reaches \(\sqrt n\); no batched mechanism is recorded. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

The line's general claim. Polynomial-size \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_3})\) refutations of PHP can be excluded by combining the recorded exclusions for non-window lines with a mechanism for the window lines, the lines of projected rank of order \(n\). The last two research entries tested the simplest such mechanism: remove each window line's block on its own, and exclude the rest. Theorem Y and Theorem NDX give \(\Theta(n^\beta)\), \(\beta<1/2\), and \(\Omega(\sqrt{n/\log n})\) arbitrary lines respectively. What the goal needs is to tolerate polynomially many window lines, since nothing forces a short refutation to have few of them. By Observation CR, the cost of adding \(M\) blocks must grow with \(M\), but completeness only forces it to reach \(d_N-11\) somewhere below \(2^{O(N^2)}\) blocks. So a cost of order \((\log M)^a\) with \(a\ge1/2\) is consistent with completeness, and it would suffice. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. Both entries were refinements of recorded endpoints, which is why this cycle is a review.

Falsification attempts

F1. How far can per-block removal go? Not beyond a linear number of blocks. The recorded exclusions end with a Boolean degree barrier. The matching barrier is at most about half the board, and the graph separation ceiling \(B_H\) is at most \(n\). Each recorded one-block elimination charges at least one degree of that final replay: \((p-1)\delta\ge1\) degrees for target one, and at least \(\deg t\) for a target \(t\). So any such composition tolerates at most \(n\) removed blocks, whatever the order and the exclusion. The recorded accounting gives less: about \(\sqrt n\) in both theorems (limit). The gap between \(\sqrt n\) and \(n\) comes from one step. After the map, the old-consequence transfer's second stage weights every line by the target \(f\), which costs \(\deg f\approx\sqrt n\) per block. In the replayed derivation every use of a block axiom is already a multiple of \(f\), so that stage may be unnecessary. If so, each block costs \((p-1)^2\), and Theorem NDX would give \(\Omega(n)\) window lines, the ceiling. This is a candidate, not a claim; it is the next step.

F2. Can blocks be removed together, at less than the sum of their costs? The recorded attempt, balanced elimination, keeps the additive total. The reason is structural. The first stage for one block weights the current derivation by that block's input selectors. That derivation still contains the other blocks' axioms. Doing the first stages in parallel would make each block's derivation use the others' companions, a circular dependency, and sequential stages multiply their weights. No recorded argument breaks the cycle.

F3. Can a max-type mechanism take window blocks? The two mechanisms whose cost is a maximum over blocks are a common restriction and a common weight. For the first, the calibration argument gives a dyadic random inventory that defeats a common restriction across sizes, and random dense forms keep matching number about \(N\) under matching restrictions. For the second, the window review (F2 there) expects a single random window block to leave no weight in the separated space. That expectation rests on the semi-regular model and general position. The alignment tests found the only departure from general position to be a row collapse that fades as rows grow. The window's two ends are both linear in \(N\): exact prefix maps cost about twice the rank, and the degree barrier is at most \(n\). So the prefix side stops below \(N/40\), and weights are expected to start only near \(10^3N\).

F4. Does outside work supply a batched mechanism? The lag review searched on 22 September 2026 and found none. The published methods for dense linear lines, safe systems and closure, apply to regular or bounded-depth proofs, where the argument follows one path of the proof. They work at linear rank, the window's scale, but not for arbitrary DAG-like proofs.

Assessment of this line

Weak, unchanged. The per-block sub-line is closed at a linear ceiling. It is at \(\sqrt n\) with the recorded accounting and possibly \(\Theta(n)\) with the sharper one, and neither is the polynomial count the goal needs. What remains is a batched mechanism: a joint elimination, or a max-type map for window blocks, with cumulative cost sublinear in the number of blocks. Completeness allows one. Every recorded max-type mechanism fails on window blocks, heuristically for weights and by the calibration argument for restrictions. The recorded joint elimination is additive. The evidence is a proved ceiling for the removal route, and heuristics, not proofs, for the other two.

Next step on the highest-risk item

Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. First settle the per-block sub-line at its ceiling. The lemma to prove says that if a PC derivation of an old target \(t\) uses a fresh block's axioms only through multiples of \(t\), the block is eliminated at \((p-1)\delta\) degrees, keeping that property for the other blocks. Applied after the map in Theorem NDX, it would give \(\Omega(n)\) lines of large nonlocal dimension. It needs the record check and a breaking reviewer. After that, the next cycle should formulate the batched question at its smallest case: whether the first stages of two blocks can share one weighting, and whether the derivation order of the compiled refutation breaks the circular dependency of F2. If neither yields a mechanism, the review after that should weigh the scope-and-review write-up against continuing.

Sheaf check

The removal route glues local sections one at a time, and each gluing costs the per-piece charge; the ceiling says such gluings stop at a linear number of pieces. A useful sheaf would glue many window pieces at once. F2's circular dependency is the obstruction to doing that with elimination stages: each piece's local section is defined only relative to the others.

Verification gate. No result is claimed. Re-read the window review (F1 to F5), the alignment entry, the lag review's literature paragraph, Observation CR, Theorems Y and NDX with the limit observation, and the old-consequence transfer's three stages. Searched the record for elimination from target-weighted derivations and for balanced or joint elimination. The closest records are the balanced-elimination audit and the binary few-fresh-blocks remark. Neither states the weighted form, so it goes through the full gate in its own cycle. No computation was run.

Target-weighted elimination removes a block at \((p-1)\delta\) degrees: short refutations need \(\Omega(n)\) lines of large nonlocal dimension

22 September 2026 · Working proof · Polynomial-size \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) refutations of PHP need \(\Omega(n)\) lines of nonlocal dimension above \(n^{1/(p-1)-\varepsilon}\). Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The route review found that per-block removal cannot pass a linear number of window lines. The recorded accounting reaches only about \(\sqrt n\). The gap comes from the old-consequence transfer (BC): after the map of Theorem NDX, its second stage weights every line by the target \(f\), at \(\deg f\approx\sqrt n\) per block. This cycle tests whether that stage is needed when every use of a block's axioms already carries the target. The test ends with a proof of the cheaper elimination, or with a step of BC that the weighting does not replace. The missing implication itself, polynomially many window lines, is not addressed: the ceiling is linear.

The lemma

Setting. Work over \(\mathbb F_p\), as in BC. Let \(Y\) be the old variables and \(\mathcal G_0\subseteq\mathbb F_p[Y]\) a set of axioms that contains the Boolean or field equation of every variable of \(Y\). Let \(U_1,\ldots,U_K\) be complete blocks of any accuracy. Each \(U_b\) has nonzero inputs \(f_{b,i}\in\mathbb F_p[Y]\) of degree at most \(\delta_b\), accuracy \(h_b\), private coefficients \(R_b=\{r_{b,v,i}\}\) disjoint from \(Y\) and from the other blocks, product \(P_b=\prod_{v=1}^{h_b}\bigl(1-\sum_ir_{b,v,i}f_{b,i}\bigr)\), companions \(E_{b,i}=f_{b,i}P_b\) and field equations \(r^p-r\), \(r\in R_b\). Zero inputs are dropped. Fix a target \(t\in\mathbb F_p[Y]\). A \(t\)-weighted leaf of \(U_b\) is a polynomial \(twA\) with \(w\in\mathbb F_p[Y]\) and \(A\) an axiom of \(U_b\). A PC derivation is \(t\)-weighted if it derives \(t\) from \(\mathcal G_0\) and finitely many \(t\)-weighted leaves, each treated as an axiom of degree \(\deg(twA)\). Such a leaf is a legal multiple of \(A\), derivable from \(A\) within \(\deg(twA)\), so a \(t\)-weighted derivation of degree \(d\) is an ordinary PC derivation of degree \(d\) from \(\mathcal G_0\) and the blocks.

Lemma WE (target-weighted elimination). If a \(t\)-weighted derivation has degree \(d\), there is a \(t\)-weighted derivation of degree at most \(d+(p-1)\delta_1\) that uses leaves of \(U_2,\ldots,U_K\) only. Removing all \(K\) blocks in turn gives a derivation of \(t\) from \(\mathcal G_0\) alone through \(d+(p-1)\sum_b\delta_b\).

Proof. Write \(U=U_1\), \(R=R_1\), \(f_i=f_{1,i}\), \(\delta=\delta_1\), and let \(\pi\) be the given derivation.

  1. First stage, as in BC. Run this stage for every input \(f_j\) whose companion occurs in a leaf of \(U\). Fix such a \(j\) and \(\alpha\in\mathbb F_p^\times\). Specialize \(r_{1,1,j}=\alpha^{-1}\), the coefficient of \(f_j\) in the first row, and every other variable of \(R\) to zero; then \(P_U\) becomes \(1-\alpha^{-1}f_j\). Multiply every line of \(\pi\) by \(\chi_\alpha(f_j)=1-(f_j-\alpha)^{p-1}\). Each line gains at most \((p-1)\delta\) in degree, and inference steps stay valid, since specialization is a ring map fixing \(Y\) and the other blocks' variables. A leaf \(twE_i\) of \(U\) becomes \(\chi_\alpha(f_j)\,tw\,f_i(1-\alpha^{-1}f_j)=\alpha^{-1}tw\,f_i(f_j^p-f_j)\) by the polynomial identity of BC. Its degree is at most \(\deg(tw)+\deg f_i+p\deg f_j\le\deg(twE_i)-1+(p-1)\deg f_j\le d+(p-1)\delta\), since \(\deg P_U\ge1+\deg f_j\). It lies in \(\mathbb F_p[Y]\), because \(t\), \(w\) and the inputs do, and it vanishes on the Boolean or \(\mathbb F_p\)-valued domain of \(Y\). So domain reduction certifies it from the equations of \(Y\) in \(\mathcal G_0\) within its own degree; the other blocks' field equations are not needed, and they may stay inside weighted leaves. A field leaf \(tw(r^p-r)\) becomes zero. A leaf \(twB\) of another block becomes \(t(\chi_\alpha(f_j)w)B\), again a \(t\)-weighted leaf, since \(B\) does not involve \(R\) and \(\chi_\alpha(f_j)w\in\mathbb F_p[Y]\). This preservation is what makes the induction on \(K\) valid. Axioms of \(\mathcal G_0\) become legal multiples. The last line is \(\chi_\alpha(f_j)t\). Since \(\sum_{\alpha\ne0}\alpha\chi_\alpha(x)=x\) is a polynomial identity, combining over \(\alpha\) derives \(tf_j\) through \(d+(p-1)\delta\), from \(\mathcal G_0\) and \(t\)-weighted leaves of the other blocks.
  2. Second stage, without weighting. Specialize every variable of \(R\) to zero in \(\pi\) itself. Then \(P_U\) becomes \(1\), so a leaf \(twE_i\) becomes \(twf_i\). Derive it from the line \(tf_i\) of the first stage by multiplying by \(w\), within \(\deg(twf_i)\le\deg(twE_i)\le d\). Field leaves become zero. Leaves of other blocks, axioms of \(\mathcal G_0\) and the target \(t\) do not involve \(R\) and are unchanged. The result derives \(t\) through \(\max(d,d+(p-1)\delta)\), and every block axiom it uses sits in a \(t\)-weighted leaf of \(U_2,\ldots,U_K\). \(\square\)

The proof never uses that the blocks are complete or that their field equations are present: leaves of any subset of a block's axioms are handled the same way. This is BC's first stage followed by specialization. BC's second stage weights \(\pi\) by \(t\), because in general a companion leaf is used without the factor \(t\). Its third stage then removes the square \(t^2\). In a \(t\)-weighted derivation the factor is already present, so both are unnecessary. The charges \(d+\deg t\) and \(p\deg t\) disappear, and the stages do not accumulate: the derivation stays \(t\)-weighted. For \(t=1\) every derivation is \(1\)-weighted, and the lemma is BC's case \(t=1\). The recorded prime-dependent loss is consistent with it: its derivation uses the companion \(x(1-rx)\) without a factor of the target \(x\), so it is not \(x\)-weighted.

The linear count

Theorem NDX′. Fix an odd prime \(p\), \(\delta=p-1\), \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(c>0\). There is \(C>0\), depending only on \(p\), such that for all sufficiently large \(n\) the following holds. Every standard syntactic \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) refutation of ordinary unary \(\mathrm{PHP}^{n+1}_n\), or of its functional variant, with at most \(n^c\) lines has more than \(Cn\) lines of nonlocal dimension above \(n^{1/\delta-\varepsilon}\).

Proof. Follow the proof of Theorem NDX through its step 3. With \(K\) wide lines, it gives a PC derivation \(\pi_0\) of the weight \(f\) through \(d_0=(4p-1)T_n+k_n\). The derivation is over the projected graph base \(\Gamma'_H\), which contains Booleanity in \(Y\), and the at most \(K\) wide blocks \(W'\). Lemma WE needs three facts about \(\pi_0\). It derives \(f\) from \(\Gamma'_H\subseteq\mathbb F_p[Y]\) and the multiples \(fA\) of wide-block axioms; the narrow images, the projection-lemma proofs and the replayed multiplications are all derived from \(\Gamma'_H\). Each wide axiom \(A\) enters only through \(fA\), taken as a leaf with \(w=1\). And distinct wide blocks have disjoint coefficient sets outside \(Y\), with nonzero inputs in \(\mathbb F_p[Y]\) of degree at most \(\delta\). So \(\pi_0\) is \(f\)-weighted for the target \(t=f\in\mathbb F_p[Y]\), with \(\mathcal G_0=\Gamma'_H\). Lemma WE, applied \(K\) times, derives \(f\) from \(\Gamma'_H\) through \(d_K\le d_0+K\delta^2\), since each charge is \((p-1)\delta_b\le\delta^2\). Step 5 of Theorem NDX then applies unchanged. The proof lifts to \(\Gamma_H\), and the separation of \(f\) through \(B_H\) forces \(d_K>B_H\). By step 6 there, \(d_0\le B_H/2\) for large \(n\). So \(B_H<d_K\le B_H/2+K\delta^2\), and \(K>B_H/(2\delta^2)\). The graph family of the fixed-graph entry (its section 4) has \(L=\lfloor\gamma n\rfloor\) for a fixed \(\gamma>0\), \(\delta_H=64\) and \(d=128\). So \(B_H\ge\lambda n\) for large \(n\), with \(\lambda=\gamma/9\) independent of \(c\) and \(\varepsilon\). Take \(C=\lambda/(2\delta^2)\). \(\square\)

The count now meets the linear ceiling of the route review, up to the constant. It depends on \(c\) and \(\varepsilon\) only through "sufficiently large". The limit observation of Theorem NDX concerned BC's recorded accounting and stands as stated; Lemma WE is a different accounting.

Assessment

The per-block sub-line is now settled up to constants. A polynomial-size refutation needs linearly many lines with more than \(n^{1/(p-1)-\varepsilon}\) independent nonlocal forms, and no per-block argument can ask for more than linearly many. At \(p=3\) this makes the quantitative problem exact up to constants: refutations with at most \(Cn\) lines of nonlocal dimension above \(n^{1/2-\varepsilon}\) are excluded, and those with more are open. It is a real improvement, from \(\sqrt n\) to \(n\), but it is a refinement of the same kind as Theorems Y and NDX. The window line's prospects stay weak: what remains is a batched mechanism, and none is recorded.

Sheaf check

Lemma WE is a gluing statement. Once the global section, the weight, is chosen, each window piece glues on at a constant cost, because every piece is already expressed relative to that section. What does not glue is many pieces at once: each piece's first stage is defined relative to the others, which is the circular dependency of the route review.

Next step

Next step (odd-prime-clause-transfer): pose the batched question at two blocks. Take a \(t\)-weighted derivation with two wide blocks, and ask whether removing both can ever cost less than \(2(p-1)\delta\). If it cannot, find a family that forces the sum. The alternative is a joint first stage that breaks the circular dependency, for example by following the derivation order of the compiled refutation. A forced sum over every base would show that a batched mechanism must use PHP structure. If this gives no mechanism, the following review should weigh the scope-and-review write-up against continuing.

Verification gate. Re-read the old-consequence transfer (setting, statement and all three stages), the prime-dependent loss example, the mixed elimination and clamping audit, the greedy internal-reference transfer, and the proof of Theorem NDX with its limit observation. Searched the record for elimination from target-weighted derivations, for the old-consequence transfer's second stage and for joint elimination. Before drafting, a fresh-context reviewer answered whether the record implies Lemma WE. Its verdict: implied by BC's first stage but never stated, to be recorded as a refinement of BC. The greedy transfer it flagged retains its terminal blocks rather than eliminating them, so it is not a special case. It found no contradiction. It asked for the leaf degree, the use of the equations of \(Y\) only, and the preservation of weighting to be stated; all three are. A second fresh-context reviewer, given the draft, BC in full and the proof of Theorem NDX, tried to break both results and could not build a weighted derivation needing more than \(d+(p-1)\delta\). Its verdict: both are correct. It required writing out \(P_b\) and the row index of the specialized coefficient, running the first stage for every used input, an inequality for the leaf degree, a precise description of \(\pi_0\) instead of "every line is \(f\sigma(\ell)\)", the inequality chain for \(K\), the independence of \(\lambda\) from \(c\) and \(\varepsilon\), and dropping an ambiguous remark on Theorem Y. It also found completeness of the blocks unused. All were adopted; the unused hypothesis is noted rather than removed, so the stated claim is unchanged. No computation was run.

Route review: blocks batch only when their spans nest, and window blocks do not

22 September 2026 · Route review of odd-prime-clause-transfer · The recorded batch theorems need spans nested modulo annihilators; window blocks are not; next: test a reuse-free gluing. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

The line's general claim. After the common weight, the window blocks can be removed together, at a cost that grows more slowly than their number. What the goal needs is that polynomially many window blocks cost \(o(n)\) degrees in the final replay. Theorem NDX′ reaches the linear ceiling of one-at-a-time removal. The last review asked whether two blocks can ever cost less than the sum, and whether derivation order breaks the circular dependency between their first stages. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer.

Falsification attempt: does the record contain a batched mechanism?

Yes, and it answers the two-block question. The historical nested-span theorem removes a chain of blocks with input spans \(V_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq V_s\) for one charge \((p-1)\delta\), whatever its length. Its target form, the batch modulo target annihilators (TAB), needs nesting only modulo a space \(H\) with \(tH\) cheaply derivable. The historical core–residual theorem relaxes nesting to nested cores, at a multiplier that grows with the residual rank. These theorems break the circular dependency by nesting. When the current input \(f\) lies in every later block's span, every later block can be specialized to the product \(1-\alpha^{-1}f\) at once. Its companions then become field consequences, not axioms that still need removing. So two blocks cost one charge when their spans nest modulo \(H\), and every recorded argument charges the sum otherwise.

Window blocks do not nest, for two reasons.

  • What an annihilator space can absorb. After the map, \(H\) must satisfy \(fH\subseteq\mathcal C_c(\Gamma_H)\) for the weight \(f\). It contains the PHP consequences of low degree, which the quotient rank already factors out. For one matching monomial, the affine annihilators are exactly the recorded space \(H_M\), by the rigidity theorem (MAR) of the TAB entry. If \(H\) lies in the PHP consequences plus affine forms, then \(V_a\subseteq V_b+H\) forces the nonlinear quotients to nest. For a window block these have rank up to about \(r^2/2\) at nonlocal dimension \(r\). The record does not characterize nonlinear annihilators of the weight, but nothing in it makes the nonlinear parts of two random dense lines nested modulo annihilators.
  • Derivation order does not create nesting. Over \(\mathbb F_3\), resolving on equations \(L_A=0\) and \(L_B=0\), with \(L_A,L_B\) affine, produces \(\alpha L_A+\beta L_B=0\) with \(\alpha,\beta\ne0\). Since \(\alpha^2=\beta^2=1\), its selector is \(1-(\alpha L_A+\beta L_B)^2=(1-L_A^2)+(1-L_B^2)-1-2\alpha\beta L_AL_B\). The product \(L_AL_B\) is not in general in the span of the premises' selectors. So a resolvent's span lies in the sum of its premises' spans, the constants and the one product \(L_AL_B\). It drops the resolved selectors, so in general it neither contains nor is contained in a premise's span. Only weakening steps, which add equations, give nested spans.

So the record's batched mechanisms apply exactly to nested or low-residual families, and dense window lines are neither.

What completeness leaves open

Observation CR refutes every block-count-independent PC lag over PHP, because the compiled refutation reuses lines. It does not refute a reuse-free statement. The NS test found that fresh blocks add nothing at the Nullstellensatz level in all 53 small cases, where PC gains. The binary form of that statement is the open level-one conjecture. CR's argument does not apply to an NS form as it stands: it uses the PC compilation, whose degree bound relies on reuse. Whether completeness refutes an NS form independent of the block count depends on the NS degree of compiled refutations, which grows with how deeply lines are reused. Nothing recorded bounds it. If such a statement held, it would batch window blocks for free, but only where they are used without PC reuse. Its possible use is therefore an endpoint in which the cost depends on how deeply window lines are reused, not on how many there are. That use is not formulated yet, and the conjecture is unproved even for one binary block.

Assessment of this line

Weak. Per-block removal is at its ceiling (Theorem NDX′). The recorded batch theorems need nesting, which window blocks lack, and derivation order does not supply it. Max-type weights and restrictions fail on window blocks (last review, F3). The one statement these arguments do not reach is reuse-free gluing. It is a conjecture with small-case support, and it would reach only window lines that are not reused deeply. The user overrode the earlier pause, so window work continues. This review recommends that the next window cycle test that one open possibility, and that the scope-and-review write-up of the partial endpoints (Corollaries ND and NDp, Propositions MX″ and MXp, Theorems Y and NDX′, Lemma WE) be scheduled as the thread's productive alternative.

Next step on the highest-risk item

Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. Formulate the reuse-free gluing precisely and test it before any use. The statement is a mixed one: a PC-closed old base, with window blocks used in NS form. The cost to count is the unfolding of window-dependent reuse in the compiled refutation. First check it against completeness: some compiled refutation must lie outside its reach at every size. Then test it at the smallest nonvacuous size against the NS test's bases, stating the count first. If it fails, or its unfolding cost is linear in the number of window lines anyway, recommend the write-up.

Sheaf check

Nested spans are exactly a sheaf condition that glues for free: along a chain, each section restricts to the next, and one global charge covers the chain. Window blocks form an antichain, so there is nothing to glue along. The reuse-free statement is the only remaining gluing that the completeness argument does not reach. At the NS level, sections over different blocks do not interact through reuse.

Verification gate. No result is claimed. Re-read the nested-span and core–residual theorems, the target-annihilator batch theorem with its annihilator rigidity, Observation CR, the NS test and the level-one conjecture's registry record. The two remarks are elementary: the first is linear algebra, and the second expands a square. Searched the record for nested-span, core and target batching, and for antichains and chain covers of blocks; nothing states a batched mechanism for non-nested dense blocks. No computation was run.

Reuse-free gluing would reach only window lines near the conclusion, and it implies a linear depth bound

22 September 2026 · Negative analysis · Unfolding reuse costs about \(2p\) degrees per inference below a window line; the window line's last open possibility gives no size bound. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Route item: odd-prime-clause-transfer. The batching review left one gluing statement that the completeness argument does not reach: fresh blocks used without PC reuse add nothing, independently of their number. It asked to formulate that statement, check it against completeness, and find what it costs to use. The stated rule was to recommend the write-up if the cost of use turned out to be linear.

Formulation

Let \(\mathcal G\) be an old base and \(\mathcal W\) the axioms of fresh one-level blocks. Write \(\mathrm{NS}_d(\mathcal W)\) for combinations \(\sum_Ag_AA\) with \(A\in\mathcal W\) and \(\deg(g_AA)\le d\). The mixed statement (MNS) is: for every old \(t\), if \(t\in\mathcal C_d(\mathcal G)+\mathrm{NS}_d(\mathcal W)\), then \(t\in\mathcal C_{d+c}(\mathcal G)\), with \(c\) independent of the number of blocks. The base may be used with PC reuse; the blocks may not. The NS test supports its pure-NS case at small sizes. The open binary level-one conjecture is a PC statement for one fresh block over level-one bases. The batching review called it the binary form of this statement; more precisely, MNS asks less of each block, which may not be reused, but asks it for any number of blocks. The ternary PC form, Conjecture C3, is refuted.

How a compiled refutation unfolds

The selector compiler works inference by inference. For a resolution step with premises \(A\), \(B\) and conclusion \(T\), it derives \(P_T\) from the completed premise lines through \[ P_T=R_A+r_ft_fR_B+r_fr_gQ,\qquad R_A=P_AP_T+\sum_jr_{A,j}t_jP_T, \] and similarly for \(R_B\). So \(P_A\) enters multiplied by \(P_T\), of degree at most \(p\), and \(P_B\) multiplied by \(r_ft_fP_T\), of degree at most \(2p\). Weakening multiplies the premise by \(P_T\) in the same way. The PC refutation avoids accumulation because it multiplies the completed premise lines, not their derivations. Rewriting it with no reuse of block-dependent lines substitutes each premise's expression into its uses. Along a path of \(\ell\) inferences the multipliers then multiply, so the resulting degree is at most about \(2p\ell\) plus the compiler's ceiling \(4p-1\). This is the standard PC-to-NS conversion, which costs degree times depth; nothing better is recorded.

Check against completeness

Apply MNS with \(\mathcal G=F_N\) and all blocks of a compiled refutation of depth \(h\). The unfolded refutation puts \(1\) in \(\mathcal C_{4p-1}(F_N)+\mathrm{NS}_{O(ph)}(\mathcal W)\). MNS would give \(1\in\mathcal C_{O(ph)+c}(F_N)\). The matching barrier puts \(d_N\) above \((N+1)/2\). So MNS implies that every \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) refutation of PHP, of any size, has depth \(\Omega(N/p)\). Completeness refutes MNS if some refutation is shallower than that; otherwise this argument does not decide it. A linear depth bound is plausible. Closure arguments, recorded for linear systems over \(\mathbb F_2\) on the bit encoding, keep systems of rank below \(cN\) consistent with a partial matching. A form over \(\mathbb F_p\) for unary PHP is not recorded. So MNS is at least as strong as an unrecorded depth lower bound, and its consistency with completeness is open, not settled.

What it would give

Suppose MNS held. After the common weight, the narrow blocks are mapped and may be reused. Every line that depends on a window block has to be unfolded, and each inference between a window line and the empty clause adds about \(2p\) degrees. After the map these degrees are multiplied by \(T_n\approx\sqrt n\) against a budget of about \(\lambda n\). So MNS would batch only window lines within about \(\lambda n/(2pT_n)=\sqrt n/\operatorname{polylog}n\) inferences of the conclusion, together with the \(Cn\) lines of Theorem NDX′ anywhere. A polynomial-size refutation can place its window lines deep in the derivation, and then the unfolding cost is linear in its depth. So the endpoint would be a new special class, of shallow window lines, and not the unrestricted statement. A small computation cannot change this, because the limit is in the unfolding, not in MNS. No computation was run.

Assessment

The last open possibility on the window line does not lead to the goal. It is a conjecture at least as strong as an unrecorded depth lower bound, and even if proved it would reach only window lines near the conclusion. By the rule the review set, the unfolding cost is linear, so this entry recommends the scope-and-review write-up. The window line's prospects remain weak. Every recorded route to it is now closed or conditional:

  • weights and restrictions, heuristically;
  • per-block removal, at its linear ceiling;
  • nesting-based batching, which window blocks lack;
  • reuse-free gluing, which is limited by depth.

Sheaf check

At the Nullstellensatz level, sections over different blocks do not interact, which is why the test found no loss. The sections still have to be glued along the derivation. Each inference contributes a multiplier, and the gluing cost is the length of the path, not the number of pieces. The window problem needs gluing along arbitrary DAGs at a cost independent of their depth, and no recorded object does that.

Next step

Next step (scope-and-review): write up the partial endpoints as one statement set:

  • Corollaries ND and NDp;
  • Propositions MX″ and MXp;
  • Theorems Y and NDX′, with Lemma WE;
  • the linear ceiling of per-block removal.

Check each against the ordering and mixed-interface controls, as the route item requires, and list exactly what remains open: refutations with superlinearly many lines of nonlocal dimension above \(n^{1/(p-1)-\varepsilon}\). Restart the window line on any of three events:

  • a batched mechanism for non-nested dense blocks;
  • a proof of the level-one conjecture together with a depth-independent way to use it;
  • outside work on DAG-like proofs with dense linear lines.

Verification gate. No result is claimed. The implication from MNS to a depth bound uses only the compiler's local form and the barrier. The unfolding bound is the standard conversion and is stated as an upper bound for this compiler, not as a lower bound for every conversion. Searched the record for depth lower bounds of \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin})\) refutations of PHP and for reuse-free or NS-level gluing. None states a depth lower bound for \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) refutations of unary PHP. The literature context records closure and size bounds for bounded-depth \(\mathrm{Res}(\oplus)\) on the bit encoding. No computation was run.

Statement set: what is proved about \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) refutations of unary PHP, checked against the controls

22 September 2026 · Consolidation · Every recorded endpoint in one list, checked against the ordering and mixed-interface controls, with the exact open case. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5, high effort).

Question. Route item: scope-and-review. The reuse-free gluing analysis closed or made conditional the last recorded route to the window and recommended a write-up of the partial endpoints. The consolidation of the same day predates the mixed endpoints, the all-prime extensions and the exceptional-line theorems. This entry replaces its list. It states each endpoint once with its hypotheses, checks each against the two controls the route item names, and states exactly what remains open. No new result is claimed.

Conventions

The object is ordinary unary \(\mathrm{PHP}^{n+1}_n\) and, where stated, its functional variant. Refutations are standard syntactic \(\mathrm{Res}(\mathrm{lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) refutations, with size measured in lines, and with no restriction on width, depth or sharing unless stated. "Excluded" means that for every fixed \(c\), refutations with at most \(n^c\) lines do not exist for large \(n\). Forms are taken modulo the linear row equations. A form is local if it is supported in one row or one column. A line's nonlocal dimension is the dimension of the span of the linear parts of its nonlocal equations. Its cell support is the union of the supports of its forms. Every endpoint compiles the refutation by the complete-board transfer or its weak-base form, one block per line, and ends at a PHP-specific barrier, such as the matching filtration or the separation of a fixed robust graph.

Endpoints in which every line lies in one class

  • Local lines, \(p=3\): every form row- or column-local (local corollary). It is the case of nonlocal dimension zero of the next item, which holds for every odd \(p\).
  • Low nonlocal dimension, every odd \(p\): nonlocal dimension at most \(n^{1/(p-1)-\varepsilon}\) (Corollary NDp).
  • Probes plus row remainders, every fixed \(p\): each line has \(O(\log n)\) affine probes, and each form is a probe combination plus a remainder on \(n^\alpha\operatorname{polylog}n\) rows, \(\alpha<1\) (remainder exclusion). It contains the row-support class.
  • Column occupancy, every fixed \(p\), weak base: each form is a global affine column-occupancy statistic plus a perturbation inside one column (occupancy exclusion).
  • Subquadratic cell support, every fixed \(p\): cell support at most \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\operatorname{polylog}n\) (cell-support exclusion).

Endpoints that mix classes

  • Across lines, \(p=3\): each line lies in the row-support class with \(\alpha<1/5\), or has nonlocal dimension at most \(n^\eta\) with \(\eta<(1-\alpha)/8\) (Proposition MX). With probes and \(\alpha<1\), this is Proposition MX′.
  • Within lines: each line splits into a part with shared probes and row remainders and a part of nonlocal dimension at most \(n^\eta\). This is Proposition MX″ at \(p=3\), and Proposition MXp at every odd \(p\), with \(\eta<(1-\alpha)/(4(p-1))\).
  • The occupancy class does not join these mixtures by composition.

Endpoints that allow arbitrary lines

  • Theorem Y, every fixed \(p\): a polynomial-size refutation has more than \(\Theta(n^\beta)\) lines of cell support above \(n^{2-\varepsilon}(\log n)^A\), for \(\beta<\varepsilon/2\).
  • Theorem NDX′, every odd \(p\): a polynomial-size refutation has more than \(Cn\) lines of nonlocal dimension above \(n^{1/(p-1)-\varepsilon}\), with \(C\) depending only on \(p\). It supersedes Theorem NDX.
  • Both rest on removing blocks one at a time: the old-consequence transfer for Theorem Y, and Lemma WE for NDX′.

Limits of the methods

  • Observation CR: completeness of resolution refutes every bound on what compiled blocks add over PHP that does not depend on their number.
  • Per-block removal cannot pass a linear number of window lines (ceiling review); Theorem NDX′ reaches this ceiling up to constants.
  • The recorded batch theorems need spans nested modulo annihilators, which window blocks lack (batching review).
  • Reuse-free gluing would reach only window lines near the conclusion (analysis).
  • Common weights and restrictions are expected to fail on window blocks, heuristically (window review).

Check against the two controls

Ordering control. The balanced minimum source on the graph-ordering principle has one complete block for every node \(S\) of a balanced partition tree and every \(i\in S\): about \(n\log_2n\) blocks with affine inputs. Its source degree is \(O(h\log n)\), while the old PC degree of the expander ordering family is \(\Omega(n)\). So over a general base no elimination can be charged independently of the number of blocks. Every endpoint above ends at a PHP-specific barrier, not at a generic transfer, so the control does not apply to them. The two generic statements are consistent with it. Lemma WE with target one charges \((p-1)\sum_b\delta_b\), about \((p-1)n\log_2n\) on this source. So it bounds the old degree by the source degree plus that charge, which is above the \(\Omega(n)\) lower bound. Observation CR concerns PHP only. The control does add one fact to the limits above. A batched mechanism for window blocks cannot be generic: it must use PHP structure.

Mixed-interface control. The canonical-OR certificates give a binary helper block that gains one degree over a retained second-level base. That is within the per-block charge \((p-1)\delta=1\) of BC and Lemma WE at \(p=2\). The endpoints above remove only one-level compiled blocks, whose inputs are old, so the second-level base of the control does not arise in them. None of the listed statements asserts conservativity, so none is contradicted.

Relations

The line classes are pairwise incomparable, by the separating examples of the consolidation. Theorems Y and NDX′ are incomparable too. The forms \(x_{1,j}+x_{2,j+1}\), \(j<n\), have cell support \(2n-2\) and nonlocal dimension \(n-1\). Row-local forms \(\sum_ja_{i,j}x_{i,j}\) with all \(a_{i,j}\ne0\), one for each row \(i\), have nonlocal dimension zero and cell support \(n(n+1)\).

What remains open

  • The window. To escape every endpoint above, a polynomial-size refutation must have more than \(Cn\) lines of nonlocal dimension above \(n^{1/(p-1)-\varepsilon}\) (Theorem NDX′) and more than \(\Theta(n^\beta)\) lines of cell support above \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\operatorname{polylog}n\) (Theorem Y). It must also have lines outside the mixed and occupancy classes. No statement excludes such refutations. At \(p=3\) their typical dense lines have projected rank of order \(n\) spread over many rows. Nested chains and shallow placement of these lines would help only through arguments that are not proved (batching review, reuse-free analysis).
  • The occupancy class in mixtures.
  • Dense-rank criteria for \(p\ge5\). The graph-level dense side exists only at \(p=3\), and it has no proof-system form at any prime.
  • Verification. No endpoint is Lean-verified or independently checked for novelty. The endpoints depend on the working complete-board transfer and on the fixed-graph and quotient-rank chain, which have fresh-context reviews only.

Assessment

The thread has a coherent set of partial results. They exclude short refutations whose dense lines are few, local, low-dimensional, sparsely supported, probe-structured or mixtures of these. Up to constants they also give the exact number of dense lines that per-block methods tolerate. They do not give the goal, and every recorded route to the rest is closed or conditional. As a statement set it is ready for review. A publication would need an independent check of the complete-board transfer and the fixed-graph chain first.

Sheaf check

The statement set is the list of local sections the thread has: each endpoint is an exclusion on one class of lines, and the mixed propositions are the gluings that worked. The window is the region no local section covers. It is also where the recorded gluings fail: per piece at linear cost, by nesting, or by reuse-free assembly.

Next step

Next step (odd-prime-clause-transfer, thread level): a thread route review. It should ask whether any route item remains live. The window's routes are closed or conditional; same-graph composition is a bookkeeping item; this entry completes the scope-and-review write-up. If no item is live, the thread should wait for a user decision rather than produce further special cases. The options are an independent check of the complete-board transfer with the fixed-graph chain, toward publication; a Lean assignment; or a new window idea from outside the recorded mechanisms.

Verification gate. No result is claimed. Every endpoint was restated from its registered summary and anchor, with its prime range and parameters, and every anchor was checked to exist. The two controls were re-read in full, and the ordering source's block count, about \(n\log_2n\), was computed from its construction. The two incomparability examples for Theorems Y and NDX′ were checked against the definitions: support and nonlocal dimension. No computation or reviewer was needed.
